children.title: Variable Objects
children.top_down_role: Symbolic decision objects, their identifiers, value spaces, plus roles within model expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract decision-variable leaf in a disciplined convex modeling expression graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A variable object is a symbolic leaf \(v=(\iota,s,D,A)\), where \(\iota\) is a unique identifier, \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) is a finite shape, \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_k}\) is its declared value domain, and \(A\) is consistent structural metadata. A valuation assigns \(v\) some \(x_v\in D\). Unlike a constant or assigned parameter, \(x_v\) is selected when the represented optimization problem is solved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A variable is an identified symbolic leaf whose shape, domain, and structural metadata constrain the value chosen by optimization.
assumptions_latex: \(k\geq 0\) and \(n_i\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
\(D\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\) denotes a decision value \(x_v\in D\) selected during optimization.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: abstract symbolic-variable semantics are standard in algebraic modeling systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Variable Objects leaf and is internally coherent, but the tuple representation, domain semantics, and solve-time interpretation have no cited authoritative source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Scalar Variable Attributes
children.top_down_role: Declared scalar sign, integrality, Boolean status, plus related structural classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Variable Attributes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain-refining attributes for real scalar decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real scalar variable \(v\), an attribute is a declared predicate restricting its admissible value \(x_v\). Standard attributes correspond to domains such as unrestricted \(\mathbb{R}\), nonnegative \(\mathbb{R}_+\), nonpositive \(\mathbb{R}_-\), integer \(\mathbb{Z}\), or Boolean \(\{0,1\}\). Multiple attributes are consistent precisely when the intersection of their associated domains is nonempty; the effective domain is that intersection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scalar attributes restrict a decision value by sign or integrality predicates, and combined attributes mean intersection of their domains.
assumptions_latex: \(x_v\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_v=\bigcap_{a\in A_v}D_a\neq\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: sign and integrality domains are standard variable metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the scalar-attribute leaf, but supported attributes, simultaneous-attribute rules, and the claim that consistency is exactly nonempty domain intersection depend on the modeling system and are uncited.

children.title: Vector Variable Attributes
children.top_down_role: Dimension, sign patterns, sparsity structure, plus vector-specific declarations.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Variable Attributes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shape and component-domain attributes for real vector decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real vector variable has shape \((n,)\) and value \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Its attributes may impose componentwise predicates, including \(x\geq0\), \(x\leq0\), \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), or \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\), where vector inequalities are componentwise. More generally, a declared vector-domain attribute identifies a nonempty set \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\); every valuation of the variable must belong to the intersection of all declared domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vector attributes fix dimension and impose componentwise or set-valued restrictions on every admissible vector value.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
\(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in D_v:=\bigcap_{a\in A_v}D_a\neq\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: vector shape and componentwise domains are standard modeling metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition has the correct local role, but the supported vector attributes and intersection semantics are modeling-system-specific and lack an authoritative citation with a locator.

children.title: Matrix Variable Attributes
children.top_down_role: Symmetry, triangularity, definiteness, sparsity, plus matrix value-space declarations.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Variable Attributes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and cone-domain attributes for real matrix decision variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A real matrix variable has shape \((m,n)\) and value \(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Attributes may require symmetry \(X=X^{\mathsf T}\), diagonality, entrywise sign restrictions, or integrality. When \(m=n\), cone attributes may require positive semidefiniteness \(X\succeq0\) or negative semidefiniteness \(X\preceq0\). The effective matrix domain is the intersection of the declared structural sets and must be nonempty; symmetry is implicit in either semidefinite cone condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix attributes constrain shape, entries, structure, or semidefinite cone membership; their effective domain is the nonempty intersection.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
\(X\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\in D_X:=\bigcap_{a\in A_X}D_a\neq\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: matrix structure and semidefinite domains are standard convex-modeling metadata

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the matrix-attribute leaf, but the supported structures, attribute-combination rules, and convention that semidefinite membership implicitly enforces symmetry require a framework or precise mathematical source.

children.title: Constant Data Semantics
children.top_down_role: Fixed data and the semantic classifications inferred from them.

children.title: Scalar Constants
children.top_down_role: Fixed scalar values used as leaves or coefficients in symbolic expressions.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed scalar leaves in symbolic optimization expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar constant is a symbolic expression leaf carrying a fixed value \(c\in\mathbb{F}\), where \(\mathbb{F}\) is the modeling system's supported real or complex scalar field. Its shape is scalar, its value is independent of all decision variables, and repeated evaluation returns \(c\). Sign, integrality, and related metadata are properties inferred from \(c\), not optimization constraints imposed on an unknown value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar constant is a fixed scalar-valued leaf whose metadata follows from its stored value and which introduces no decision freedom.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is representable as valid numerical data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{value}(c)=c\) independently of every decision-variable valuation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed scalar leaves are standard symbolic-expression objects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and fixed-leaf interpretation fit Scalar Constants, but the supported scalar field, evaluation behavior, and metadata inference semantics are framework-specific and uncited.

children.title: Array Constants
children.top_down_role: Fixed vector, matrix, tensor, sparse, or structured numerical inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Array Constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed shaped numerical data embedded in symbolic expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An array constant is a symbolic leaf carrying a fixed tensor \(C\in\mathbb{F}^{n_1\times\cdots\times n_k}\) with immutable mathematical shape \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\). Evaluation returns \(C\) independently of decision variables. Its sign, symmetry, diagonality, sparsity, and integrality metadata, when defined for its rank and field, must be sound consequences of the entries and structure of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An array constant is fixed shaped data; evaluation returns the same tensor, and all asserted metadata must follow from its entries.
assumptions_latex: \(k\geq1\) and \(n_i\in\mathbb{N}_{>0}\).
Every entry of \(C\) is valid numerical data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{value}(C)=C\) for every decision-variable valuation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed arrays are standard symbolic-expression leaves

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Array Constants, but supported ranks and fields, immutable-shape semantics, sparsity metadata, and the precise inference guarantees have no cited source.

children.title: Constant Metadata Inference
children.top_down_role: Shape, sign, value-space, symmetry, plus definiteness classifications inferred from fixed data.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Metadata Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sound derivation of structural metadata from fixed numerical data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input valid constant data \(C\). First record its rank, shape, and scalar field. Then evaluate each supported attribute predicate \(P_a(C)\), such as entrywise nonnegativity, integrality, symmetry, or positive semidefiniteness when dimensionally applicable. Output \(A(C)=\{a:P_a(C)\text{ is certified true}\}\); unsupported, inapplicable, or numerically undecidable predicates remain unknown rather than true. The inference is sound when every reported attribute satisfies \(a\in A(C)\Rightarrow C\in D_a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infer shape and every certifiably true supported property of constant data; uncertain or inapplicable properties remain unknown.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) has valid supported numerical entries.
Each supported attribute \(a\) has a specified predicate \(P_a\) and domain \(D_a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\in A(C)\Longrightarrow P_a(C)\Longrightarrow C\in D_a\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: metadata inference by sound predicate evaluation is a standard symbolic-modeling pattern

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate role for this leaf, but the supported predicates, certification criteria, numerical tolerances, and treatment of undecidable tests are unspecified and unsupported by a citation.

children.title: Numerical Data Validity
children.top_down_role: Nonfinite values, incompatible data types, malformed sparsity, plus unsupported numerical representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Data Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for numerical data entering a finite-valued model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Numerical data \(C\) are valid for a finite-valued symbolic model exactly when their rank, shape, scalar type, and storage representation are supported, every required entry is defined, and every entry is finite. For real data this requires \(C_i\in\mathbb{R}\) with \(|C_i|<\infty\); for complex data it requires finite real and imaginary parts. Values representing missing data, not-a-number, or signed infinity are invalid unless the modeling language explicitly defines an extended-value context for them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical input is valid when its structure and type are supported and all required scalar entries are defined and finite.
assumptions_latex: The model expects ordinary finite-valued numerical data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\text{ is valid}\Longleftrightarrow C\text{ has supported structure and all required entries are finite}\).

notation.meaning: an entry of the supplied numerical datum

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finiteness and supported-shape checks are standard numerical-input conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the appropriate role, but the exact biconditional depends on supported types, sparse-storage rules, missing-entry semantics, and extended values. These framework-dependent details need an authoritative source before the formula is reliable.

children.title: Parameter Object Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Data-bearing symbolic objects retained across related problem instances.

children.title: Parameter Objects
children.top_down_role: Symbolic data placeholders retained across related model instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic leaves fixed within a solve but assignable between solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A parameter object is a symbolic leaf \(p=(\iota,s,D,A,
u)\) with identifier \(\iota\), fixed shape \(s\), declared admissible domain \(D\), structural metadata \(A\), and optionally assigned value \(
u\in D\). Within one instantiated optimization problem, \(
u\) is fixed and introduces no decision freedom. Reassigning a valid value between solves changes numerical problem data while preserving the parameter's symbolic identity and declared structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter is symbolic problem data with fixed structure, held constant during a solve but validly reassignable between solves.
assumptions_latex: \(D\neq\varnothing\).
Any assigned value satisfies \(\nu\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\) evaluates to fixed data \(\nu\) during each solve.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: mutable symbolic parameters are standard in optimization modeling systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits Parameter Objects, but optional assignment, solve-time constancy, reassignment timing, and preservation of symbolic identity are lifecycle semantics requiring an authoritative framework citation.

children.title: Parameter Structural Attributes
children.top_down_role: Shape, sign, symmetry, definiteness, plus value-space declarations attached to parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Structural Attributes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant shape and domain metadata attached to a parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The structural attributes of a parameter \(p\) are its declared shape \(s\), scalar field, and predicates defining an admissible domain \(D_p\). Examples include entrywise sign, integrality, symmetry, and semidefinite cone membership when applicable. These attributes are invariants of the symbolic object: every assigned value \(\nu\) must have shape \(s\) and satisfy \(\nu\in D_p\). Attributes may therefore support symbolic curvature or sign analysis before a numerical value is assigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Parameter attributes are invariant declarations of shape, field, and admissible domain that every assigned value must satisfy.
assumptions_latex: \(D_p\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\(\operatorname{shape}(
u)=s\) and \(
u\in D_p\) for every valid assignment \(
u\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariant parameter domains enable static symbolic analysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the structural-attributes leaf, but the supported attributes and their use in pre-assignment sign or curvature analysis are framework-specific and uncited.

children.title: Parameter Value Mutation
children.top_down_role: Replacement of numerical parameter values without reconstruction of the source model.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Value Mutation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantics of replacing assigned parameter data between solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a parameter \(p=(\iota,s,D,A,\nu)\) and candidate value \(w\). Check that \(w\) is valid numerical data, has shape \(s\), and belongs to \(D\). If every check succeeds, replace only the stored value, producing \(p'=(\iota,s,D,A,w)\); otherwise reject the mutation and retain \(p\). Subsequent expression evaluation uses \(w\), while the identifier, expression-graph position, shape, and declared attributes remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To mutate a parameter, validate the new value and replace only stored data; otherwise preserve the prior parameter unchanged.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) has fixed identifier, shape, domain, and attributes.
\(w\) is supplied between problem evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in D\Longrightarrow \operatorname{value}(p')=w\), with \((\iota,s,D,A)\) unchanged.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validated value replacement captures standard parameter mutation semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is suitable for this leaf, but atomic failure behavior, mutation timing, identity preservation, and cache implications need a framework source. The conclusion also states only membership in the domain, while the algorithm additionally requires numerical-data and shape validity.

children.title: Parameter Assignment Validity
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of assigned values with declared dimensions, signs, structures, plus data types.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter Assignment Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient checks for assigning numerical data to a parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let parameter \(p\) have declared shape \(s\), scalar field \(\mathbb{F}\), and admissible domain \(D_p\). A candidate numerical value \(w\) is a valid assignment exactly when \(w\) is valid numerical data, \(\operatorname{shape}(w)=s\), every entry belongs to \(\mathbb{F}\) or an explicitly permitted lossless coercion into it, and \(w\in D_p\). Failure of any conjunct makes the assignment invalid and leaves the parameter unassigned or unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parameter assignment is valid exactly when its data, shape, scalar field, and every declared domain restriction are compatible.
assumptions_latex: \(D_p\neq\varnothing\).
The parameter's structural declarations are internally consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Valid}(p,w)\Longleftrightarrow \operatorname{DataValid}(w)\land\operatorname{shape}(w)=s\land w\in\mathbb{F}^{s}\land w\in D_p\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: shape, type, and domain compatibility are standard assignment-validity conditions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role, but lossless coercion rules and the asserted unchanged-or-unassigned failure behavior are framework-specific. An authoritative source with a precise locator is required to validate the biconditional.

children.title: Model Statement Object Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Top-level model objects subsequently checked for disciplined admissibility.

children.title: Objective Objects
children.top_down_role: Minimization, maximization, plus feasibility-oriented top-level objective representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic minimization and maximization objectives with scalar-valued expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\) denote the model variables and let \(f(x)\in\mathbb{R}\) be a scalar symbolic expression. An objective object is either \(\operatorname{Minimize}(f)\) or \(\operatorname{Maximize}(f)\), specifying respectively the order relation used to compare feasible points. Under disciplined convex programming, \(\operatorname{Minimize}(f)\) is admissible when \(f\) is convex, and \(\operatorname{Maximize}(f)\) is admissible when \(f\) is concave. Constant and affine expressions satisfy both admissibility rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An objective wraps a scalar expression and declares minimization or maximization; disciplined convexity requires a convex minimand or concave maximand.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal{D}\to\mathbb{R}\) is scalar-valued on its declared domain \(\mathcal{D}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Minimize}(f)\) or \(\operatorname{Maximize}(f)\) is a well-formed objective object under the corresponding curvature rule.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the Objective Objects container, and the DCP curvature rules are stated precisely. However, the record supplies no source reference or inspectable locator for the modeling-system object semantics and admissibility rules.

children.title: Constraint Objects
children.top_down_role: Scalar equality, scalar inequality, plus structured constraint representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic equality and inequality constraints accepted by disciplined convex programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For scalar expressions \(f\) and \(g\) with a common domain, a constraint object represents one predicate: \(f\leq g\), \(f\geq g\), or \(f=g\). Under disciplined convex programming, \(f\leq g\) is admissible when \(f\) is convex and \(g\) is concave; \(f\geq g\) is admissible under the reversed curvature assignment; and \(f=g\) is admissible when both expressions are affine. Array inequalities are interpreted componentwise when their shapes are compatible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint stores an equality or inequality predicate and is DCP-valid when its operands have compatible shapes and the required curvature.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) have compatible scalar or array shapes.
Both expressions are defined on a common declared domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate defines a well-formed constraint object exactly when its shape and curvature rules hold.

notation.meaning: Symbolic expressions forming the two sides of a constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Constraint Objects container and gives the standard scalar DCP curvature rules plus shape compatibility. No cited source or locator supports the object taxonomy, componentwise array interpretation, or exact modeling-system conventions.

children.title: Set-Membership Objects
children.top_down_role: Top-level declarations placing expressions within supported convex sets or cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Membership Objects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Symbolic membership constraints for convex sets with compatible ambient spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e(x)\) be a symbolic expression valued in a finite-dimensional real vector space \(V\), and let \(C\subseteq V\) be a declared set. A set-membership object \(e(x)\in C\) denotes the constraint that the evaluated expression belongs to \(C\). In a disciplined convex model, this object is convex when \(C\) is convex and the modeling system recognizes the expression-to-set combination as a valid convex constraint, including any required affine mapping or cone-specific rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set-membership object requires an expression to lie in a declared compatible set; convex modeling additionally requires a recognized convex membership rule.
assumptions_latex: \(e:\mathcal{D}\to V\) and \(C\subseteq V\).
The dimensions and structural attributes of \(e(x)\) and \(C\) are compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e(x)\in C\) is a well-formed symbolic membership constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Set-Membership Objects container, but the phrase recognizing an expression-to-set combination delegates the substantive admissibility condition to an unspecified modeling system. A source with a specific locator is required to determine the intended affine, conic, or other membership rule.

children.title: Top-Level Object Assembly
children.top_down_role: Organization of objectives, constraints, memberships, plus model-level metadata into a problem object.

knowledge_statements.title: Top-Level Object Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assembly of an objective and finite constraint collection into a symbolic optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given model variables \(x\), an objective object \(O(f(x))\), and a finite ordered collection of constraint objects \((c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x))\), the top-level problem object represents \[\operatorname{Problem}\!\left(O(f(x)),[c_1(x),\ldots,c_m(x)]\right).\] Its feasible set is \(F=\{x:c_i(x)\text{ holds for every }i\}\), and its mathematical meaning is to optimize \(f\) over \(F\) in the direction declared by \(O\). Parameters are data placeholders and variables are optimization unknowns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A top-level problem combines one objective with finitely many constraints, whose conjunction defines the feasible set over which the objective is optimized.
assumptions_latex: Each constituent object is well formed and refers to a compatible modeling context.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assembled object represents optimization of \(f\) over \(F\) with the direction specified by \(O\).

notation.meaning: Objective constructor declaring minimization or maximization.
Feasible set defined by all constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the correct role for Top-Level Object Assembly, and the objective-plus-finite-constraints semantics are coherent. The record has no citation or inspectable locator supporting this symbolic Problem object interface and its parameter-variable distinction.

children.title: Expression-Graph Representations
children.top_down_role: Recursive and shared representations of compound symbolic expressions.

children.title: Expression Trees
children.top_down_role: Tree-structured syntax for recursive semantic analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Expression Trees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rooted syntax-tree representation of recursively constructed symbolic expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symbolic expression tree is a finite rooted ordered tree \(T=(N,E,r)\). Every leaf is labeled by a variable, parameter, or constant; every internal node \(v\) is labeled by an atom \(a_v\) whose arity equals the number of ordered children of \(v\). Its semantics are recursive: a leaf evaluates to its labeled object, while an internal node evaluates as \(\operatorname{val}(v)=a_v(\operatorname{val}(v_1),\ldots,\operatorname{val}(v_k))\). The expression represented by \(T\) is \(\operatorname{val}(r)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expression tree has labeled leaves and atom-labeled internal nodes; recursively evaluating children and then each atom yields the root expression.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite, rooted, and ordered.
Every atom is applied to the number and types of arguments in its signature.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}(r)\) is the symbolic expression represented by \(T\).

notation.meaning: Recursive semantic value at node v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is appropriate for Expression Trees, and the recursive syntax and semantics are internally consistent. No source reference or locator is supplied for this expression-representation convention.

children.title: Shared-Expression DAG Representation
children.top_down_role: Shared-expression structures used for memoized analysis and transformation.

children.title: Expression DAG Structure
children.top_down_role: Node identity, directed dependencies, root expressions, plus shared graph topology.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Successor order and atom signatures are compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A reverse topological evaluation assigns a unique semantic value to every node of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed acyclic syntax graph allowing multiple parents for shared expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expression DAG is a finite directed acyclic graph \(G=(N,E)\) with edges directed from each operation node to its ordered arguments. Every leaf is labeled by a variable, parameter, or constant, and every nonleaf \(v\) is labeled by an atom \(a_v\) with ordered successors \((v_1,\ldots,v_k)\). Its semantics are \(\operatorname{val}(v)=a_v(\operatorname{val}(v_1),\ldots,\operatorname{val}(v_k))\). A node may have multiple predecessors, so one computed subexpression may feed several parent operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expression DAG recursively represents expressions like a tree but permits a node to supply the same subexpression to multiple parents.
knowledge_statements.title: Expression DAG Structure

children.title: Common-Subexpression Sharing
children.top_down_role: Single graph nodes referenced from multiple expression contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subexpression Sharing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DAG compression obtained by identifying repeated symbolic subexpressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T\) be an expression tree and let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation on its nodes such that \(u\sim v\) only when their rooted subtrees have the same operator labels, leaf identities, and ordered argument structure. The quotient representation identifies every equivalence class \([v]\) with one DAG node and retains edges induced by child relations. The resulting DAG has the same root semantics as \(T\), while each repeated subexpression represented by one equivalence class is stored and analyzed once.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Common-subexpression sharing merges structurally identical rooted subexpressions into one DAG node without changing the represented root expression.
assumptions_latex: \(\sim\) respects leaf identity, atom labels, argument order, and arity.
Node labels are immutable during quotient construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{val}_{T}(r)=\operatorname{val}_{T/\sim}([r])\).

notation.meaning: Quotient DAG formed by merging equivalent subtrees.
Equivalence class represented by a shared DAG node.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is suitable for Common-Subexpression Sharing, and the structural equivalence conditions support the stated semantic preservation. No source reference or locator supports the quotient-DAG construction or its asserted storage and analysis behavior.

children.title: Shared-Node Metadata Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of semantic classifications across repeated references to the same expression node.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Node Metadata Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of sound semantic annotations at every reference to one immutable DAG node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be an immutable node in an expression DAG, and let \(M(v)\) be metadata determined solely by the node label, its ordered successors, their metadata, and fixed modeling context. Examples include shape, sign, curvature, and domain annotations. Because every incoming edge references the same node and recursive inputs, computing \(M(v)\) once yields the same result for every occurrence of \(v\). Thus cached metadata may be reused at all parents without changing recursive semantic analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metadata determined only by an immutable node and its children can be computed once and reused by every parent referencing that node.
assumptions_latex: The expression DAG and modeling context remain immutable during analysis.
\(M(v)\) is a deterministic function of local node data and successor metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every reference to \(v\) may use one cached value \(M(v)\).

notation.meaning: Deterministically derived semantic metadata for v.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Property is an appropriate content kind for metadata reuse. The claim is conditional and coherent under immutability and deterministic local analysis, but the included metadata classes and caching contract are modeling-system-specific and have no cited source or locator.

children.title: Graph Identity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among structurally equal expressions, object identity, copied nodes, plus mutated inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Graph Identity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion determining when two expression occurrences may share one DAG node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two expression occurrences \(u\) and \(v\) may be assigned the same DAG-node identity only if they denote the same immutable symbolic object: their atom or leaf labels agree, their ordered child identities agree recursively, and all semantic attributes that affect evaluation or analysis agree. If variable identity, parameter identity, value-space structure, shape, domain, or other semantic context differs, then \(u\) and \(v\) must remain distinct nodes even when their printed forms coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Occurrences may share node identity only when all evaluation-relevant structure and identities agree; identical printing alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Node identity is intended to preserve both evaluation and semantic-analysis results.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u\equiv_G v\) is permitted only when \(\operatorname{key}(u)=\operatorname{key}(v)\) for a complete semantic identity key.

notation.meaning: Occurrences u and v share one graph node.
Complete immutable semantic identity key of occurrence u.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for Graph Identity Boundaries. The criterion is plausible, but a complete semantic identity key is intentionally system-dependent and is not defined by any cited implementation or formal modeling-system source.

children.title: Expression Shape Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Expression classes distinguished by output shape and algebraic action.

children.title: Scalar Expression Shapes
children.top_down_role: Zero-dimensional or singleton-valued symbolic outputs used in scalar model contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Scalar Expression Shapes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-axis expression shape representing one real or complex scalar value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A scalar expression is a symbolic expression whose value space is \(\mathbb{F}\), where \(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\), and whose shape is the empty tuple \(()\). It has no indexed axes and contains one scalar entry. This shape is distinct from the one-dimensional vector shape \((1)\) and the two-dimensional matrix shape \((1,1)\), even when a modeling system provides explicit conversions among them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scalar expression has value space over one scalar and empty shape; it remains structurally distinct from length-one vectors and one-by-one matrices.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb{F}\) is the declared scalar field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{shape}(e)=()\) and \(e\in\mathbb{F}\).

notation.meaning: Empty shape tuple for a scalar.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Scalar Expression Shapes, but the empty-tuple scalar convention and asserted distinction from shapes \((1)\) and \((1,1)\) are representation-system conventions. No source or locator identifies the intended convention.

children.title: Vector Expression Shapes
children.top_down_role: One-dimensional symbolic outputs with orientation, length, plus indexing semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Vector Expression Shapes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-axis expression shape representing an ordered finite vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(n\geq 1\), a vector expression is a symbolic expression whose value space is \(\mathbb{F}^{n}\) and whose shape is the one-tuple \((n)\). Its entries are indexed by one axis as \(e_i\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The vector shape \((n)\) is distinct from the matrix shapes \((n,1)\) and \((1,n)\); conversions to column or row matrices require an explicit reshape or a declared promotion rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vector expression has one axis of length n and is structurally distinct from row and column matrices unless an explicit conversion applies.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(n\geq 1\).
\(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{shape}(e)=(n)\) and \(e\in\mathbb{F}^{n}\).

notation.meaning: One-axis vector shape of length n.
The ith scalar entry of vector expression e.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits Vector Expression Shapes and is internally consistent under a one-axis shape convention. The distinction between \((n)\), \((n,1)\), and \((1,n)\), including reshape or promotion behavior, requires a cited modeling-system source with a specific locator.

children.title: Matrix Expression Shapes
children.top_down_role: Two-dimensional symbolic outputs with row, column, plus structured-matrix semantics.

assumptions_latex: \(m,n\in\mathbb{N}\) with \(m,n\geq 1\).
\(\mathbb{F}\in\{\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{shape}(E)=(m,n)\) and \(E\in\mathbb{F}^{m\times n}\).

notation.meaning: Ordered matrix shape with m rows and n columns.
Entry in row i and column j.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-axis expression shape representing a finite rectangular array.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integers \(m,n\geq 1\), a matrix expression is a symbolic expression whose value space is \(\mathbb{F}^{m\times n}\) and whose shape is the ordered pair \((m,n)\). Its entries are indexed as \(E_{ij}\) with \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The order of the dimensions is significant: \((m,n)\) records row and column axes, so transposition changes the shape to \((n,m)\), although the two shapes coincide numerically when \(m=n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix expression has ordered row and column dimensions; transposition reverses them, even though square matrices retain the same numerical shape.
knowledge_statements.title: Matrix Expression Shapes

children.title: Shape Promotion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Broadcasting, scalar promotion, axis interpretation, plus dimension compatibility across expression classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Shape Promotion Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract promotion rules; concrete scalar, vector, and matrix conventions remain modeling-system dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal S\) be a set of array shapes and let \(V_s\) denote the value space of shape \(s\in\mathcal S\). A shape-promotion regime is a collection \(\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal S\times\mathcal S\) with maps \(P_{s,t}:V_s\to V_t\) for \((s,t)\in\mathcal P\). Each map must be value preserving under a declared indexing or replication convention, satisfy \(P_{s,s}=I_{V_s}\), and obey \(P_{t,u}\circ P_{s,t}=P_{s,u}\) whenever all three promotions are admitted. An expression may be promoted from \(s\) to \(t\) exactly when \((s,t)\in\mathcal P\); otherwise the composition is shape invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A promotion regime specifies coherent, value-preserving conversions between expression shapes and rejects every conversion not explicitly admitted.
assumptions_latex: \(V_s\) is defined for every declared shape \(s\).
Each admitted promotion has a fixed indexing or replication convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((s,t)\in\mathcal P\) is the complete predicate for valid promotion from \(s\) to \(t\).

notation.meaning: value space associated with shape s
promotion map from shape s to shape t

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the proposed coherence axioms and the meaning of value preservation under indexing or replication are modeling-system-specific and unsupported by an inspectable source. Source support is required before the mathematical formulation can be relied upon.

children.title: Expression Value-Space Taxonomy

children.title: Real Value Spaces
children.top_down_role: Real scalar, vector, plus matrix expression values with ordinary sign metadata.

knowledge_statements.title: Real Value Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional real scalar, vector, and array value spaces used by expression nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\), the real value space of shape \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) is \[\mathbb R^s:=\{x:\{1,\ldots,n_1\}\times\cdots\times\{1,\ldots,n_k\}\to\mathbb R\},\] equipped with pointwise addition and real scalar multiplication. Its dimension is \(\prod_{j=1}^k n_j\). The empty shape denotes the scalar space \(\mathbb R\); shapes \((n)\) and \((m,n)\) denote real vectors and real matrices, respectively. Thus a real-valued expression of shape \(s\) evaluates to exactly one element of \(\mathbb R^s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real expression of a fixed shape takes values in the finite-dimensional real vector space of real arrays having that shape.
assumptions_latex: \(k\geq 1\) and \(n_j\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), unless the scalar empty-shape convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb R^s\) is a real vector space of dimension \(\prod_{j=1}^k n_j\).

source_refs.locator: 4.2.1 Real Vector Spaces p. 270

source_witnesses.locator: 4.2.1 Real Vector Spaces p. 270

children.title: Complex Value Spaces
children.top_down_role: Complex-valued expressions, conjugation-sensitive structure, plus real-imaginary reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Complex Value Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional complex scalar, vector, and array value spaces used by expression nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For positive integers \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\), the complex value space of shape \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) is \[\mathbb C^s:=\{z:\{1,\ldots,n_1\}\times\cdots\times\{1,\ldots,n_k\}\to\mathbb C\}.\] It is a complex vector space under pointwise operations, with complex dimension \(\prod_{j=1}^k n_j\), and a real vector space of twice that dimension. The empty shape denotes \(\mathbb C\). Complex conjugation acts entrywise, and a complex expression of shape \(s\) evaluates to exactly one element of \(\mathbb C^s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A complex expression takes values in an array space over the complex numbers, with twice as many real as complex coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(k\geq 1\) and \(n_j\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), unless the scalar empty-shape convention is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C^s=\prod_{j=1}^k n_j\) and \(\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C^s=2\prod_{j=1}^k n_j\).

children.title: Symmetric Matrix Spaces
children.top_down_role: Real symmetric matrix values with structure-preserving expression semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Matrix Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real symmetric matrices as a structured real value space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), the symmetric matrix space is \[\mathbb S^n:=\{X\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:X^\mathsf T=X\}.\] Under matrix addition and real scalar multiplication, \(\mathbb S^n\) is a real vector subspace of \(\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) having dimension \(n(n+1)/2\). Its elements are determined by their diagonal and upper-triangular entries. The trace inner product is \(\langle X,Y\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\) for \(X,Y\in\mathbb S^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The symmetric matrix value space consists of real square matrices equal to their transposes and has n(n+1)/2 independent real coordinates.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb S^n\) is a real vector space with \(\dim\mathbb S^n=n(n+1)/2\).

notation.meaning: space of real symmetric n by n matrices

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Real symmetric matrices and the space \(\mathbb S^n\)
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines real symmetric matrices and their linear value space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric if \(A=A^\top\), equivalently if \(A_{ij}=A_{ji}\) for all \(1\le i,j\le n\). The set \(\mathbb S^n=\{A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}:A=A^\top\}\) is a linear subspace of \(\mathbb R^{n\times n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A real square matrix is symmetric when it equals its transpose, equivalently when A_ij=A_ji for every pair of indices. The symmetric n-by-n matrices form the linear subspace S^n.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\in\mathbb S^n\iff A=A^\top\iff (\forall i,j)\ A_{ij}=A_{ji},\qquad \mathbb S^n\text{ is a linear subspace of }\mathbb R^{n\times n}.

children.title: Hermitian Matrix Spaces
children.top_down_role: Complex Hermitian matrix values with spectral or cone-order classifications.

knowledge_statements.title: Hermitian Matrix Spaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complex Hermitian matrices regarded as a structured real value space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(n\in\mathbb N_{>0}\), the Hermitian matrix space is \[\mathbb H^n:=\{X\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}:X^*=X\},\] where \(X^*=\overline X^{\mathsf T}\). It is closed under addition and real scalar multiplication, but not generally under multiplication by nonreal scalars; hence it is naturally a real vector space. Its real dimension is \(n^2\): diagonal entries are real, while each strictly upper-triangular complex entry determines its conjugate lower-triangular entry. A real inner product is \(\langle X,Y\rangle=\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}(X^*Y)=\operatorname{tr}(XY)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hermitian matrices equal their conjugate transposes and form a real, not complex, vector space of dimension n squared.
assumptions_latex: \(n\in\mathbb N_{>0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb H^n\) is a real vector space with \(\dim_{\mathbb R}\mathbb H^n=n^2\).

notation.meaning: space of n by n Hermitian matrices

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mathematical definition and real-dimension statement are standard and the content kind fits, but no source is cited. The trace-inner-product equality and real-vector-space interpretation require an inspectable authoritative locator.

children.title: Structured-Space Reduction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where value-space conversions lose declared structure or require unsupported reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured-Space Reduction Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coordinate reductions must retain the defining equations of symmetric or Hermitian structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A coordinate reduction of a structured matrix space is exact only if its reconstruction map has precisely that space as its image. For symmetric matrices, upper-triangular coordinates must reconstruct \(X_{ji}=X_{ij}\). For Hermitian matrices, diagonal coordinates must be real and reconstruction must enforce \(X_{ji}=\overline{X_{ij}}\). Treating the retained entries as unconstrained coordinates in \(\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) or \(\mathbb C^{n\times n}\) enlarges the value space. Consequently, an atom or constraint whose meaning uses symmetry, conjugation, eigenvalues, or semidefinite order cannot cross such a reduction unless reconstruction preserves that structure exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Removing redundant matrix entries is exact only when reconstruction enforces symmetry or conjugate symmetry; otherwise structured atoms and cone constraints change meaning.
assumptions_latex: The reduced representation is intended to parameterize all and only the original structured matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\mathbb S^n\) or \(\operatorname{range}(R)=\mathbb H^n\) is necessary for an exact reduction with reconstruction map \(R\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification fits the leaf and the range condition captures exact parameterization, but the broader claim about which atoms and constraints may cross a reduction is unsupported and depends on modeling-system semantics.

children.title: Output Shape Metadata
children.top_down_role: Scalar, vector, matrix, tensor, plus structured output-shape classifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar, vector, matrix, tensor, and structured refinements of output-shape metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the empty-tuple scalar convention, an output shape \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) is classified as scalar, vector, matrix, or higher-order tensor according as \(k=0\), \(k=1\), \(k=2\), or \(k\ge3\). Structural annotations such as symmetric, diagonal, triangular, sparse-patterned, or Hermitian refine the value space but are not determined by the shape tuple. In particular, shape \((n,n)\) is necessary but not sufficient for symmetry or diagonality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank classifies scalar, vector, matrix, and tensor outputs, while symmetry and similar structure require annotations beyond shape.
assumptions_latex: Scalars use the empty shape tuple.
Structural annotations are maintained separately from axis lengths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{shape}(e)=(n,n)\not\Rightarrow e=e^{\mathsf T}.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape Classes and Structural Annotations
Output Shape Metadata
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static shape annotation attached to every expression-graph node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an expression node \(e\) evaluate in an array value space. Its output-shape metadata is an ordered tuple \(\operatorname{shape}(e)=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) of positive axis lengths such that every admissible evaluation of \(e\) lies in the value space of that shape. The tuple is determined from the operator and its operands before numerical evaluation. A scalar uses the declared scalar-shape convention. A composition \(f(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\) is shape valid only when the operands' shapes satisfy the operator's compatibility predicate, in which case its stored output shape equals the predicate's uniquely determined result.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Output-shape metadata records the fixed axis lengths of an expression and is inferred statically from the operator and operand shapes.
assumptions_latex: Each operator declares a shape-compatibility predicate and an output-shape rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{shape}(f(e_1,\ldots,e_r))\) exists exactly when the operator's shape predicate is satisfied.

notation.meaning: ordered tuple of output axis lengths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local topic are appropriate, but static shape inference, uniqueness of output shape, and the scalar-shape convention are system-specific claims with no cited source.

children.title: Dimension Metadata
children.top_down_role: Axis lengths, matrix dimensions, parameterized sizes, plus dimension provenance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compile-time symbolic axis lengths and records of how they arise from declarations and shape rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Before numerical evaluation, an axis length may be a positive-integer literal or a symbolic size variable fixed for construction of the expression graph. Dimension provenance records whether each length was declared by an input or derived by an operator rule, together with the equality constraints imposed by that derivation. Two symbolic axes are statically compatible only when their equality follows from the declared size constraints; coincidental equality in one instantiated graph does not establish a reusable symbolic identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symbolic dimension is fixed during graph construction and carries its declaration or derivation provenance; compatibility requires a certified symbolic equality.
assumptions_latex: Symbolic size variables range over positive integers.
All shape rules and size-equality constraints are fixed while constructing the expression graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_1\sim d_2\text{ is accepted only when the stored size constraints entail }d_1=d_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Static Symbolic Dimensions and Provenance

assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{shape}(e)=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\) is statically known.
\(n_j\in\mathbb N_{>0}\) for every axis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{size}(e)=\prod_{j=1}^{k}n_j\), and dimensional equality is equality of ordered shape tuples.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension data derived from a fixed expression shape.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an expression \(e\) with output shape \(s=(n_1,\ldots,n_k)\), its dimension metadata consists of its rank \(k\), axis lengths \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\), and total scalar size \[\operatorname{size}(e)=\prod_{j=1}^{k}n_j.\] Under the empty-product convention, a scalar has rank \(0\) and size \(1\). Dimension metadata is valid only when every \(n_j\) is a positive integer fixed at model-construction time. Two expressions have identical dimensions exactly when their ordered shape tuples agree, not merely when their total scalar sizes agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dimension metadata gives rank, ordered axis lengths, and total scalar size; equal total size alone does not imply equal dimensions.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Metadata

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The proposal ambiguously treats numerical model parameters as shape parameters and assumes a system-specific symbolic equality engine.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A parameterized dimension may be represented by an integer-valued symbolic expression \(d(\theta)\) together with provenance. Compatibility is statically certified only when equality or positivity holds for every admissible parameter value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symbolic dimension records an integer expression and provenance, with compatibility required over all parameter values.
assumptions_latex: Every admissible parameter value gives positive-integer axis lengths.
The system has a symbolic equality mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_1\equiv d_2\text{ is required; equality at one parameter instance is insufficient}.
knowledge_statements.title: Parameterized Dimensions and Provenance

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory covers rank, ordered axis lengths, scalar size, tuple equality, compile-time symbolic sizes, equality constraints, and provenance. The runtime-parameter formulation is deferred as system-specific and ambiguous. Output classes, broadcasting, and linear-algebra compatibility are excluded to their sibling leaves.

children.title: Broadcast Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Permitted scalar promotion, array broadcasting, plus axis alignment across operands.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-operand extension of the declared trailing-axis broadcast convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s^{(1)},\ldots,s^{(k)}\) be finitely many shapes, left-padded by ones to common rank \(r\). They are jointly broadcast compatible exactly when, on every axis \(j\), all nonunit lengths are equal. The output length is that common nonunit length when one exists and \(1\) otherwise. Under this condition, every ordering of successive compatible binary broadcasts yields the same output shape.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Several arrays broadcast jointly exactly when each aligned axis has at most one nonunit length; the result is order independent.
assumptions_latex: Trailing axes are aligned and absent leading axes are treated as length one.
The operation is elementwise and has finitely many operands.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: c_j=\max_{1\le \ell\le k}s^{(\ell)}_j\quad\text{when axis }j\text{ has at most one distinct nonunit length}.
knowledge_statements.title: Multioperand Broadcast Shape
Broadcast Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trailing-axis broadcasting convention for elementwise array operations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=(a_1,\ldots,a_p)\) and \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\) be operand shapes. Pad the shorter tuple on the left with ones so both have length \(r=\max(p,q)\), obtaining \(\tilde a,\tilde b\). The shapes are broadcast compatible exactly when, for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,r\}\), \[\tilde a_j=\tilde b_j\quad\text{or}\quad\tilde a_j=1\quad\text{or}\quad\tilde b_j=1.\] When compatible, the unique output shape is \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_r)\), where \(c_j=\max(\tilde a_j,\tilde b_j)\); otherwise the elementwise operation is shape invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two shapes broadcast when each aligned axis is equal or one has length one; the output takes the larger aligned lengths.
assumptions_latex: Broadcasting aligns axes from the trailing end.
All axis lengths are positive integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a\) and \(b\) are broadcast compatible if and only if the displayed coordinatewise predicate holds.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly states trailing-axis broadcasting under the declared convention and fits the leaf, but that convention is modeling-system-specific and no authoritative array-semantics source is supplied.

children.title: Linear-Algebra Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Inner dimensions, transpose-sensitive shapes, block layouts, plus structured matrix compatibility.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shape conditions for common structured matrix expressions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\) of shape \((m,n)\), the expressions \(A=A^{\mathsf T}\), \(A\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(A)\) under the ordinary square-matrix trace convention are dimensionally meaningful only when \(m=n\). For \(x\) of length \(n\), \(x^{\mathsf T}Ax\) requires \(A\) to have shape \((n,n)\). These predicates do not certify symmetry or positive semidefiniteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Symmetry, semidefinite order, square-matrix trace, and quadratic forms require matching square dimensions, but shape alone proves no matrix structure.
assumptions_latex: Ordinary finite-dimensional real matrix conventions are used.
Trace is declared only for square matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A=A^{\mathsf T},\ A\succeq0,\ \operatorname{tr}(A)\text{ require }m=n;\quad x^{\mathsf T}Ax\text{ requires }\operatorname{shape}(A)=(n,n).
knowledge_statements.title: Structure-Sensitive Matrix Compatibility

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rectangular block layouts with consistent block-row heights and block-column widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A block array \(M=(M_{ij})_{i=1,j=1}^{r,s}\) defines a matrix exactly when positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_r\) and \(n_1,\ldots,n_s\) exist such that every \(M_{ij}\) has shape \((m_i,n_j)\). Its assembled shape is \((\sum_i m_i,\sum_j n_j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block matrix is valid when block-row heights and block-column widths are consistent; its dimensions are their sums.
assumptions_latex: The block layout is a fixed rectangular grid.
Each block is matrix-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{shape}(M)=\left(\sum_{i=1}^r m_i,\sum_{j=1}^s n_j\right).

notation.meaning: block in row i and column j

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Matrix Compatibility
Linear-Algebra Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension predicates for ordinary matrix-vector and matrix-matrix products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\), \(B\), and \(x\) have shapes \((m,n)\), \((p,q)\), and \((r)\), respectively. The matrix product \(AB\) is defined exactly when \(n=p\), and then has shape \((m,q)\). The matrix-vector product \(Ax\) is defined exactly when \(n=r\), and then has shape \((m)\). Addition of two vectors or matrices is defined without broadcasting exactly when their complete shapes agree. Transposition maps shape \((m,n)\) to \((n,m)\). These predicates concern dimensional validity only and do not establish algebraic properties such as symmetry or definiteness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear-algebra operations are shape valid when contracted dimensions agree; dimensional validity alone does not imply symmetry, definiteness, or other structure.
assumptions_latex: \(m,n,p,q,r\in\mathbb N_{>0}\).
Products use ordinary two-dimensional matrix conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(AB\) is compatible iff \(n=p\), while \(Ax\) is compatible iff \(n=r\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-dimensional compatibility predicates are mathematically correct and the condition content kind is appropriate, but the record has no source establishing that these are the intended modeling-system operator semantics.
