knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local witness structure for a successful bottom-up metadata classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A root metadata certificate consists of the leaf declarations and, for every reachable atom node, the selected atom contract together with the child classifications and the local composition-rule conclusion. It is checkable in child-before-parent order. It certifies only the derived metadata relative to those contracts; an unsupported atom, failed domain or shape premise, or failed composition premise prevents construction of a root certificate but does not prove that the represented function is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A successful certificate records each leaf declaration and each node's contract, child classifications, and local transfer conclusion. Failure to build it means the expression is not certified by these rules, not necessarily nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: Local contracts and transfer rules have checkable premises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{all local witnesses valid}\Rightarrow\text{root metadata is certified relative to the supplied contracts}.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Metadata Certificate
Bottom-Up Metadata Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Postorder curvature, sign, shape, and domain analysis of an expression DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an acyclic expression graph and a trusted atom registry. Process nodes in topological order from leaves to roots. Initialize each constant or variable with its declared shape, sign, curvature, and domain. At an atom node \(v=a(v_1,\ldots,v_r)\), retrieve the atom signature, check argument shapes and domains, and apply its curvature and monotonicity rules to child metadata. Store either the derived metadata and local certificate or a rejection reason. Stop unsuccessfully at the first invalid node; otherwise output root metadata together with the collected local certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse the expression DAG from leaves upward, combining child metadata with trusted atom signatures and returning root metadata, certificates, or a precise rejection.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Every referenced atom has a registry entry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs certified root metadata or rejects at a node whose signature or composition rule fails.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the checker-architecture leaf and the postorder analysis is well specified for a finite acyclic graph. A source is required for the claimed DCP metadata fields, certificate behavior, and first-failure architecture.

children.title: Atom Registry Semantic Lookup
children.top_down_role: Registry-mediated access to atom semantics.

children.title: Atom Signature Lookup
children.top_down_role: Registry access to atom arity, argument roles, shapes, domains, plus value classifications.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional contract for retrieving an atom's registered shape, domain, sign, and curvature semantics; monotonicity interpretation and registry corruption are owned by sibling leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R(a,c)\) be the registered signatures for atom identifier \(a\) applicable to call descriptor \(c\), where \(c\) records arity, argument shapes and value spaces, and literal options. Lookup filters the signatures by their declared applicability predicates. It succeeds only when the registry's dispatch relation determines one semantic contract; it then returns that contract's output shape, domain, sign, curvature, and references to argument-monotonicity data. No match is an unsupported-call result, and an unresolved multiple match is an ambiguity result, not a certified signature.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter an atom's registered signatures against the call descriptor and return metadata only when the registry's dispatch rule determines one contract; otherwise report unsupported or ambiguous lookup.
assumptions_latex: The registry defines decidable applicability predicates and a deterministic dispatch relation.
Returned metadata is treated as a conditional registry contract, not as independently proved analytic truth.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{lookup}(a,c)\in\{\operatorname{success}(S),\operatorname{unsupported},\operatorname{ambiguous}\},\quad \operatorname{success}(S)\Rightarrow S\text{ is the uniquely dispatched applicable contract}.
knowledge_statements.title: Signature Matching Contract
Atom Signature Lookup
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Registry lookup selecting semantic metadata for an atom application.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an atom identifier \(a\), ordered argument shapes and types \(\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_r)\), and any literal parameters. Query the trusted registry for signatures of \(a\) with arity \(r\). Discard signatures whose type, shape, or parameter predicates fail. If exactly one most-specific signature remains, return its output shape, domain, sign, curvature, and per-argument monotonicity metadata. If none remains, reject the application; if incomparable signatures remain, report an ambiguity rather than selecting one arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Match an atom application against registered signatures and return the unique most-specific semantic contract; reject missing or ambiguous matches.
assumptions_latex: The registry supplies decidable signature predicates.
Signature specificity is defined by the registry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Lookup returns one applicable semantic signature or a missing-signature or ambiguity failure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits atom-signature lookup, but unique-most-specific dispatch, ambiguity handling, and the returned metadata contract are registry-design choices rather than universal DCP facts. No source or defined registry specification supports those choices.

children.title: Argument Monotonicity Lookup
children.top_down_role: Registry access to increasing, decreasing, constant, sign-dependent, or unknown argument behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract semantic query after an applicable atom signature has been resolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After an applicable atom signature with domain \(D\) has been resolved, query each argument position \(i\) for certified coordinatewise monotonicity on \(D\). Return nondecreasing if \(f(z)\le f(z')\) whenever \(z,z'\in D\) agree outside coordinate \(i\) and \(z_i\le z_i'\); return nonincreasing when the inequality is reversed; return constant when both hold; otherwise return uncertified. The result is semantic metadata for the composition check, not a claim of monotonicity outside the applicable domain or signature variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each argument of an already resolved atom signature, lookup reports nondecreasing, nonincreasing, constant, or uncertified monotonicity on that signature's domain slice.
assumptions_latex: An applicable atom signature and its domain \(D\) have already been resolved.
The output order on the atom's values and the coordinate order for argument \(i\) are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The query returns a sound coordinatewise monotonicity label for each argument on }D.

notation.meaning: Registered atom under the resolved signature
Domain of the resolved signature variant

knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Slice Argument Monotonicity Query

assumptions_latex: The atom registry stores a signature for every admitted atom and arity.
Each argument has a declared domain and a curvature class supplied by bottom-up analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lookup returns exactly the monotonicity labels used by the DCP composition rule, or rejects the signature when no applicable registry entry exists.

notation.meaning: Curvature metadata of the argument expressions

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: DCP composition checks require coordinatewise monotonicity metadata from the atom registry.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic lookup for coordinatewise monotonicity during bottom-up DCP checking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an atom occurrence \(f(e_1,\ldots,e_m)\), determine the applicable registered signature from the atom identifier, arity, argument domains, and any declared parameter attributes. For each \(i\), return \(\mu_i=\uparrow\) when \(f\) is nondecreasing in coordinate \(i\) on the applicable domain slice, \(\mu_i=\downarrow\) when it is nonincreasing, \(\mu_i=0\) when it is constant, and \(\mu_i=?\) when no monotonicity is certified. The checker may accept a convex outer atom only with convex arguments in nondecreasing coordinates, concave arguments in nonincreasing coordinates, and affine arguments in unknown coordinates; reverse convex and concave for a concave outer atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lookup selects the applicable atom signature and returns each argument's certified monotonicity, which determines whether the DCP composition rule accepts its curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Argument Monotonicity Lookup

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the lookup leaf, and the DCP monotonicity branches are broadly standard. However, no source is cited for the proposed registry key, constant and unknown labels, rejection behavior, or exact checker architecture. An authoritative DCP implementation or specification with a precise locator is required before the mathematical and operational details can be relied upon.

children.title: Context-Sensitive Signature Variants
children.top_down_role: Atom metadata variants selected by argument shape, sign, value space, axis, or declared options.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-dependent selection among an atom's registered semantic variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For registered variants \(\{(P_j,S_j)\}_{j\in J}\) and certified call context \(c\), define \(A(c)=\{j\in J:P_j(c)\}\). Dispatch is well defined when the registry's declared precedence selects one member of \(A(c)\), or when all surviving members induce the same semantic contract. If \(A(c)=\varnothing\), the call is unsupported in that context; if surviving variants are semantically incompatible and precedence does not resolve them, the call is ambiguous. Guards may depend on declared shape, value space, sign, axis, literal parameters, and options, but not on unproved runtime properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate registered guards against certified call metadata. Dispatch succeeds when precedence selects one variant or all surviving variants agree; uncovered or unresolved incompatible contexts cannot be certified.
assumptions_latex: The variant family and each guard are finite or otherwise effectively decidable.
Guard inputs are certified analysis metadata or literal data.
Any precedence relation is part of the registry specification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A(c)=\varnothing\Rightarrow\operatorname{unsupported};\quad A(c)\text{ unresolved and incompatible}\Rightarrow\operatorname{ambiguous};\quad\text{otherwise dispatch returns a well-defined }S.

notation.meaning: Guard and semantic signature of variant j

knowledge_statements.title: Guarded Signature Dispatch

assumptions_latex: A finite registry of signature variants is associated with each atom identifier.
Variant predicates depend only on declared domains, shapes, signs, parameter values, and other analysis metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A signature is usable precisely when one unique applicable variant is selected; absence or ambiguity prevents certification.

notation.meaning: Metadata context for an atom occurrence
Predicate and semantic signature of variant j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Conditional atom semantics are modeled by guarded signature variants.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule for atom signatures whose semantics vary with certified context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an atom occurrence with context \(c\), let \((P_j,S_j)\) be its registered variants, where \(P_j:\mathcal{C}\to\{\mathrm{true},\mathrm{false}\}\) is a decidable guard and \(S_j\) contains domain, sign, curvature, and argument-monotonicity metadata. The occurrence has a well-defined context-sensitive signature exactly when \(|J(c)|=1\), where \(J(c)=\{j:P_j(c)\}\). The checker then uses the unique \(S_j\). If \(|J(c)|=0\), the occurrence is unsupported in that context; if \(|J(c)|>1\) and the selected signatures are not semantically identical, lookup is ambiguous and must not certify the expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A context-sensitive atom is certifiable only when its metadata makes exactly one semantic signature variant applicable, up to identical overlapping variants.
knowledge_statements.title: Context-Sensitive Signature Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the signature-variant leaf. The unique-or-semantically-identical selection policy is a plausible registry design, but it is not a universal DCP rule and no evidence supports the finite guarded-family representation or ambiguity policy. A precise implementation or formal-system source is required.

children.title: Registry Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Missing entries, incompatible signatures, incomplete monotonicity metadata, plus untrusted registrations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal false-positive family demonstrating the registry trust boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a registry incorrectly label \(q(x)=-x^2\) as convex on \(\mathbb{R}\). A checker that trusts this label may accept minimization of \(q(x)\), or the sublevel constraint \(q(x)\le -1\), as convex. Yet \(q\) is concave and \(\{x:-x^2\le -1\}=(-\infty,-1]\cup[1,\infty)\) is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the concave function minus x squared is registered as convex, a trusting checker can falsely accept a nonconvex objective or sublevel constraint.
assumptions_latex: The checker trusts the registered curvature label.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{An unsound curvature registration can yield a false DCP certificate.}
knowledge_statements.title: Unsound Curvature Registration Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary for any checker that trusts registered atom semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a checker certifies compositions using registered contracts without independently reproving them. Certification is sound only relative to registrations whose implemented function and declared domain agree and whose shape, sign, curvature, and monotonicity claims hold on every context in which they are used. Missing required fields, an unsupported call, contradictory contracts, or unresolved incompatible variants must produce an unknown or rejection result. An incorrect semantic field can produce false certification; a missing sound entry produces only incompleteness when the checker fails closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A registry-driven checker must reject or return unknown for missing, contradictory, ambiguous, or unsupported metadata. Incorrect trusted metadata can cause false certification, whereas a missing entry causes only incompleteness under fail-closed handling.
assumptions_latex: The checker relies on registered semantic contracts.
Rejection or unknown is not interpreted as mathematical nonconvexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{sound trusted registrations and fail-closed dispatch}\Rightarrow\text{registry-relative soundness};\quad\text{unsound trusted metadata}\not\Rightarrow\text{sound certification}.
knowledge_statements.title: Fail-Closed Registry Boundary

assumptions_latex: Registry entries are intended to be sound certificates for their declared domains.
The checker relies on registry metadata without re-proving analytic properties.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Beyond these boundaries, registry lookup cannot serve as a sound DCP certificate.

notation.meaning: Declared domain of an atom signature

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Sound registry-driven checking requires correct, complete, and unambiguous semantic entries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness boundary of registry-driven atom certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Registry-based certification is sound only if every selected signature \(S=(D,\kappa,\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m)\) satisfies four boundaries: the implemented atom agrees with the registered mathematical function on \(D\); the curvature label \(\kappa\) is valid throughout \(D\); every monotonicity label \(\mu_i\) is valid on the domain slices used by composition; and conditional guards select a unique compatible signature. A missing entry yields incompleteness, while an incorrect domain, curvature, monotonicity, or overlapping incompatible guard can yield false certification. Therefore unsupported, contradictory, or ambiguous registry states must be rejected rather than assigned optimistic metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Registry certification fails safely unless implementation, domain, curvature, monotonicity, and conditional-variant metadata are mutually sound and unambiguous.
knowledge_statements.title: Registry Consistency Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the terminal container. The stated boundaries are plausible soundness requirements, but the claims about checker trust, incompatible guards, and false certification describe a particular registry architecture without cited evidence. A source specifying that architecture and its failure behavior is required.

children.title: Top-Level Problem Validation
children.top_down_role: Objective and constraint validation after expression analysis.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Final checker pass over already analyzed objective and constraint roots.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given certified metadata for an objective and \(q\) constraints, check the objective orientation and each constraint's curvature orientation, domain validity, and shape compatibility, and accept if and only if every check succeeds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The final pass checks the objective and every constraint root and accepts exactly when all checks pass.
assumptions_latex: Expression metadata have already been computed and are accessible at every problem root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{accept}(P)\iff\bigwedge_{r\in\{\mathrm{objective},1,\ldots,q\}}\operatorname{valid}(r).
knowledge_statements.title: Top-Level Validation Pass

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity excludes preceding expression-tree or expression-DAG analysis and diagnostic storage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every analyzed problem root exposes constant-time curvature, domain-status, and shape queries, validating one objective and \(q\) constraints takes \(O(q)\) time and \(O(1)\) auxiliary space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After expression analysis, the final validation pass is linear in the number of constraints.
assumptions_latex: Every required metadata query at a problem root takes \(O(1)\) time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{validate}}(q)=O(q),\qquad S_{\mathrm{aux}}(q)=O(1).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear Final-Pass Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Problem-level soundness after expression curvatures, domains, and shapes have been soundly certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a minimization problem passes top-level DCP validation, its objective is convex and its feasible set is convex. If a maximization problem passes, its objective is concave and its feasible set is convex. Thus every accepted problem is a convex optimization problem after sign reversal of a maximization objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sound expression metadata and successful top-level validation certify a convex optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: All expression curvature, domain, and shape metadata are sound.
Every objective and constraint passes the top-level DCP rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{DCPValid}(P)\Longrightarrow P\text{ is a convex optimization problem}.
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of Top-Level DCP Validation

assumptions_latex: Every objective and constraint expression has already received sound curvature metadata.
Constraint equalities and inequalities use their ordinary real-valued componentwise meanings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The problem is DCP-valid exactly when its objective orientation and every constraint satisfy the displayed curvature conditions.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: These are the standard top-level DCP objective and constraint rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar top-level DCP validation after expression metadata analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A minimization problem is DCP-valid only if \(f_0\) is convex; a maximization problem is DCP-valid only if \(f_0\) is concave. A feasibility problem may use a constant objective. Each inequality \(f_i\leq g_i\) is valid only if \(f_i\) is convex and \(g_i\) is concave, equivalently \(f_i-g_i\leq0\) has a convex left side. Each equality \(h_j=k_j\) is valid only if both sides are affine, equivalently \(h_j-k_j=0\) is affine. All expressions must also satisfy their certified domains and have compatible shapes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After expression analysis, minimization needs a convex objective, maximization a concave objective, inequalities convex-to-concave, and equalities affine-to-affine.
knowledge_statements.title: Top-Level Problem Validation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind correctly expresses top-level DCP validation, and the objective, inequality, and equality rules are standard. Nevertheless, the record supplies no authoritative textbook or DCP specification citation with a section or page locator. The inventory sources shown do not address disciplined convex programming, so source support is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: DCP Rejection Does Not Prove Nonconvexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed grammar-incompleteness example based on expression-level product analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The product expression \(x x\) may fail a standard DCP product rule even though it represents the convex function \(x^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex function can have an expression that fails DCP analysis.
assumptions_latex: Multiplication of two nonconstant expressions is unsupported by the applicable DCP product rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \neg\operatorname{DCPValid}(x x)\quad\text{while}\quad x\mapsto x^2\text{ is convex}.
review_flags: deferred_misplaced_claim: The failure occurs during expression-level curvature analysis, whereas this leaf owns objective and constraint validation after expression analysis.
cross_index_preferred: Place the grammar-incompleteness example under the expression-analysis or DCP-rule failure-boundary topic.
knowledge_statements.title: DCP Rejection Does Not Prove Nonconvexity

intermediate_metadata.reason: The locally owned inventory is the immutable acceptance condition, its soundness consequence, the final root scan, and its conditional linear complexity. The proposed product counterexample is deferred because it belongs to expression-level DCP incompleteness. Bottom-up analysis, atom-registry lookup, and metadata reuse remain excluded architecture siblings.

children.title: Reusable Metadata Analysis
children.top_down_role: Reuse of semantic results across shared or unchanged expression structure.

children.title: Node-Level Metadata Memoization
children.top_down_role: Cached semantic classifications keyed by stable expression-node identity.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Creation and retrieval of node-local metadata cache entries; shared-reference reuse and invalidation policy are owned by sibling leaves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M(v,\eta)\) be deterministic bottom-up metadata for expression node \(v\) under complete semantic environment \(\eta\). To evaluate \((v,\eta)\), return a valid entry from table \(T\) if present. Otherwise evaluate each child under its required environment, apply the local metadata transfer, store the resulting success or stable local failure at \(T[(v,\eta)]\), and return it. On a finite DAG the recursion terminates. During one analysis epoch with fixed valid keys, each distinct pair \((v,\eta)\) is computed at most once; a stored entry is correct exactly when it equals fresh bottom-up evaluation for that pair.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cache deterministic metadata by node and complete semantic environment. On a miss, evaluate children, compute and store the local result; on a valid hit, return it. Each distinct key is computed at most once per fixed analysis epoch.
assumptions_latex: The expression representation is a finite directed acyclic graph.
The key identifies stable node structure and every environmental input affecting metadata.
Local transfers are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T[(v,\eta)]\text{ valid}\Rightarrow T[(v,\eta)]=M(v,\eta),\qquad \#\operatorname{computations}(v,\eta)\le 1\text{ per fixed epoch}.

notation.meaning: Expression node and complete semantic environment

knowledge_statements.title: Node-and-Environment Memoization

assumptions_latex: The expression representation is a directed acyclic graph.
Analysis results are deterministic functions of a node and an analysis environment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each valid cache entry equals a fresh bottom-up analysis of the same node under the same environment.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Pure bottom-up DAG analysis admits memoization keyed by node and semantic environment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memoization of deterministic semantic metadata at expression nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: To analyze node \(v\) under environment \(\eta\), first query \(T[(v,\eta)]\). If a valid entry exists, return it. Otherwise recursively obtain metadata for every child of \(v\), apply the registered atom rule and domain checks to compute \(M(v,\eta)\), store that value at \(T[(v,\eta)]\), and return it. The key must distinguish every environmental attribute capable of changing the result, including parameter attributes and registry version. Evaluation terminates because children precede parents in the expression directed acyclic graph. The output for a root is its stored or newly computed metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Analyze each expression node once per semantic environment, cache its metadata, and reuse it whenever the complete cache key still matches.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Level Metadata Memoization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits node-level memoization. The procedure is coherent under its assumptions, but the environment key, registry-version dependency, validity semantics, and claimed DCP checker behavior are implementation-specific and uncited. An inspectable implementation or architecture source is required.

children.title: Common-Subexpression Cache Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of cached results across multiple references to a shared graph node.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse across multiple graph references to the same immutable expression node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an immutable expression DAG, and let metadata be a deterministic function \(M(v,\eta)\) of node \(v\) and complete semantic environment \(\eta\). Every reference to the same pair \((v,\eta)\) has the same result, so one valid cached evaluation may serve all incoming parent paths. If each distinct node is evaluated once and its local rule costs \(T_v\), full analysis costs \(O(|V|+|E|+\sum_vT_v)\), whereas occurrence-wise evaluation of the expanded tree may repeat a shared descendant once per occurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All references to the same immutable DAG node under the same complete environment may share one metadata evaluation. This makes work proportional to the DAG plus rule costs rather than the potentially larger expanded tree.
assumptions_latex: Node identity denotes immutable structure.
The environment key contains every semantic dependency.
Metadata evaluation is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (v,\eta)=(v',\eta')\Rightarrow M(v,\eta)=M(v',\eta'),\qquad \operatorname{work}=O\!\left(|V|+|E|+\sum_{v\in V}T_v\right).

notation.meaning: Metadata for node v in semantic environment eta

knowledge_statements.title: Shared-Node Semantic Reuse

assumptions_latex: Structurally shared occurrences refer to the same immutable expression node.
The cache key includes every semantic dependency of metadata analysis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reuse preserves the metadata result and reduces analysis from occurrence-wise work to node-wise work.

notation.meaning: Number of syntactic occurrences in an expanded tree

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Referentially transparent DAG nodes can share cached semantic analysis.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of semantic analysis across identical shared DAG nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an immutable expression directed acyclic graph and suppose two parent paths reach the same node \(v\). Because metadata analysis is a deterministic function of \(v\) and its complete environment key, both occurrences require the same value \(M(v,\eta)\). A cache entry computed along the first path may therefore be returned along every later path with the same key. If each node rule takes time proportional to its arity, complete analysis costs \(O(|V|+|E|)\), rather than work proportional to \(N_{\mathrm{occ}}\) in the fully expanded expression tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shared immutable subexpressions may reuse one metadata result, preserving semantics while making analysis proportional to the DAG rather than its expanded tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Subexpression Cache Reuse

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind is suitable for cache reuse, though the record also embeds a complexity bound. The semantic reuse claim and the O(|V|+|E|) bound depend on immutable node identity, complete cache keys, traversal details, and constant-cost rule operations beyond arity. No cited source establishes these conditions for a DCP checker.

children.title: Incremental Dependency Reanalysis
children.top_down_role: Selective reconsideration of graph regions affected by changed symbolic inputs or metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective recomputation after changes to local semantics or cached dependencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For changed nodes \(S\) in a finite expression DAG \(G=(V,E)\), let \(A(S)\) be \(S\) together with every ancestor reachable through child-to-parent dependency edges. Retain valid entries outside \(A(S)\), and recompute nodes of \(A(S)\) in child-before-parent order from current local inputs and child metadata. Propagation above a recomputed node may stop only when the node's complete semantic result, including every component observed by parents, is unchanged. Under complete dependency edges and deterministic local transfers, the resulting metadata equals a fresh whole-DAG analysis. Work is \(O(|V_A|+|E_A|+\sum_{v\in V_A}T_v)\) for the actually processed affected region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recompute changed nodes and their dependent ancestors from children upward, retaining unaffected valid entries. With complete dependencies, the result matches full recomputation and costs only the processed affected region plus rule costs.
assumptions_latex: The graph is finite and acyclic.
Every semantic child-to-parent dependency is represented.
Local transfers are deterministic and unaffected retained entries are valid.
Early stopping compares every result component observable by parents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M^{\mathrm{incremental}}=M^{\mathrm{full}},\qquad \operatorname{work}=O\!\left(|V_A|+|E_A|+\sum_{v\in V_A}T_v\right).

notation.meaning: Changed nodes and their dependency ancestors
Actually processed affected nodes and dependency edges

knowledge_statements.title: Affected-Ancestor Reanalysis

assumptions_latex: Metadata at a node depends only on its local semantics, environment, and child metadata.
Reverse dependency edges from each node to its parents are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reanalysis of the affected closure produces the same metadata as full recomputation while retaining all unaffected valid entries.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Incremental DAG dataflow analysis recomputes the reverse-reachable dependency closure.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incremental recomputation of metadata after localized semantic changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given changed nodes \(S\), compute \(A(S)\), the set containing \(S\) and every node reachable from \(S\) through reverse child-to-parent dependency edges. Invalidate cached metadata for \(A(S)\), retain entries for \(V\setminus A(S)\), and process \(A(S)\) in child-before-parent topological order. At each processed node, recompute metadata from its current local semantics and current child metadata; optionally stop propagation above a node when its recomputed value and validity token equal the previous values. Return the root metadata after every affected root ancestor has been processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a local change, invalidate and recompute only the changed nodes and their dependent ancestors in child-before-parent order.
knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Dependency Reanalysis

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits incremental dependency reanalysis. Reverse-reachable invalidation is a standard incremental-dataflow pattern, but the optional early-stop rule, validity tokens, and equivalence to full DCP recomputation require a cited incremental-analysis or implementation source with a precise locator.

children.title: Cache Invalidation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural mutation, parameter-class changes, registry updates, plus context changes requiring cache retirement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient semantic condition for reusing a cached metadata result, independent of any particular token encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_v\) be all inputs on which the metadata computation at node \(v\) semantically depends, including its operator and children, relevant leaf or parameter attributes and values, selected registry contracts, analysis mode, and transitive child results. A cached value is reusable exactly when every member of \(D_v\) has the same semantic value as when the entry was computed. A validity token is sufficient only if token equality implies this semantic equality; hash collision or omission of a dependency invalidates that implication. Changes outside \(D_v\) require no invalidation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached result is reusable exactly while all of its semantic dependencies are unchanged. Tokens are sound only when equality guarantees that fact; unrelated changes need not invalidate the entry.
assumptions_latex: The metadata computation is deterministic from its semantic dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{reuse}(v)\Longleftrightarrow D_v^{\mathrm{current}}=D_v^{\mathrm{cached}};\qquad \tau_v^{\mathrm{current}}=\tau_v^{\mathrm{cached}}\Rightarrow D_v^{\mathrm{current}}=D_v^{\mathrm{cached}}\text{ is required for token soundness}.

notation.meaning: Complete semantic dependency state for node v

knowledge_statements.title: Complete-Dependency Cache Validity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal stale-certification family caused by an incomplete cache dependency key.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the same syntactic node \(v=\sqrt{x}\). In environment \(\eta_1\), \(x\) is declared nonnegative and the node receives a valid real-valued concave classification. If the declaration is removed in \(\eta_2\) but the cache key records only node identity, reuse returns the obsolete classification even though the required domain premise is no longer certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Caching square root only by node identity becomes stale when the argument's nonnegativity declaration changes, demonstrating why environment attributes must be dependencies.
assumptions_latex: The checker uses the nonnegativity declaration to certify the square-root domain.
The incomplete key omits that declaration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \tau_v(\eta_1)=\tau_v(\eta_2)\centernot\Rightarrow M_v(\eta_1)=M_v(\eta_2)\text{ when a semantic dependency is omitted}.

notation.meaning: Analysis environments before and after the attribute change

knowledge_statements.title: Omitted-Attribute Stale Cache

assumptions_latex: Every cached result records a dependency token covering all semantic inputs used to compute it.
Expression nodes are immutable or expose version changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cached result may be reused if and only if every dependency represented by its validity token remains unchanged.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Cache validity is bounded by the complete transitive semantic dependency set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic events that delimit valid reuse of cached DCP metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cache entry \((M_v,\tau_v)\) is reusable exactly when \(\tau_v=\widehat{\tau}_v\). The token must change whenever any metadata-determining input changes: node operator or arguments, child metadata, shape or domain, variable attributes, parameter value when semantics are value-dependent, certified sign or integrality, atom-registry signature or version, or checker policy. Invalidating a node also invalidates every cached ancestor whose token transitively depends on it. Changes outside this dependency closure need not invalidate \(M_v\). Omitting any semantic dependency from \(\tau_v\) permits stale certification and therefore crosses the soundness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cached metadata remains valid only while every local and transitive semantic dependency, including registry and parameter-sensitive state, is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Cache Invalidation Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits cache invalidation boundaries. The if-and-only-if reuse claim is valid only if token equality is formally defined to be a complete and collision-free representation of every semantic dependency. That token model and the listed invalidation events are architecture-specific and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Trusted Atom-Set Library
children.top_down_role: Trusted function and set families determining the expressive reach of disciplined models.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Basic functions and sets
Atomic functions and constraints
Sections 3.3 and 4.2, conic-quadratic and semidefinite representability

children.title: Atom Certification-Representation Contracts
children.top_down_role: Information required for atoms to participate in certification and canonicalization.

children.title: Composition Metadata Contracts
children.top_down_role: Composition-facing semantic classifications.

children.title: Atom Curvature Contracts
children.top_down_role: Affine, convex, concave, quasiconvex, quasiconcave, or unknown classifications exposed by atoms.

assumptions_latex: The atom is real-valued on a declared convex domain.
The contract is trusted only on that declared domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The curvature label is a valid atom contract exactly when the corresponding displayed inequality holds throughout the declared domain.

notation.meaning: Registered atom and its convex domain

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Atom curvature contracts are the defining Jensen inequalities restricted to the registered domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical soundness predicate for registered scalar atom curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For all \(x,y\in D\) and \(\theta\in[0,1]\), a registered convex contract requires \(f(\theta x+(1-\theta)y)\leq\theta f(x)+(1-\theta)f(y)\). A registered concave contract requires the reverse inequality. An affine contract requires equality. The domain \(D\) must itself be convex for this contract and must include all shape, sign, and definiteness restrictions under which the label is asserted. A checker may use \(\kappa\) in composition only for arguments already certified to lie in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom's curvature contract is sound when its declared Jensen inequality holds over every pair of points in its registered convex domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Curvature Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind appropriately states when a curvature contract is sound, and the Jensen inequalities are mathematically standard. No authoritative convex-analysis or DCP atom-library source with a specific locator is cited, and the supplied inventory does not establish the registry-contract claims.

children.title: Argument Monotonicity Contracts
children.top_down_role: Per-argument increasing, decreasing, constant, sign-dependent, or unknown behavior.

assumptions_latex: The atom is real-valued on a declared domain.
Other coordinates are fixed at values for which both compared points remain in the domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A coordinate label is sound exactly when its order inequality holds on every admissible slice of the declared domain.

notation.meaning: Vectors differing only in coordinate i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: DCP argument monotonicity is coordinatewise order monotonicity on admissible domain slices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness predicate for coordinatewise atom monotonicity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix coordinate \(i\). For every \(x,y\in D\) satisfying \(x_j=y_j\) for \(j\neq i\) and \(x_i\leq y_i\), the label \(\mu_i=\uparrow\) requires \(f(x)\leq f(y)\), while \(\mu_i=\downarrow\) requires \(f(x)\geq f(y)\). The label \(\mu_i=0\) requires equality, and \(\mu_i=?\) asserts no usable order property. These requirements apply over the entire registered domain slice, including sign or definiteness restrictions. Only certified labels may justify the corresponding DCP composition branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An argument monotonicity label must hold for every admissible pair differing only in that argument; unknown monotonicity grants no composition rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Argument Monotonicity Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits argument-monotonicity contracts, and the coordinatewise order conditions are precise for scalar real arguments. The connection to certified DCP composition branches and the label system remains uncited. An authoritative DCP source or atom-library specification with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Conditional Curvature Regimes
children.top_down_role: Curvature classifications selected by argument signs, domains, shapes, parameter values, or atom options.

assumptions_latex: Each regime predicate is decidable from metadata certified before atom composition.
Each regime supplies a curvature label valid on its associated domain subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conditional curvature contract is usable only where applicable regimes agree on a sound curvature label or a unique regime applies.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Conditional curvature is represented by guarded domain-restricted curvature certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarded representation of curvature that changes across certified argument regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a conditional curvature contract by a finite family \(\{(P_r,D_r,\kappa_r)\}_{r\in R}\). For context \(c\), regime \(r\) applies when \(P_r(c)\) is true and the arguments are certified to lie in \(D_r\). On each \(D_r\), the atom must satisfy the Jensen inequality corresponding to \(\kappa_r\). The effective curvature is \(\kappa_r\) when exactly one regime applies, or when all applicable regimes declare the same sound label. If no regime applies, or applicable regimes conflict, curvature is unknown and the atom cannot be certified through a conditional curvature rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional curvature is a family of guarded domain-specific curvature certificates; uncovered or conflicting contexts yield unknown curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Curvature Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind matches a guarded conditional-curvature container. The finite regime family, agreement rule for overlapping regimes, and fallback to unknown curvature are plausible design choices rather than source-independent DCP facts. No evidence supports this exact representation or selection semantics.

children.title: Conditional Monotonicity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Argument order behavior selected by value regions, signs, or structural attributes.

assumptions_latex: Each regime predicate is decidable from metadata available before composition.
Each regime's coordinatewise monotonicity labels are valid throughout its associated domain subset.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conditional monotonicity is usable only when applicable regimes determine one sound label for each coordinate needed by composition.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise monotonicity vector in regime r

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Conditional monotonicity is represented by guarded domain-restricted coordinatewise order certificates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarded representation of argument monotonicity that changes across certified regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent conditional monotonicity by \(\{(P_r,D_r,\mu^{(r)})\}_{r\in R}\). Regime \(r\) applies in context \(c\) when \(P_r(c)\) holds and the atom arguments are certified to lie in \(D_r\). Each component \(\mu_i^{(r)}\) must satisfy its coordinatewise order inequality throughout \(D_r\). For coordinate \(i\), the effective label is the common label of all applicable regimes; a unique applicable regime supplies its own label. If no regime applies or applicable regimes disagree, the effective label is \(?\), so that coordinate cannot justify a monotonicity-dependent composition step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional monotonicity uses guarded domain-specific label vectors; missing or conflicting regimes make the affected argument monotonicity unknown.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Monotonicity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits conditional monotonicity regimes. The guarded vectors and common-label rule are coherent, but the exact overlap, conflict, and unknown-label semantics are implementation-specific and unsupported by any citation. An authoritative atom-library or DCP checker source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Semantic Contract Gaps
children.top_down_role: Missing or insufficient curvature or monotonicity metadata that prevents disciplined certification.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to Y\) is an atom proposed for a disciplined convex modeling library.
Each argument expression has certified curvature, sign, shape, and domain metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Gamma_f\not\vdash \mathcal C(f(e_1,\ldots,e_k))\) whenever required metadata are absent or unresolved.

notation.meaning: declared semantic contract of the atom

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: A DCP composition certificate requires complete domain, curvature, monotonicity, sign, and structural metadata.
No supplied locator directly documents semantic contract gaps in an atom library.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure concerns certifiability by DCP rules, not the actual convexity of the mathematical expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:D\to Y\) have declared contract \(\Gamma_f\), and let \(e_1,\ldots,e_k\) be certified argument expressions. A semantic contract gap occurs when deciding the requested certificate \(\mathcal C(f(e_1,\ldots,e_k))\) requires a domain, curvature, monotonicity, sign, value-range, argument-role, or shape fact not entailed by \(\Gamma_f\). In that case the composition is uncertifiable under the library rules and must be rejected or deferred, even if the represented function is mathematically well defined and possesses the requested curvature. Missing metadata may not be replaced by an unstated property of a particular implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A missing semantic fact makes an atom composition uncertifiable by DCP, although the underlying expression may still be mathematically valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Semantic Contract Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the statement appropriately distinguishes DCP certifiability from actual convexity. However, no inspectable source supports the asserted mandatory metadata set or the reject-or-defer behavior, so the proposed contract cannot be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Atom Domain-Range Contracts
children.top_down_role: Domain and value information supplied by an atom.

children.title: Atom Domain Contracts
children.top_down_role: Permitted argument regions supplied by an atom implementation.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a \(k\)-argument atom with ambient argument spaces \(X_1,\ldots,X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) is admissible exactly when \((x_1,\ldots,x_k)\in D_f\).

notation.meaning: declared effective domain of the atom

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: An atom domain contract is naturally the exact admissible subset of the product of its argument spaces.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP atom-domain contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The contract records the exact effective domain, including coupled restrictions among arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The domain contract of a \(k\)-argument atom \(f\) is a declared set \(D_f\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_k\) such that \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) has a finite, library-defined value exactly for tuples in \(D_f\). The declaration must include strict or non-strict scalar inequalities, cone membership, definiteness, dimension requirements, and coupled restrictions whenever they are part of the effective domain. For extended-real convex atoms one may equivalently define \(f(x)=+\infty\) outside \(D_f\), but the modeling front end must still generate or verify the constraints establishing membership in \(D_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An atom domain contract gives the exact argument tuples on which the atom is defined and identifies every required domain constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Domain Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Atom Domain Contracts, and the variables and admissibility condition are explicit. A source is required for the library-specific claims that the contract is exact, must enumerate all listed restrictions, and obligates the front end to generate or verify domain constraints.

children.title: Atom Sign Contracts
children.top_down_role: Output sign classifications available under supported argument regimes.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D_f\to Y\) is an atom whose codomain carries an entrywise order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The declared sign must contain \(f(D_f)\) and is valid only if \(f(D_f)\subseteq S_f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Sign metadata are sound precisely when the declared sign class contains every attainable output.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP atom-sign contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign is an output invariant over the declared domain, interpreted entrywise for array-valued atoms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sign contract for an atom \(f:D_f\to Y\) declares a set \(S_f\subseteq Y\), usually one of the entrywise classes nonnegative, nonpositive, zero, or unknown. The contract is sound if and only if \(f(D_f)\subseteq S_f\). A nonnegative declaration requires \(f(x)\geq 0\) for every \(x\in D_f\), a nonpositive declaration requires \(f(x)\leq 0\), and a zero declaration requires \(f(x)=0\). If neither inequality is guaranteed throughout the entire declared domain, the unconditional sign must be unknown unless a separately certified conditional regime applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sign contract is valid only when every output over the atom's full declared domain belongs to the stated sign class.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Sign Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is plausible and the soundness inclusion is mathematically coherent. No cited source establishes the stated sign classes, entrywise interpretation, unconditional unknown fallback, or interaction with conditional regimes in the intended atom library.

children.title: Atom Value-Range Contracts
children.top_down_role: Output intervals, cones, matrix orders, plus structured value spaces exposed by atoms.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D_f\to Y\) is a scalar- or array-valued atom.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A range contract is sound exactly when \(f(D_f)\subseteq R_f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: A value-range contract is a sound enclosure of all outputs over the declared effective domain.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP value-range contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The declared range may be an exact image or a sound enclosure used by downstream composition rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A value-range contract for \(f:D_f\to Y\) is a declared set \(R_f\subseteq Y\) satisfying \(f(D_f)\subseteq R_f\). The set may encode intervals, cone membership, spectral bounds, integrality, or other output invariants, and it need not equal the exact image \(f(D_f)\). Any downstream inference may use only properties entailed by membership in \(R_f\). Consequently, replacing \(R_f\) by a smaller set is valid only after certifying that every attainable output remains included; replacing it by a larger set is sound but may weaken later sign, domain, or monotonicity certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-range contract soundly encloses all possible atom outputs and supplies only those output facts guaranteed by that enclosure.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Value-Range Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the enclosure condition is precise. The downstream inference and refinement claims are library-contract semantics for which no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Conditional Value Regimes
children.top_down_role: Output classifications selected by argument domains, signs, shapes, or parameter values.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D_f\to Y\) is an atom and \(P_1,\ldots,P_m\) are decidable predicates on its arguments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under certified \(P_j(x)\), the usable range is \(R_{f,j}\); without such certification it is \(R_{f,0}\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Conditional metadata may be used only when its guard is itself certified and its range implication is sound.
No supplied locator directly specifies conditional value regimes for DCP atoms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional range strengthens, but never silently replaces, the atom's unconditional range contract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A conditional value regime for \(f:D_f\to Y\) is a pair \((P_j,R_{f,j})\) such that \(x\in D_f\) and \(P_j(x)\) imply \(f(x)\in R_{f,j}\). The predicate \(P_j\) must be decidable from certified argument metadata or explicit model constraints. A compiler may use \(R_{f,j}\) only after certifying \(P_j(x)\); otherwise it must use the unconditional range \(R_{f,0}\) satisfying \(f(D_f)\subseteq R_{f,0}\). If several certified regimes apply, their combined inference may use \(\bigcap_j R_{f,j}\), provided the intersection is consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional value guarantee is usable only when its guard is certified; otherwise the atom's unconditional output range applies.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Value Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but no source supports the guard-certification or fallback rules. In addition, the final intersection should be indexed explicitly by the regimes certified for the current argument rather than by all j; source-backed semantics are needed before choosing the exact formulation.

children.title: Contract Consistency Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conflicts or gaps among declared domains, signs, value ranges, plus implementation behavior.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D_f\to Y\) has declared sign set \(S_f\), range set \(R_f\), and conditional regimes \((P_j,R_{f,j})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency requires \(R_f\cap S_f\neq\varnothing\) and, for every feasible regime, \(R_{f,j}\cap R_f\cap S_f\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: values permitted by the sign declaration

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Contract components must have a common realization on every feasible regime; empty intersections expose contradictions.
No supplied locator directly establishes these contract-consistency boundaries.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary detects contradictory declarations; nonempty intersections are necessary but do not alone prove semantic soundness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_j=\{x\in D_f:P_j(x)\}\). The domain, sign, and range declarations are inconsistent if \(D_f=\varnothing\), if \(R_f\cap S_f=\varnothing\), or if some nonempty \(F_j\) has \(R_{f,j}\cap R_f\cap S_f=\varnothing\). They are semantically unsound if any \(x\in D_f\) satisfies \(f(x)\notin R_f\cap S_f\), or if any \(x\in F_j\) satisfies \(f(x)\notin R_{f,j}\). A contradictory contract must not certify compositions. Merely passing the nonemptiness checks establishes logical compatibility, not that the declared sets actually contain all outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Atom metadata fail at contradictions among domain, sign, and range declarations, or whenever an attainable output violates a declared invariant.
knowledge_statements.title: Contract Consistency Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A failure-boundary record is appropriate, and the statement correctly notes that nonempty intersections do not prove soundness. Nevertheless, no source establishes these as the intended consistency checks, and treating an empty declared domain as inconsistent requires an explicit nonempty-domain or properness convention.

children.title: Output Shape Contracts

assumptions_latex: \(f\) accepts arguments with declared shapes \(s_1,\ldots,s_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible call with input shapes \((s_1,\ldots,s_k)\) must produce shape \(\sigma_f(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Output-shape metadata are a deterministic transfer rule on admissible input shapes.
No supplied locator directly specifies structural shape contracts for DCP atoms.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shape includes rank and dimensions; scalar expansion or broadcasting must be explicitly declared.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An output shape contract for a \(k\)-argument atom \(f\) is a partial function \(\sigma_f\) mapping each admissible input-shape tuple \((s_1,\ldots,s_k)\) to exactly one output shape. For every admissible call \(y=f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) with \(\operatorname{shape}(x_i)=s_i\), the contract requires \(\operatorname{shape}(y)=\sigma_f(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\). The domain of \(\sigma_f\) must encode dimension-equality requirements and any permitted scalar expansion, broadcasting, reduction axes, or matrix multiplication rule. An input-shape tuple outside that domain is structurally invalid, independently of curvature or numerical values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output shape contract deterministically maps every admissible tuple of argument shapes to the atom's result shape.
knowledge_statements.title: Output Shape Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Output Shape Contracts and the partial shape-transfer function is internally coherent. children.title: Atom Arity Contracts

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is represented as an ordered atom application.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A call is arity-valid exactly when its number of supplied arguments lies in \(A_f\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Arity is the set of permitted operand counts for an atom application.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP atom-arity contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The contract distinguishes fixed, optional, and variadic signatures without assigning semantic roles to arguments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An arity contract for an atom \(f\) is a nonempty set \(A_f\subseteq\mathbb N_0\) of permitted argument counts. An application \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) is arity-valid if and only if \(k\in A_f\). Fixed arity \(r\) is represented by \(A_f=\{r\}\); bounded optional arguments by a finite set; and a variadic tail beginning at \(r\) by \(A_f=\{k\in\mathbb N_0:k\geq r\}\). Defaults may supply omitted optional arguments only when the resulting expanded application has a uniquely specified ordered signature and belongs to \(A_f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arity contract states exactly which numbers of ordered arguments form valid calls to an atom.
knowledge_statements.title: Atom Arity Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Atom Arity Contracts, and the fixed and variadic cases are precise. The optional-argument and default-expansion semantics are implementation-specific and have no cited support.

children.title: Argument Role Contracts
children.top_down_role: Distinctions among expression arguments, numerical data, axes, indices, weights, plus configuration values.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) has an arity-valid ordered signature with argument positions \(1,\ldots,k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each position \(i\) is valid only when its supplied object belongs to the class and variability permitted by \(\rho_i\).

notation.meaning: semantic role assigned to argument position i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Argument roles constrain whether positions accept expressions, constant data, indices, axes, or other parameters.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP argument-role contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Roles distinguish mathematical expressions from structural or constant parameters that control atom semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An argument role contract assigns each position \(i\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) a role \(\rho_i\) specifying the admissible object class and whether the object may depend on optimization variables. Typical roles include expression operand, constant parameter, dimension, axis, index set, cone, and Boolean option. A call satisfies the role contract only if every supplied argument belongs to its declared class and obeys its variability restriction. In particular, an argument used to choose dimensions, indices, or a representation branch must be constant unless the atom contract explicitly defines variable-dependent semantics and corresponding certification rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Argument roles say what kind of object each position accepts and whether that object may depend on optimization variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Argument Role Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and clearly separates object class from variability. No source establishes the proposed role taxonomy or the rule requiring branch-controlling arguments to be constant absent special certification semantics.

children.title: Argument Structure Contracts
children.top_down_role: Required dimensions, symmetry, definiteness, sparsity, integrality, plus value-space attributes.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) has ordered arguments \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\) satisfying its arity and role contracts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The call is structurally admissible exactly when \(Q_f(\tau(x_1),\ldots,\tau(x_k))\) holds.

notation.meaning: joint structural predicate for the atom

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Structural admissibility is a decidable predicate on certified argument descriptors.
No supplied locator directly specifies DCP argument-structure contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structure covers shape, symmetry, triangularity, sparsity pattern, and other non-value descriptors required by an atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each argument \(x_i\), let \(\tau(x_i)\) record its certified structural descriptors, such as scalar, vector, or matrix shape, symmetry, Hermitian structure, triangularity, diagonality, or fixed sparsity pattern. An argument structure contract is a decidable predicate \(Q_f\) on the tuple \((\tau(x_1),\ldots,\tau(x_k))\). The application \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) is structurally admissible if and only if this predicate holds. Coupled requirements, including equal dimensions, compatible matrix products, or matching block partitions, belong to \(Q_f\) rather than to independent per-argument declarations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An argument structure contract is the complete predicate governing shape and structural compatibility of all atom operands together.
knowledge_statements.title: Argument Structure Contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role is suitable and the joint predicate handles coupled structural requirements coherently. No cited source supports the selected descriptor scope or establishes this predicate as the complete structural admissibility contract.

children.title: Structural Contract Mismatches
children.top_down_role: Invalid arity, incompatible dimensions, unsupported broadcasting, plus absent structural declarations.

assumptions_latex: \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) is checked against declared arity, role, argument-structure, and output-shape contracts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If any structural predicate fails or the inferred output shape is not unique, the application has no valid atom certification.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Structural certification fails whenever a call violates signature predicates or lacks a uniquely determined output shape.
No supplied locator directly characterizes structural contract mismatches.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural rejection precedes curvature analysis and does not assert that a nearby reformulation is invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A structural contract mismatch occurs when an application \(f(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\) has \(k\notin A_f\), violates an argument role, fails \(Q_f(\tau(x_1),\ldots,\tau(x_k))\), or does not determine a unique value of \(\sigma_f(s_1,\ldots,s_k)\). It also occurs when the implementation's produced shape differs from the declared output shape. Any such mismatch invalidates the atom application before domain, sign, or curvature composition is considered. A compiler must reject the call or select a separately declared overload; it may not infer an undeclared broadcast, reshape, role conversion, or overload merely to obtain a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Wrong arity, roles, structures, or ambiguous output shape invalidate an atom call before DCP curvature analysis begins.
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Contract Mismatches

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits Structural Contract Mismatches, and the statement is internally consistent. The precedence of structural rejection, overload policy, and prohibition on implicit conversions are compiler-specific claims without an inspectable source.

children.title: Graph Recovery Contracts

children.title: Epigraph Graph Contracts
children.top_down_role: Canonical epigraph representations supplied for supported convex atoms.

assumptions_latex: \(f:D_f\subseteq\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper, closed, and convex.
The representation predicate \(G_f(x,t,z)\) is jointly convex-representable in its variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{epi} f=\{(x,t):\exists z\;G_f(x,t,z)\}\).

notation.meaning: auxiliary variables in the graph implementation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: A convex atom's epigraph graph implementation is exact when projection of its lifted feasible set equals the epigraph.
The supplied convex-algebraic-geometry locator is only indirectly relevant to DCP epigraph graph contracts.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is an exact lifted epigraph representation for a scalar convex atom, not merely a relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 5.4 An Algebraic View of Convex Hulls p. 224
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An epigraph graph contract for a scalar convex atom \(f\) specifies auxiliary variables \(z\) and a conjunction \(G_f(x,t,z)\) of trusted primitive convex constraints such that \[\operatorname{epi}f=\{(x,t)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R:\exists z\;G_f(x,t,z)\}.\] Exactness requires both directions: every feasible \((x,t,z)\) satisfies \(t\geq f(x)\), and for every \(x\in D_f\) and \(t\geq f(x)\), some \(z\) satisfies \(G_f(x,t,z)\). Thus replacing a constraint \(f(x)\leq t\) by \(\exists z\;G_f(x,t,z)\) preserves its feasible projection onto the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epigraph graph contract exactly represents a convex atom's upper-bound constraint as the projection of trusted primitive convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Epigraph Graph Contracts

source_witnesses.locator: 5.4 An Algebraic View of Convex Hulls p. 224

children.title: Hypograph Graph Contracts
children.top_down_role: Canonical hypograph representations supplied for supported concave atoms.

knowledge_statements.title: Hypograph Graph Contracts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact hypograph representation and recovery for an extended-real-valued concave atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be convex and let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\). Its hypograph is \[\operatorname{hypo}f=\{(x,t)\in D\times\mathbb{R}:t\leq f(x)\}.\] A set description \(H\subseteq D\times\mathbb{R}\) is an exact hypograph contract for \(f\) precisely when \((x,t)\in H\Longleftrightarrow t\leq f(x)\). Under this equivalence, \[f(x)=\sup\{t\in\mathbb{R}:(x,t)\in H\},\] with the supremum of the empty set defined as \(-\infty\). Moreover, \(f\) is concave exactly when \(H=\operatorname{hypo}f\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact hypograph contract represents every lower scalar bound on an atom, recovers the atom by a fiberwise supremum, and is convex exactly for concave atoms.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is convex.
\(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H=\operatorname{hypo}f\), \(f(x)=\sup\{t:(x,t)\in H\}\), and \(f\) is concave if and only if \(H\) is convex.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex-analysis definition and graph-recovery identity
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is mathematically standard, precise, and appropriate for the hypograph-contract leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

children.title: Conic Graph Contracts
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary variables, affine maps, cones, plus constraint blocks associated with atom reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Graph Contracts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted conic representation of an epigraph or hypograph relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be a closed convex cone. A graph relation \(G\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\) has a conic graph contract if there are fixed linear maps \(A,B\), vectors \(b,c\), and an auxiliary variable \(u\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[G=\{(x,t):\exists u,\ Ax+bt+Bu+c\in K\}.\] The contract is exact for a convex atom \(f\) when membership is equivalent to \(f(x)\leq t\), and exact for a concave atom when membership is equivalent to \(t\leq f(x)\). Eliminating \(u\) must therefore recover the intended graph inequality in both directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conic graph contract is an existential affine-cone lift whose projection equals, rather than merely contains, the intended epigraph or hypograph.
assumptions_latex: \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) is a closed convex cone.
\(A,B,b,c\) are fixed data of compatible dimensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G=\{(x,t):\exists u,\ Ax+bt+Bu+c\in K\}\) exactly represents the specified epigraph or hypograph relation.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The existential affine-cone lift and bidirectional exactness requirement fit the conic graph-contract leaf, but the record has no supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Inverse-Mapping Contracts

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Mapping Contracts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of a concave function from the vertical fibers of its graph relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\subseteq D\times\mathbb{R}\), where \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and define each vertical fiber by \(H_x=\{t:(x,t)\in H\}\). Suppose every fiber is either empty or has the form \(( -\infty,\alpha_x]\). Define \[f(x)=\sup H_x,\qquad \sup\varnothing=-\infty.\] Then \(H=\operatorname{hypo}f\); thus the fiberwise supremum is inverse to hypograph formation on this class of relations. If, in addition, \(D\) and \(H\) are convex, then the recovered function \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{-\infty\}\) is concave.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A downward-closed, upper-attaining vertical fiber uniquely determines its endpoint; taking those endpoints reverses hypograph construction and yields a concave function when the relation is convex.
assumptions_latex: \(H\subseteq D\times\mathbb{R}\).
Each fiber \(H_x\) is empty or equals \(( -\infty,\alpha_x]\).
For the concavity conclusion, \(D\) and \(H\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For \(f(x)=\sup H_x\), one has \(H=\operatorname{hypo}f\); convexity of \(H\) implies concavity of \(f\).

notation.meaning: vertical fiber of H above x

children.title: Representation Contract Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Contract Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness, domain, and closedness boundaries for lifted graph representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proposed lifted relation \(R=\{(x,t):\exists u,\Phi(x,t,u)\in K\}\) is an exact graph contract only if both implications between membership in \(R\) and the intended graph inequality hold on the declared domain. One implication alone gives only an inner or outer approximation. Closed lifted feasible sets do not guarantee a closed projection: \[C=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^2:x>0,\ y\geq 1/x\}\] is closed and convex, while its projection onto the first coordinate is \((0,\infty)\), which is not closed. Consequently, elimination, attainment, domain closure, and boundary values require separate certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-sided equivalence yields only an approximation, and projecting a closed convex lift can lose closedness; exactness and boundary attainment must be certified separately.
assumptions_latex: The intended graph inequality and its domain are specified.
\(K\) and \(\Phi\) define the proposed lifted relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact recovery requires bidirectional equivalence; closedness of the lifted feasible set alone does not ensure closedness or attainment after projection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: elementary projection counterexample and exactness criterion
