knowledge_statements.title: Exact Graph-to-Cone Conversion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural bound for explicit graph-template conversion and product-cone assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r_a\) is the explicit scalar-data size of the selected conic representation for graph constraint \(a\), then, with constant-time representation lookup and append operations, conversion and product-cone assembly require \[O\!\left(M+\sum_a r_a\right)\] time and emit \(O(\sum_a r_a)\) scalar data, where \(M\) is the number of input graph constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Graph-to-cone conversion is linear in the number of constraints plus the total explicit size of the selected conic templates.
assumptions_latex: Representation lookup and output append operations have constant amortized overhead.
\(r_a\) counts emitted variables, affine coefficients, offsets, and cone-dimension metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Conversion time is \(O(M+\sum_a r_a)\), and output size is \(O(\sum_a r_a)\).

notation.meaning: Explicit scalar-data size of the conic template selected for constraint a.

review_flags: Bound excludes registry construction, representation search, and later presolve.
knowledge_statements.title: Output-Sensitive Cone-Conversion Bound
Cone Representation Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of expanded graph constraints into affine cone-membership blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input affine graph constraints with registered conic representations. For each constraint \(G_a\), select a representation consisting of auxiliary variables \(z_a\), an affine map \(L_a\), and a product cone \(K_a\) such that \[G_a(v,t,w)\iff \exists z_a:\ L_a(v,t,w,z_a)+d_a\in K_a.\] Append this membership block, record its cone type and dimensions, and retain the projection map. Output stacked affine-conic data and reject any constraint lacking an exact representation in the permitted target cone families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone conversion replaces every expanded graph constraint by an equivalent existential affine membership in supported canonical cones.
assumptions_latex: Each accepted graph constraint has a registered exact conic representation.
All representation dimensions are finite and shape-consistent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_a(v,t,w)\iff \exists z_a:\ L_a(v,t,w,z_a)+d_a\in K_a\) for every converted atom.

notation.meaning: affine map for the conic representation of atom a
product cone used for atom a

review_flags: The representation registry and permitted target families require a system-specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Cone Representation Conversion, and the existential affine-cone template is coherent. The claims about registered exact representations, permitted target families, retained projection maps, and rejection behavior require a system-specific source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Expansion Composition
children.top_down_role: Composition of nested atom representations across an expression graph.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order independence of composing exact relational expansions on a finite expression DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_a\) be exact lifted relations assigned to the nodes of a finite acyclic expression graph. After variables on common edges are identified, any topological expansion order and any parenthesization produce the same conjunction \(G=\bigwedge_aG_a\), up to renaming and reordering auxiliary coordinates. Consequently, their projections onto the root and source coordinates are equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact relational expansions of an acyclic expression graph are invariant under topological expansion order and parenthesization, apart from auxiliary-coordinate naming and ordering.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
All local lifted relations are exact.
Variables representing the same graph edge are identified consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}G^{(1)}=\operatorname{proj}_{x,t}G^{(2)}\) for any two valid topological expansion orders.

notation.meaning: Exact lifted relation for graph node a.
Global relations assembled in two valid orders.

knowledge_statements.title: Parenthesization and Expansion-Order Invariance
Expansion Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of recursively composed exact atom expansions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an expression graph be acyclic, and suppose every replaced atom relation \(R_a(v_a,t_a)\) has an exact lifted formulation \[R_a(v_a,t_a)\iff \exists w_a:\ G_a(v_a,t_a,w_a).\] Form the global expansion by identifying variables on graph edges and conjoining all \(G_a\). Then existential elimination of all auxiliary variables yields the original root relation: \[R_{\mathrm{root}}(x,t)\iff \exists (t_a)_{a\ne\mathrm{root}},(w_a)_a:\ \bigwedge_a G_a(v_a,t_a,w_a).\] Thus exact local expansions compose exactly, including when shared subexpressions use one common output variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact local graph expansions compose into an exact global lifted formulation when edge variables are identified consistently.
assumptions_latex: The expression graph is finite and acyclic.
Every local atom expansion is exact.
Shared subexpressions use consistent common variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{\mathrm{root}}(x,t)\iff \exists (t_a)_{a\ne\mathrm{root}},(w_a)_a:\bigwedge_aG_a(v_a,t_a,w_a)\).

notation.meaning: exact lifted relation for atom a

review_flags: A formal source for compositional graph canonicalization is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property content kind fits Expansion Composition, and the local-to-global exactness claim is plausible under the stated finite-DAG and variable-identification assumptions. A formal source is still required to support the precise compositional claim, especially for shared subexpressions and the quantification of intermediate outputs.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Failure of Composition Under Inconsistent Sharing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed boundary based on duplicating a shared subexpression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two consumers of one shared subexpression are assigned independent output variables \(y_1,y_2\). If the expansion omits \(y_1=y_2\), its projected relation can strictly contain the relation obtained with one common output. For example, the shared relation \(y=x\), followed by constraints \(y_1\ge0\) and \(y_2\le-1\), is claimed to become feasible when the copies are unlinked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed example claims that duplicating a shared output without identification can destroy exactness.
assumptions_latex: The duplicated local expansions are intended to remain exact representations of the shared relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_xG_{\mathrm{consistent}}\subsetneq\operatorname{proj}_xG_{\mathrm{unlinked}}\) is claimed.
review_flags: DEFER_INCORRECT_COUNTEREXAMPLE: Exact copies of the stated relation impose y_1=x and y_2=x, so the downstream constraints remain infeasible; omitting only y_1=y_2 does not produce the claimed relaxation.
For deterministic expression nodes, separately exact copies already have equal outputs at a common input.
knowledge_statements.title: Failure of Composition Under Inconsistent Sharing

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is exact existential composition and invariance under valid topological order and parenthesization. The proposed inconsistent-sharing example was deferred because exact copies of y=x still force equal outputs. Individual atom expansion, cone conversion, and unsupported-conversion policy were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Unsupported Conversion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where expanded structures lack a compatible target-cone representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unsupportedness relative to the allowed cone family and exact-conversion registry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For classes of admissible cone lifts \(\mathcal K_1\subseteq\mathcal K_2\), every exact lift allowed under \(\mathcal K_1\) is also allowed under \(\mathcal K_2\). Hence nonexistence over \(\mathcal K_2\) implies nonexistence over \(\mathcal K_1\), whereas nonexistence over \(\mathcal K_1\) need not imply nonexistence over \(\mathcal K_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unsupportedness is relative to the allowed target cones and exact conversions; enlarging the admissible family can restore support.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal K_1\subseteq\mathcal K_2\) are classes of admissible finite-dimensional cone lifts.
Both comparisons use the same source relation and exactness criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathcal K_1}(R)\subseteq\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathcal K_2}(R)\).

notation.meaning: Exact lifts of relation R admitted by family K.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Family Relative Unsupportedness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary convexity condition for an exact affine lift over convex cones.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be a convex cone and \(S=\{x:\exists z,\ L(x,z)+d\in K\}\), where \(L\) is affine. Then \(S\) is convex. Consequently, a nonconvex source set cannot possess an exact finite-dimensional lift of this form over convex cones, although a selected convex branch or an explicitly declared relaxation may be representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projection of an affine convex-cone constraint is convex, so a nonconvex source set has no exact lift of that form.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a convex cone.
\(L\) is affine in source and auxiliary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\text{ nonconvex}\Longrightarrow\nexists(K,L,d):\ S=\{x:\exists z,\ L(x,z)+d\in K\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convexity Obstruction to Convex-Conic Conversion
Unsupported Conversion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure conditions for exact atom-to-cone conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact conversion must fail or return unsupported when some normalized atom-context pair has no registered representation over the allowed target cones, when a required parameter violates a representation domain, or when the selected solver cannot accept a required cone block and no exact permitted conversion exists. The canonicalizer must not silently replace the relation by a strict relaxation or approximation. Formally, if no finite lift \(L(x,z)+d\in K\), with allowed product cone \(K\), satisfies \[R(x)\iff \exists z:\ L(x,z)+d\in K,\] then exact canonicalization into that target family is unsupported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conversion is unsupported when no registered exact finite conic lift exists; an approximation must not be silently presented as equivalent.
assumptions_latex: Only exact finite-dimensional lifts over the allowed target cone family are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists(L,d,K):\ R(x)\iff\exists z,\ L(x,z)+d\in K\ \Longrightarrow\ \text{exact conversion is unsupported}.\)
review_flags: Failure behavior and approximation policy require authoritative canonicalizer documentation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary content kind is the correct role for Unsupported Conversion Boundaries. The policy against silent approximation and the registered-representation failure cases are implementation-dependent, while the formal nonexistence notation does not explicitly specify the admissible domains of L, d, and K. An authoritative canonicalizer specification is needed before fixing the exact statement.

children.title: Canonical Target Assembly Interface
children.top_down_role: Selection of a compatible solver form and construction of its data.

children.title: Canonical Target Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection among solver-compatible canonical form families.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between candidate filtering and preference ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\rho\) be any ranking criterion. If every candidate in \(\mathcal T\) fails the required exactness conditions, then minimizing \(\rho\) over \(\mathcal T\) cannot produce an exact target. An exact selection procedure must return unsupported rather than choose an inexact candidate, unless approximation is explicitly requested as a different task.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A ranking rule cannot turn an inexact representation into an admissible exact target.
assumptions_latex: Canonicalization is required to be exact.
Approximation has not been requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal T_{\mathrm{admissible}}=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\text{no exact target may be selected}.
knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Cannot Restore Exactness
Canonical Target Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection among exact canonical forms before numerical data assembly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input the expanded problem, its admissible exact cone representations, and a solver-capability set \(\mathcal S\). Enumerate target candidates whose cone blocks are supported directly or through registered exact conversions. Discard candidates that fail domain, dimension, or projection-equivalence checks. Rank the remainder by a fixed policy, such as minimizing unsupported cones first and then estimated auxiliary variables and cone dimensions. Output the highest-ranked target together with its representation choices and recovery maps; return unsupported if the admissible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target selection filters exact representations by solver compatibility and consistency, then chooses one using a fixed declared ranking policy.
assumptions_latex: The available representation alternatives are exact.
Solver capabilities \(\mathcal S\) and the ranking policy are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{T\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{admissible}}}\rho(T)\), or unsupported when \(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{admissible}}=\varnothing\).
review_flags: Target ranking policies vary across modeling systems and require a specific source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Canonical Target Selection. Enumeration, admissibility checks, ranking, tie handling, and recovery-map output are modeling-system policies rather than universal mathematical facts; no source defines the candidate set or ranking criterion used here.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed semantic consistency criterion for candidate targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A candidate target \(T\) is admissible for a source problem \(P\) when its lifted feasible set projects exactly to the feasible set of \(P\), its objective transformation preserves values, all representation-domain conditions hold, and recovery metadata are defined for every promised source output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A target is eligible only after feasibility, objective, domain, and recovery requirements hold.
assumptions_latex: The candidate declares its projection, objective transformation, domain conditions, and recovery promises.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T\in\mathcal T_{\mathrm{admissible}}\Longrightarrow\operatorname{proj}(\operatorname{feas}T)=\operatorname{feas}P.

notation.meaning: Candidates satisfying the proposed semantic checks.

review_flags: DEFER_MISPLACED: Exact projection, objective, domain, and recovery validation belongs primarily to the Assembly Consistency Checks sibling; selection should consume rather than redefine those predicates.
knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Canonical Target

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns enumeration of available exact targets, filtering, declared ranking, and the empty-candidate outcome. The proposed restatement of semantic admissibility was deferred to Assembly Consistency Checks. Matrix construction, validation, solver capability predicates, and individual LP/SOCP/SDP target definitions were excluded.

children.title: Canonical Data Assembly
children.top_down_role: Construction of solver-facing matrices, vectors, dimensions, and cone descriptors.

knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Data Assembly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block assembly of affine maps, cones, objectives, and recovery metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a selected target whose constraints are \(A_i u+b_i\in K_i\) and whose objective is \(c^{\mathsf T}u+d\). Assign nonoverlapping index ranges to variables and cone blocks, stack \(A_i\) and \(b_i\) in the same order, and form \(K=\prod_iK_i\). Emit \((A,b,c,d,K)\), parameter-update locations, and inverse maps. Before output, verify that every matrix dimension matches its indexed variables, every row belongs to exactly one cone coordinate, and every objective and constraint coefficient is assembled once with the declared sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Data assembly indexes variables and cone blocks, stacks affine coefficients, and emits solver data plus parameter and recovery metadata.
assumptions_latex: Each selected block has finite, shape-resolved affine data.
A deterministic variable and cone-block ordering is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Au+b\in\prod_iK_i\iff A_iu+b_i\in K_i\text{ for every assembled block }i\).
review_flags: Assembly layout and metadata requirements need an authoritative interface specification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Canonical Data Assembly, and the block-stacking equivalence is standard. The emitted tuple, index layout, parameter-update locations, inverse maps, sign convention, and validation requirements need an authoritative target-interface specification with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed formal identity for assembling primitive affine-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine maps \(r_i(u)=A_i u+b_i\) and cones \(K_i\), define \(A=\operatorname{vstack}(A_1,\ldots,A_q)\), \(b=(b_1,\ldots,b_q)\), and \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\). Then \(Au+b\in K\iff A_i u+b_i\in K_i\) for all \(i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stacking affine residuals and taking the product of their cones represents their conjunction.
assumptions_latex: All blocks act on the same indexed variable vector.
Every block dimension matches its cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Au+b\in\prod_iK_i\iff\bigwedge_i(A_i u+b_i\in K_i).
review_flags: DEFER_DUPLICATE: The immutable Canonical Data Assembly seed already states the same block-stacking equivalence and conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Product-Cone Block Stacking Identity

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory is deterministic indexing and construction of solver-facing matrices, vectors, cone descriptors, parameter locations, and recovery metadata. The proposed NEW stacking identity was deferred as duplicative of the immutable seed. Target choice, consistency checks, and solver compatibility were excluded as sibling scopes.

children.title: Solver-Capability Matching
children.top_down_role: Alignment of model requirements with available solver interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility under finite registered exact conversions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_0\) be the solver's directly supported descriptors and let registered exact conversions map one descriptor to finitely many descriptors. Define \(C^*\) as the least set containing \(C_0\) and containing any descriptor that has a registered exact conversion into descriptors already in \(C^*\). A finite target matches the solver exactly when every required descriptor lies in \(C^*\) and all global target restrictions hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatibility is membership in the closure of direct capabilities under finite registered exact conversions, together with global restrictions.
assumptions_latex: The target has finitely many descriptors.
Every admitted conversion is exact and produces finitely many descriptor blocks.
Numeric-type, integrality, and objective restrictions are checked separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{match}(\mathcal R,\mathcal S)\iff\mathcal R\subseteq C^*\text{ and all global restrictions hold}.

notation.meaning: Closure under registered finite exact conversions.

knowledge_statements.title: Direct and Converted Capability Closure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capability matching must include dimensions, parameters, and global restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Equality of cone-family labels is not sufficient for a direct solver match. A descriptor \((F,n,p)\) may fail because its dimension \(n\), parameter \(p\), numeric type, integrality feature, or objective form lies outside the solver's admitted subset, even when family \(F\) is nominally supported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support for a cone-family name does not imply support for every dimension, parameterization, data type, or associated feature.
assumptions_latex: Capabilities are predicates on complete descriptors and global target features.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\in\mathcal F_{\mathrm{solver}}\centernot\Longrightarrow(F,n,p)\in C_0.

notation.meaning: Cone family, dimension, and family-specific parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Family Labels Alone Are Insufficient
Solver-Capability Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility test between assembled cone requirements and solver features.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a canonical target require block descriptors \(\mathcal R=\{(F_i,n_i,p_i)\}_i\), recording cone family, dimension, and parameters, and let \(\mathcal S\) describe the solver's supported descriptors and restrictions. A direct match holds exactly when every required descriptor satisfies the corresponding support predicate and the objective, variable, and data types meet solver restrictions. An indirect match holds when each unmatched block has a registered exact conversion whose resulting descriptors all match \(\mathcal S\). Otherwise the solver is not capability-compatible with the target.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A solver matches a target when all cone blocks and data features are supported directly or through registered exact conversions.
assumptions_latex: Target requirements and solver capabilities use comparable cone descriptors.
Only registered exact conversions are admitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{match}(\mathcal R,\mathcal S)\iff\forall r\in\mathcal R,\ r\text{ is directly supported or exactly convertible to supported descriptors}.\)
review_flags: Capability descriptor semantics and solver restrictions require implementation-specific sources.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits Solver-Capability Matching. The descriptor schema, support predicates, data-type restrictions, and admissible conversion registry are implementation-specific, and no cited solver or modeling-system documentation establishes the stated biconditional.

children.title: Assembly Consistency Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural validation of assembled canonical data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural certificate that assembled residual coordinates form a well-defined target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(K=K_1\times\cdots\times K_q\), with \(\dim K_i=m_i\), structural consistency requires \(m=\sum_i m_i\) and a disjoint exhaustive ordered partition \(I_1\dot\cup\cdots\dot\cup I_q=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), where \(|I_i|=m_i\). Together with \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), these conditions certify that each residual and objective coefficient has a well-defined solver coordinate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible dimensions and a disjoint exhaustive row-to-cone partition certify that assembled data are structurally well typed.
assumptions_latex: The target is \(Au+b\in K\) with objective \(c^{\mathsf T}u+d\).
Each primitive cone block has a declared finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m=\sum_i m_i,\quad I_i\cap I_j=\varnothing\ (i\ne j),\quad\bigcup_iI_i=\{1,\ldots,m\},\quad c\in\mathbb R^n.

notation.meaning: Residual rows assigned to cone block i.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Partition and Dimension Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structural Checks Do Not Certify Semantic Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates well-typed canonical data from source-problem equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dimension, index-partition, and cone-descriptor checks are necessary for well-formed assembly but do not imply projection equivalence to the source model. For example, replacing the source constraint \(x\ge1\) by the dimensionally valid target constraint \(x\ge0\) passes structural checks while changing the feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Well-typed matrices and cone blocks do not by themselves prove equivalence to the source problem.
assumptions_latex: Structural validation checks only dimensions, indices, and descriptor compatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{structurallyValid}(Q)\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{feas}(P)=R(\operatorname{feas}(Q)).
knowledge_statements.title: Structural Checks Do Not Certify Semantic Equivalence

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the source problem and \(Q\) is its assembled canonical problem.
\(E\) maps every source-feasible point to a canonical-feasible point, and \(R\) maps every canonical-feasible point to a source-feasible point.
\(f_P(Rz)=\alpha f_Q(z)+\beta\) and \(f_Q(Ex)=\alpha^{-1}(f_P(x)-\beta)\), where \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{feas}(P)\neq\varnothing\iff\operatorname{feas}(Q)\neq\varnothing\), and whenever either optimum is attained, \(p_P^\star=\alpha p_Q^\star+\beta\). Moreover, the assembly is recovery-consistent precisely when \(R(Ex)=x\) for every source-feasible \(x\), up to an explicitly declared equivalence of source solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checks exact feasibility, objective, and recovery consistency of an assembled canonical target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An assembly of \(P\) into \(Q\) is consistent if its declared maps and objective transformation preserve feasibility and optimal values. Concretely, require \(E(\operatorname{feas}(P))\subseteq\operatorname{feas}(Q)\), \(R(\operatorname{feas}(Q))\subseteq\operatorname{feas}(P)\), and the displayed objective identities. If exact source recovery is promised, additionally require \(R\circ E\) to equal the identity on source-feasible points, modulo only the declared solution equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assembly is consistent when forward and recovery maps preserve feasibility, objective values transform as declared, and their composition recovers each source solution up to an explicit equivalence.
knowledge_statements.title: Assembly Consistency Checks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the assembly-consistency leaf and is mathematically coherent, but the canonicalization-specific feasibility, value, and recovery requirements have no inspectable citation.

children.title: Inverse Reduction Recovery Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Transport of solver outputs back to source-model objects.

children.title: Inverse Reduction Chains
children.top_down_role: Reverse mappings associated with composed forward reductions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stored inverse data must remain paired with the forward instance that created it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a recovery map has the form \(S_i(\cdot;d_i)\), chain recovery is justified only when \(d_i\) was produced by the same instantiated forward transformation at stage \(i\). Reusing metadata from a different parameterization or variable ordering does not inherit the local inverse identity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each recovery map must use metadata from its matching forward reduction instance.
assumptions_latex: Forward reductions may depend on instance-specific parameters, indices, scaling, or coordinate order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_i'\ne d_i\Longrightarrow S_i(\cdot;d_i')\circ T_i(\cdot;d_i)\text{ is not guaranteed to equal }\operatorname{id}.

notation.meaning: Instance-specific metadata created by forward stage i.

knowledge_statements.title: Metadata Provenance Invariant

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recovery Maps Generally Do Not Commute
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessity of reversing the actual forward-reduction order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Recovery maps cannot generally be reordered. For example, \(S_2(y)=2y\) and \(S_1(y)=y+1\) satisfy \(S_1(S_2(y))=2y+1\), whereas \(S_2(S_1(y))=2y+2\). Thus stage maps must be composed in the reverse of the actual forward order, not in an arbitrary order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery maps need not commute, so their order must reverse the forward-reduction order.
assumptions_latex: At least two stage recovery maps act noncommutatively on compatible result objects.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_1\circ S_2\ne S_2\circ S_1\text{ can occur}.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Maps Generally Do Not Commute

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compositional correctness when each local recovery map is correct.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_i:\mathcal R_{i-1}\to\mathcal R_i\) be forward transformations on admissible result objects and let \(S_i:\mathcal R_i\to\mathcal R_{i-1}\) satisfy \(S_i(T_i(r))=r\) for every admissible \(r\in\mathcal R_{i-1}\). Then \(S_1\circ\cdots\circ S_m\) is a left inverse of \(T_m\circ\cdots\circ T_1\) on admissible source results.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local left inverses composed in reverse order form a left inverse of the complete forward chain.
assumptions_latex: Each recovery map uses metadata from its corresponding forward instance.
Every intermediate object lies in the required domain.
\(S_i\circ T_i\) is the identity on admissible stage-i−1 results.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (S_1\circ\cdots\circ S_m)\circ(T_m\circ\cdots\circ T_1)=\operatorname{id}.

notation.meaning: Admissible result space at stage i.
Forward transformation and associated recovery map.

knowledge_statements.title: Correctness of Reverse-Order Recovery Composition

assumptions_latex: \(P_0\xrightarrow{T_1}P_1\xrightarrow{T_2}\cdots\xrightarrow{T_m}P_m\) is a sequence of reductions.
Each reduction stores recovery data \(d_i\) and supplies an inverse-result map \(S_i(\cdot;d_i)\).
A solver result \(r_m\) for \(P_m\) lies in the domain of every required inverse map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered source result is \(r_0=(S_1(\cdot;d_1)\circ S_2(\cdot;d_2)\circ\cdots\circ S_m(\cdot;d_m))(r_m)\), with the maps evaluated from \(S_m\) back through \(S_1\).

notation.meaning: Stored recovery data for reduction i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies reverse-order composition of result recovery maps for a reduction chain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the terminal result \(r_m\), initialize \(r\leftarrow r_m\). For \(i=m,m-1,\ldots,1\), verify that \(r\in\operatorname{dom}S_i(\cdot;d_i)\), then update \(r\leftarrow S_i(r;d_i)\). Output \(r_0=r\). The chain is well-defined only if each intermediate result belongs to the next inverse map's domain and the stored data correspond to the same forward reduction instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply each reduction's recovery map in reverse order, using its stored metadata, and stop with failure if an intermediate result is outside the next map's domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Reduction Chains

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reverse-order recovery algorithm and its notation are consistent, but no source supports this reduction-chain interface or its domain requirements.

children.title: Source Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Transport of canonical solver outputs to source-model objects.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates validation of a recovered source point from the reduction theorem used to transport optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After computing x=R_d(z), validate x directly against every source-domain and source-feasibility condition and verify the declared value relation f_P(x)=\phi(f_Q(z)). Passing these checks certifies that x is a value-consistent source-feasible recovery. Source optimality additionally requires a valid canonical optimality result and an optimizer-transport contract such as exact feasible-set coverage with an order-preserving objective map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Direct source feasibility and value checks certify a consistent recovered point; optimality also requires a valid canonical optimality result and a correct transport contract.
assumptions_latex: x=R_d(z)\text{ is defined}.
Source constraints, domains, and objective values can be evaluated.
The reduction declares an objective-value map \phi.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States sufficient exact feasibility and objective-correspondence conditions for transporting canonical optimizers to source optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F_Q and F_P be the canonical and source feasible sets. Suppose R_d(F_Q)=F_P and there is a strictly increasing function \phi such that f_P(R_d(z))=\phi(f_Q(z)) for every z\in F_Q. children.title: Auxiliary-Variable Elimination
children.top_down_role: Removal or interpretation of representation-specific variables during recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary-Variable Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses partial minimization to remove auxiliary variables while preserving the source optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Auxiliary-variable elimination represents the source problem by partial minimization of a lifted problem. For a feasible set \(F\subseteq X\times U\) and a real-valued objective \(g:F\to\mathbb{R}\), define \(f(x)=\inf\{g(x,u):(x,u)\in F\}\), with \(f(x)=+\infty\) when no such \(u\) exists. Then \(\operatorname{dom}f=\operatorname{proj}_X F\), and \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf_{(x,u)\in F}g(x,u)\). Every attained lifted minimizer \((x^\star,u^\star)\) projects to a source minimizer \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partially minimize the real-valued lifted objective over auxiliary variables. The projected feasible set is the effective domain of the resulting value function, the infimum is preserved, and any lifted minimizer projects to a source minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are the source and auxiliary variable spaces, and \(F\subseteq X\times U\) is the lifted feasible set.
\(g:F\to\mathbb{R}\) is real-valued at every lifted-feasible pair.
The source extended-value objective is \(f(x)=\inf\{g(x,u):(x,u)\in F\}\), with value \(+\infty\) if the feasible fiber is empty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dom}f=\operatorname{proj}_X F\) and \(\inf_{x\in X}f(x)=\inf_{(x,u)\in F}g(x,u)\). If \((x^\star,u^\star)\in F\) attains the lifted infimum, then \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition for equality between reduced optimizers and projections of lifted optimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=\inf\{g(x,u):(x,u)\in F\}\), assume the common global infimum is finite and every \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\) has a feasible \(u_x\) attaining its fiber infimum. Then \[\operatorname*{argmin}_x f(x)=\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x,u)\in F}g(x,u).\] Without fiber attainment, only projection of an existing lifted optimizer into the reduced optimizer set is guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer sets correspond exactly when each reduced optimizer has an auxiliary witness attaining its fiber infimum.
assumptions_latex: The common global infimum is finite.
Every reduced minimizer has a feasible auxiliary witness attaining its fiber infimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}f=\operatorname{proj}_X\operatorname*{argmin}_{F}g.

The projected domain is \(x>0\), and \(f(x)=\inf\{u:(x,u)\in F\}=0\) for every \(x>0\), but no feasible \(u\) attains this infimum. Thus reduced minimizers need not lift to joint minimizers, and the projected effective domain need not be closed.

If \(f(x)>-\infty\) for every \(x\), then \(f\) is convex. Fiber attainment is not required for convexity, but additional assumptions are needed for lower semicontinuity, closed epigraph, or recovery of an attaining auxiliary point.

\(f(x)>-\infty\) for every x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers failure when the retained solver output is outside the recovery map's domain or contains no recoverable primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let R_d:D_d\to X be the recovery map determined by stored data d. A source solution can be returned only when the solver output contains a canonical primal point z\in D_d. If z\notin D_d, an inverse stage is undefined, or the solver returns only a status or certificate without such a point, then R_d(z) is unavailable; a recovery procedure must report that boundary rather than fabricate a source solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recovery fails when the solver supplies no canonical primal point accepted by every inverse stage, or when that point lies outside the stored recovery map's domain.
assumptions_latex: R_d:D_d\to X is a partial recovery map determined by retained reduction data d.
The requested output is a source-level primal solution.

Domain on which the recovery map is defined.

assumptions_latex: A reduction records only a canonical result \(z\) and discards recovery metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies information loss as a sharp obstruction to unique source-result recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact deterministic recovery fails whenever the retained canonical output does not distinguish source results that must be returned differently. In particular, if \(x_1\neq x_2\) are both compatible with the same retained result \(z\), then a single-valued map \(R\) cannot recover both because \(R(z)\) has only one value. knowledge_statements.title: Primal Variable Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers coordinate recovery when source variables are explicitly embedded in an exact canonical lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: When an exact canonical lifting retains the source variable as a coordinate block, primal recovery is coordinate projection. Let the canonical feasible set be \(F_Q\subseteq X\times U\), let the source feasible set satisfy \(F_P=\operatorname{proj}_X F_Q\), and suppose \(f_P(x)=\alpha f_Q(x,u)+\beta\) for every \((x,u)\in F_Q\), where \(\alpha>0\). Define \(R(x,u)=x\). Then \(R\) sends canonical-feasible points to source-feasible points and sends every attained canonical minimizer to a source minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an exact lifting that covers the entire source feasible set and preserves objective order, recover source variables by projecting the canonical variable onto its source-coordinate block.
assumptions_latex: The canonical primal variable is \(z=(x,u)\in X\times U\), with canonical feasible set \(F_Q\subseteq X\times U\).
The source feasible set is exactly \(F_P=\operatorname{proj}_X F_Q\).
For every \((x,u)\in F_Q\), the objectives satisfy \(f_P(x)=\alpha f_Q(x,u)+\beta\), where \(\alpha>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovery map \(R:X\times U\to X\) defined by \(R(x,u)=x\) sends every point of \(F_Q\) into \(F_P\). If \((x^\star,u^\star)\) minimizes \(f_Q\) over \(F_Q\), then \(x^\star\) minimizes \(f_P\) over \(F_P\).

notation.meaning: Positive objective scale and additive offset.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Recovery Through Composed Inverse Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: End-to-end recovery through substitutions, coordinate transformations, and projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\to\cdots\to P_m\) be a recorded reduction chain. If each inverse result map \(R_i\) is defined on the returned result, maps relevant feasible results of \(P_i\) to feasible results of \(P_{i-1}\), and maps attained optimizers to attained optimizers, then \[R=R_1\circ R_2\circ\cdots\circ R_m\] recovers a source-feasible point and maps every attained final optimizer to a source optimizer. The maps are applied in reverse canonicalization order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply every stored inverse reduction in reverse order; end-to-end recovery is valid when each step is defined and preserves feasibility and attained optimality.
assumptions_latex: A finite reduction chain \(P_0\to\cdots\to P_m\) is recorded.
Each inverse map \(R_i\) is defined on the returned result and preserves feasibility.
Each \(R_i\) maps attained optimizers to attained optimizers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R=R_1\circ\cdots\circ R_m,\qquad z_m^\star\mapsto R(z_m^\star)=z_0^\star.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sense Reversal and Degenerate Objective Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value transport for negative scaling and the failure of recovery under zero scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f_P(Rz)=\alpha f_Q(z)+\beta\) on corresponding feasible points. If \(\alpha<0\), the value relation remains \(v_P=\alpha v_Q+\beta\), but source minimization corresponds to canonical maximization and conversely. If \(\alpha=0\), canonical objective values contain no information about variation in \(f_P\); absent an additional independent relation, neither source values nor optimizer order can be recovered from \(v_Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative scaling requires reversing optimization sense; zero scaling destroys objective-value and optimizer-order recovery unless other metadata supplies the missing information.
assumptions_latex: The displayed affine objective relation holds on corresponding feasible points.
The canonicalization metadata records the scale, offset, and optimization sense.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\alpha<0\Rightarrow v_P=\alpha v_Q+\beta\text{ with sense reversal};\qquad\alpha=0\Rightarrow v_Q\text{ does not determine }v_P.\]
knowledge_statements.title: Sense Reversal and Degenerate Objective Scaling

assumptions_latex: Canonicalization relates objectives by \(f_P(Rz)=\alpha f_Q(z)+\beta\) on canonical-feasible points.
The scaling satisfies \(\alpha>0\).
The canonical solver reports an objective value \(v_Q\) consistent with its returned result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered source objective value is \(v_P=\alpha v_Q+\beta\). In particular, \(p_P^\star=\alpha p_Q^\star+\beta\) whenever the two problems have corresponding optimal solutions.

notation.meaning: Reported canonical and recovered source values.

For a canonical result reporting \(v_Q=f_Q(z)\), compute \(v_P=\alpha v_Q+\beta\). Positivity of \(\alpha\) preserves minimizers and order, so the same formula transports finite optimal values. assumptions_latex: The lifted feasible set is \(F\subseteq X\times U\).
The source feasible set is exactly \(C=\{x\in X:\exists u\in U,\ (x,u)\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\operatorname{proj}_X F\). Thus every lifted-feasible pair \((x,u)\) recovers the source-feasible point \(x\), and every \(x\in C\) has at least one lifted witness \(u\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lifted variable projection eliminates auxiliary coordinates existentially. For \(F\subseteq X\times U\), define \(\operatorname{proj}_X F=\{x\in X:\exists u\in U,\ (x,u)\in F\}\). An exact lifted representation of a source feasible set \(C\subseteq X\) satisfies \(C=\operatorname{proj}_X F\). Consequently, projection never creates a source-infeasible point, and every source-feasible point possesses at least one lifted feasible witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The source feasible set is recovered by projecting away auxiliary coordinates; exactness requires both feasibility preservation and a lifted witness for every source point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Topological boundary for existential elimination of auxiliary variables.

Thus finite-dimensional projection preserves convexity but need not preserve closedness, and a point in the closure of a projection need not possess a lifted witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex lifted set can have a nonclosed projection, so closure and boundary-witness claims require extra assumptions.

children.title: Partial Primal Recovery

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact safe output when available canonical data do not uniquely determine requested source coordinates.

The exact recoverable information is \[\mathcal R_J(z_I)=\{R_J(z):z\in\mathcal Z(z_I)\}.\] Point-valued recovery is valid exactly when \(\mathcal R_J(z_I)\) is a singleton. An empty compatible set indicates inconsistent data; a nonsingleton image permits only the set or a certified enclosure, not a uniquely recovered point.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Z(z_I)\) contains every full canonical result compatible with the available data.
\(R_J\) is the declared recovery map for the requested source coordinates.

assumptions_latex: A canonical result provides values only for coordinates indexed by \(I\).
The requested source coordinates indexed by \(J\) satisfy \(J\subseteq I\), or are determined by a stored map \(R_J\) on the available data.
No claim is made about source coordinates outside \(J\).

children.title: Dual Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of dual values associated with source constraints.

assumptions_latex: A source constraint residual \(g(x)\in Y\) is represented canonically as \(A g(x)\in K\), where \(A:Y\to Z\) is linear.
The cone representation is exact: \(g(x)\in C\iff A g(x)\in K\).
A canonical dual vector \(y\in K^*\) is available and the adopted Lagrangian sign convention is fixed.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dual recovery pulls canonical multipliers back through the adjoint of the constraint representation. If the canonical residual is \(Ag(x)\) and its multiplier is \(y\), define \(\lambda=A^*y\). Then \(\langle y,Ag(x)\rangle=\langle A^*y,g(x)\rangle=\langle\lambda,g(x)\rangle\), so the canonical Lagrangian contribution equals the source contribution. Membership of \(\lambda\) in the appropriate source dual cone must be checked under the fixed sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pull a canonical constraint multiplier back through the adjoint representation map, then verify source-cone membership and the adopted Lagrangian sign convention.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Composed Dual Pullback Through a Reduction Chain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse-order adjoint recovery through recorded linear constraint transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a source residual is transformed successively by linear maps \(A_i:Y_{i-1}\to Y_i\), then a final multiplier \(y_m\in Y_m^*\) is recovered recursively by \(y_{i-1}=A_i^*y_i\). Hence \[\lambda=y_0=A_1^*A_2^*\cdots A_m^*y_m=(A_m\cdots A_1)^*y_m.\] Each step must restore its recorded sign, scaling, block ordering, pairing, and cone convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply the adjoints of the recorded reduction maps in reverse order, restoring every convention at its corresponding step.
assumptions_latex: Every constraint transformation has a recorded linear map \(A_i\).
A final canonical multiplier \(y_m\) is available.
The sign, scaling, ordering, pairing, and cone conventions of every step are recorded.

children.title: Solver Status Transport

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Composition of status implications through multiple reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed mathematical status \(s\), suppose each reduction \(P_{i-1}\to P_i\) establishes \(S_i(s)\Rightarrow S_{i-1}(s)\). Then \(S_k(s)\Rightarrow S_0(s)\). Bidirectional equivalence is inherited only when every link establishes both implications; one one-way or unavailable link prevents bidirectional transport for that status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Status implications compose, while exact equivalence requires equivalence at every reduction step.
assumptions_latex: \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\quad S_i(s)\Rightarrow S_{i-1}(s).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_k(s)\Rightarrow S_0(s).

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Status Transport

assumptions_latex: The reduction establishes exact feasibility and recession correspondence between source problem \(P\) and canonical problem \(Q\).
The solver status is mathematically certified rather than merely heuristic or tolerance-limited.
Objective scaling is positive and all recovery maps required by the status are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\) being optimal, infeasible, or unbounded transports respectively to \(P\) being optimal, infeasible, or unbounded, with the optimal value transformed as declared. Without the corresponding exact equivalence, the transported status must be weakened to indeterminate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transports only mathematically justified statuses across an exact reduction correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solver status transport is valid only to the extent established by the reduction. Exact feasible-set and objective correspondence transports an attained optimal status from \(Q\) to \(P\). Equivalence of feasibility transports infeasibility in both directions. Preservation and recovery of improving recession directions transport unboundedness. If the solver reports an ambiguous, inaccurate, or tolerance-dependent status, or if the required correspondence is absent, no stronger source status may be asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transport optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness only when the reduction preserves the corresponding mathematical property; ambiguous or tolerance-based statuses remain weak.

children.title: Certificate Transport

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate transport through a sequence of verified reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose reductions \(P_0\to P_1\to\cdots\to P_k\) provide maps \(T_i:C_i\to C_{i-1}\) satisfying \(V_i(c;P_i)\Rightarrow V_{i-1}(T_i c;P_{i-1})\). Then \(T=T_1\circ\cdots\circ T_k\) satisfies \(V_k(c;P_k)\Rightarrow V_0(Tc;P_0)\). A terminal certificate can therefore be pulled back by applying the stored maps in reverse reduction order and then evaluating the source verifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified certificate transports compose through a reduction chain.
assumptions_latex: \forall i\in\{1,\ldots,k\},\quad V_i(c;P_i)\Rightarrow V_{i-1}(T_i c;P_{i-1}).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_k(c;P_k)\Rightarrow V_0((T_1\circ\cdots\circ T_k)c;P_0).

notation.meaning: Problem after the first i reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Certificate Transport

assumptions_latex: A canonical certificate \(c_Q\) satisfies a verifiable predicate \(V_Q(c_Q;Q)=\mathrm{true}\).
A stored map \(T\) converts canonical certificates to source objects.
The reduction proves \(V_Q(c_Q;Q)\Rightarrow V_P(Tc_Q;P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The object \(c_P=Tc_Q\) is a source certificate because its source predicate satisfies \(V_P(c_P;P)=\mathrm{true}\). If \(T\) or the implication is unavailable, the canonical certificate does not by itself certify the source claim.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines certificate transport through an explicit map and a verifiable predicate implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A canonical certificate is transportable when the reduction supplies a map \(T\) and establishes the verifier implication \(V_Q(c_Q;Q)=\mathrm{true}\Rightarrow V_P(Tc_Q;P)=\mathrm{true}\). Given \(c_Q\), compute \(c_P=Tc_Q\) and evaluate the source predicate \(V_P(c_P;P)\). Accept the source claim only when that predicate succeeds. This covers optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness certificates according to the predicates explicitly attached to the reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map the canonical certificate to a source object and run the source verifier; accept it only when the reduction proves the verifier implication.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Transport

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The verifier-implication formulation fits certificate transport and avoids overclaiming, but no inspectable source supports this reduction-level certificate interface.

children.title: Status Translation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Mappings between solver-specific statuses and source-model statuses.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy Cannot Be Upgraded by Translation Alone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between exact and tolerance-qualified status translation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V_C^{\mathrm{app}}(w)\) be a tolerance-qualified canonical witness predicate and \(V_P^{\mathrm{ex}}(Tw)\) the exact source predicate. An exact source status follows only if the reduction proves \(V_C^{\mathrm{app}}(w)\Rightarrow V_P^{\mathrm{ex}}(Tw)\). Without that implication, translation may preserve or weaken the accuracy label but cannot upgrade it to exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate canonical status cannot become exact merely through inverse-canonicalization relabeling.
assumptions_latex: V_C^{\mathrm{app}}(w)\text{ is weaker than exact canonical validity.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: V_C^{\mathrm{app}}(w)\not\Rightarrow V_P^{\mathrm{ex}}(Tw)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{no exact source status is justified}.
knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy Cannot Be Upgraded by Translation Alone

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical classification of source-status validity induced by canonical evidence and status-specific witness transport.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Sigma\) be a set of statuses. For each \(s\in\Sigma\), let \(W_{C,s}\) and \(W_{P,s}\) be canonical and source evidence spaces, and let \(Q_{C,s}\) and \(Q_{P,s}\) be validity predicates on those spaces. Define \(S_C(s)\iff\exists w\in W_{C,s}:Q_{C,s}(w)\) and \(S_P(s)\iff\exists u\in W_{P,s}:Q_{P,s}(u)\). Translation of \(s\) is exact when both implications \(S_C(s)\Rightarrow S_P(s)\) and \(S_P(s)\Rightarrow S_C(s)\) are established. It is conservative from canonical to source when the forward implication is established but the reverse implication is not. It is indeterminate when the forward implication required to report the source status is not established or required transport data are unavailable. A witness-level realization of the forward implication is a map \(T_s:W_{C,s}\to W_{P,s}\) satisfying \(Q_{C,s}(w)\Rightarrow Q_{P,s}(T_sw)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A status translates exactly when validity is established in both directions, conservatively when only canonical-to-source validity is established, and indeterminately when that forward implication or its required transport is unavailable.
assumptions_latex: \(W_{C,s}\) and \(W_{P,s}\) are specified for every \(s\in\Sigma\).
\(Q_{C,s}\) and \(Q_{P,s}\) are predicates on their stated evidence spaces.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{exact}:S_C(s)\Leftrightarrow S_P(s);\quad \mathrm{conservative}:S_C(s)\Rightarrow S_P(s)\text{ only};\quad \mathrm{indeterminate}:S_C(s)\Rightarrow S_P(s)\text{ is unestablished or required transport data are unavailable}.\)

notation.meaning: Canonical and source existential status-validity propositions.
Status-specific map from canonical evidence to source evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Typed Status Translation Regimes

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is an original convex model and \(C(P)\) is its canonical conic reformulation.
\(R\) maps canonical primal solutions to original variables, and \(T\) maps canonical certificates to candidate original certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{exact}\), \(\text{conservative}\), and \(\text{indeterminate}\) are distinguished by equivalence, one-way implication, and absence of a proved implication, respectively.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: status transport is classified by logical implications between original and canonical validity predicates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies deterministic status translation for an exact or relaxed canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each status \(s\), let \(V_P(s)\) and \(V_C(s)\) denote its validity for \(P\) and \(C(P)\). Translation is exact when \(V_C(s)\iff V_P(s)\), with recovered witnesses satisfying \(R(z)\in P\) or transported certificates satisfying \(V_P(Ty)\). It is conservative when only \(V_C(s)\Rightarrow V_P(s)\) is established. It is indeterminate when neither implication is established or when required recovery data are unavailable. A solver label may be reported as an original-model status only in the exact or applicable conservative regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A canonical solver status transfers exactly under equivalence, conservatively under a proved one-way implication, and otherwise remains indeterminate.
knowledge_statements.title: Status Translation Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation is supplied. Moreover, V_P is introduced as a status-validity predicate but is later applied to Ty, while z, y, and the relevant feasible or certificate sets are not defined. An authoritative source and a typed formulation are required.

children.title: Certificate Loss Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reduction or solver regimes where source-level certificates cannot be recovered.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that ambient noninjectivity alone is not a certificate-loss criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(T(a,b)=a\), let \(\mathcal V_C=\{(a,0):a>0\}\), and let \(\mathcal V_P=(0,\infty)\). Then \(\ker T=\{0\}\times\mathbb R\neq\{0\}\), while \(T(\mathcal V_C)=\mathcal V_P\) and the restriction \(T|_{\mathcal V_C}\) is injective. Thus an ambient nullspace does not itself imply certificate loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transport map can have a nontrivial kernel while preserving every valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker T\neq\{0\},\qquad T(\mathcal V_C)=\mathcal V_P.

notation.meaning: Valid canonical and source certificate sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Noninjectivity Without Certificate Loss

assumptions_latex: \(T:Y_C\to Y_P\) is the certificate-transport map for a canonicalization.
\(\mathcal V_C\subseteq Y_C\) and \(\mathcal V_P\subseteq Y_P\) are the valid canonical and original certificate sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal V_C\cap T^{-1}(Y_P\setminus\mathcal V_P)\neq\varnothing\) is precisely a certificate-transport failure, while \(\mathcal V_C\cap\ker T\neq\varnothing\) identifies complete information loss.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: loss is characterized by failure of certificate validity under the prescribed transport map
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates transport failure from mere nonuniqueness of canonical certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Certificate transport is valid exactly when \(T(\mathcal V_C)\subseteq\mathcal V_P\). Loss occurs if some \(y\in\mathcal V_C\) satisfies \(Ty\notin\mathcal V_P\); complete loss occurs when additionally \(Ty=0\) and zero is not a valid original certificate. Typical boundaries are noninjective elimination of auxiliary multipliers, aggregation without retained disaggregation data, and approximate canonicalization whose residual error exceeds the original certificate tolerance. Beyond these boundaries, canonical infeasibility or unboundedness must not be asserted for the original model solely from \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate information is lost when a valid canonical certificate maps to an invalid or vacuous original certificate, including through eliminated multipliers or aggregation.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Loss Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the transport criterion or listed failure mechanisms. The conclusion also calls membership in ker T complete loss without assuming that zero is invalid or vacuous in the original certificate system.

children.title: Representation-Dependent Dual Semantics
children.top_down_role: Interpretive boundaries caused by lifts and nonunique reformulations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Multiplier Equivalence Classes Under a Noninjective Pullback
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation-invariant semantics in the presence of redundant canonical dual coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear representation map \(A:Y\to Z\), canonical multipliers \(y_1,y_2\in Z^*\) induce the same source multiplier exactly when \[A^*y_1=A^*y_2\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad y_1-y_2\in\ker A^*.\] If both representatives satisfy the applicable canonical dual constraints, their common source semantics is the pullback \(\lambda=A^*y_i\). Thus the intrinsic object is the pullback, equivalently the admissible representative class modulo \(\ker A^*\), rather than an arbitrary canonical representative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two admissible canonical multipliers have identical source meaning exactly when their difference lies in the kernel of the adjoint pullback.
assumptions_latex: The source constraint representation uses a linear map \(A:Y\to Z\).
Canonical multipliers are interpreted through \(A^*:Z^*\to Y^*\).
Every compared representative satisfies the applicable canonical dual constraints.

notation.meaning: Adjoint map from canonical to source dual coordinates.
Canonical dual directions invisible at source level.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Equivalence Classes Under a Noninjective Pullback

assumptions_latex: \(h(x)=0\) is an original equality system.
\(S\) is invertible, so \(h(x)=0\) and \(Sh(x)=0\) define the same primal feasible set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda=S^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\lambda\), so multiplier coordinates depend on the chosen representation although \(Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) is invariant.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: covariance of equality multipliers under an invertible constraint reparameterization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses invertible equality reparameterization as the minimal representation-dependence mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda\) multiply \(h(x)=0\), and let \(\widetilde\lambda\) multiply the equivalent system \(Sh(x)=0\). Equality of their Lagrangian linear terms requires \(\lambda=S^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\lambda\). Thus numerical multiplier coordinates are not intrinsic to the primal feasible set. The representation-independent first-order contribution is \(Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}\lambda=Dh(x)^{\mathsf T}S^{\mathsf T}\widetilde\lambda\). For noninvertible lifts or redundant constraints, multipliers may also be nonunique, and only a specified pullback or aggregated dual quantity has original-model semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent constraint representations can produce rescaled or nonunique dual multipliers; only their specified pullback to original variables is representation independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Dependent Dual Semantics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplier transformation is mathematically standard and fits the representation-dependent dual-semantics container, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Canonical Variable Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in solver-facing variables introduced by a representation.

assumptions_latex: An original model has \(n\) scalar decision-variable coordinates.
Its canonical representation has \(n_c\) scalar variable coordinates, including auxiliaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta n=n_c-n\) and \(g_n=n_c/n\) for \(n>0\).

notation.meaning: original and canonical scalar variable counts

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalar coordinate counts give representation-independent bookkeeping once the canonical variable convention is fixed
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts scalar coordinates, not symbolic variable objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonical variable growth is measured additively by \(\Delta n:=n_c-n\) and, when \(n>0\), multiplicatively by \(g_n:=n_c/n\). For a model family indexed by size \(N\), a bound \(n_c(N)\le n(N)+a(N)\) certifies auxiliary growth at most \(a(N)\); equivalently, \(\Delta n(N)\le a(N)\). Counts must expand matrix and vector variables into scalar coordinates and must use the same treatment of fixed or eliminated variables in both representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical variable growth is the increase or ratio of scalar variable coordinates after expanding structured variables under a fixed counting convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Variable Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The formulas are bookkeeping definitions rather than a specific complexity bound. A source is required, and the record should normally use content_kind definition unless it asserts a substantive family bound.

children.title: Canonical Constraint Growth
children.top_down_role: Growth in solver-facing constraints introduced by a representation.

assumptions_latex: An original model has \(m\) scalar affine constraint rows.
Its canonical representation has \(m_c\) scalar affine rows under the same row-counting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta m=m_c-m\) and \(g_m=m_c/m\) for \(m>0\).

notation.meaning: original and canonical scalar row counts

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: scalar row counts give unambiguous growth after fixing treatment of cone membership
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts scalar affine rows separately from cone blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonical constraint growth is \(\Delta m:=m_c-m\) and, for \(m>0\), \(g_m:=m_c/m\). For a family indexed by \(N\), the resource bound \(m_c(N)\le m(N)+r(N)\) is equivalent to \(\Delta m(N)\le r(N)\). Equality rows, inequality rows, and affine maps feeding cones must be counted consistently. Cone-membership blocks are excluded from this row count and recorded separately, preventing a single high-dimensional cone from being confused with one scalar constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonical constraint growth compares scalar affine row counts under a fixed convention, while cone-block number and dimension are measured separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Constraint Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record primarily defines row-growth measures rather than asserting a complexity bound. It also needs a source supporting the stated counting convention, especially the separation of affine rows from cone blocks.

children.title: Auxiliary Dimension
children.top_down_role: Dimension attributable to representation-specific auxiliary objects.

assumptions_latex: The canonical variable vector is partitioned as \((x,u)\), where \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) represents original coordinates.
The auxiliary vector satisfies \(u\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{aux}}:=q=n_c-n\) when original coordinates are retained without duplication.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: auxiliary dimension is the dimension of the lifted coordinates removed by primal recovery
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies to explicit finite-dimensional lifts with a fixed original-coordinate embedding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The auxiliary dimension of the lift \((x,u)\) is \(d_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\dim u=q\). If the canonical representation retains each of the \(n\) original scalar coordinates exactly once and introduces no duplicate original coordinates, then \(d_{\mathrm{aux}}=n_c-n\). More generally, if original variables are embedded by an injective linear map \(E:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^{n_c}\), the intrinsic auxiliary dimension is \(d_{\mathrm{aux}}:=n_c-\operatorname{rank}E\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Auxiliary dimension counts lifted coordinates beyond the embedded original-variable subspace; it equals canonical minus original dimension for a direct embedding.
knowledge_statements.title: Auxiliary Dimension

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional definition fits the leaf and is internally consistent, but no inspectable source supports either the direct-lift definition or its embedded-subspace generalization.

children.title: Cone-Block Growth
children.top_down_role: Number and dimensions of cone blocks introduced by canonicalization.

assumptions_latex: The original conic representation uses blocks \(K_1,\ldots,K_b\).
The canonical representation uses blocks \(\widehat K_1,\ldots,\widehat K_{b_c}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta b=b_c-b\), with dimension growth recorded by \(\Delta d_K=\sum_{j=1}^{b_c}\dim\widehat K_j-\sum_{i=1}^{b}\dim K_i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cone products have natural block-count and total-dimension bookkeeping measures
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures both block count and total cone dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cone-block growth is \(\Delta b:=b_c-b\). Because block count alone ignores block sizes, it is paired with \(\Delta d_K:=\sum_{j=1}^{b_c}\dim\widehat K_j-\sum_{i=1}^{b}\dim K_i\). For a model family indexed by \(N\), bounds \(b_c(N)\le b(N)+\beta(N)\) and \(\Delta d_K(N)\le\delta(N)\) certify block and cone-coordinate growth. A product-cone factorization convention must be fixed, since merging adjacent identical cones changes \(b_c\) without changing the represented cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cone growth records both the increase in product-cone blocks and the increase in their total dimension under a fixed factorization convention.
knowledge_statements.title: Cone-Block Growth

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record defines cone-growth measures and only gives conditional bound templates; it does not itself establish a complexity bound. A supporting source and reconsideration of content_kind are required.

children.top_down_role: Retention of exploitable sparse and separable structure.

children.title: Sparsity Preservation
children.top_down_role: Retention of sparse coefficients and incidence patterns during canonicalization.

assumptions_latex: \(S_i\) is the set of original variable coordinates used by source atom \(i\).
Each canonical row or cone argument generated from atom \(i\) has original-coordinate support \(\widehat S_{ij}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat S_{ij}\subseteq S_i\) for every \(i,j\) is the atom-local sparsity-preservation condition.

notation.meaning: original-coordinate support of generated object j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses atom-local support containment; auxiliary-variable incidence is tracked separately.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonicalization preserves original-coordinate sparsity atomwise when \(\widehat S_{ij}\subseteq S_i\) for every generated affine row or cone argument \(j\) belonging to atom \(i\). Under this condition, canonicalization creates no direct coefficient coupling between original coordinates that did not co-occur in a source atom. This condition does not prohibit auxiliary variables or fill created later by eliminating them; those effects belong to the lifted incidence graph and its elimination ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparsity is preserved atomwise when every generated row or cone argument uses only original coordinates already present in its source atom.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A block-preserving canonicalization has \(\widehat K=\prod_{k=1}^p\widehat K_k\) and no generated local row involving both \(x_k\) and \(x_\ell\) for \(k\ne\ell\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Canonicalization preserves the partition \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_p)\) when its auxiliary variables admit a matching partition \(u=(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\), its local cone is \(\widehat K=\prod_{k=1}^p\widehat K_k\), and each generated local row depends only on \((x_k,u_k)\). Any source coupling constraint may remain as a designated coupling constraint, but canonicalization must introduce no additional cross-block row or cone factor. These predicates define block-structure preservation relative to the chosen source partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block structure is preserved when local lifts and cone factors follow the source partition and introduce no new cross-block coupling.

children.title: Fill-In Regimes
children.top_down_role: Representation choices that introduce avoidable structural density.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-In Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies symbolic fill for a specified family of lifted sparsity graphs and elimination orderings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((G_N)\) be a family of undirected lifted sparsity graphs with \(G_N=(V_N,E_N)\), let \(n_N:=|V_N|\to\infty\), and let \(\pi_N\) be a specified elimination ordering. Denote by \(F_{\pi_N}\) the edges added when each eliminated vertex's later neighbors are joined. The family is in the zero-fill regime when \(F_{\pi_N}=\varnothing\) for every \(N\). Given an explicit function \(B\) satisfying \(B(n)=o(n^2)\), it is in the nonzero \(B\)-bounded-fill regime when \(0<|F_{\pi_N}|\le B(n_N)\) for all sufficiently large \(N\). It is in the dense-added-fill regime when \(|F_{\pi_N}|=\Theta(n_N^2)\). These regimes depend on the selected orderings and do not classify intermediate growth not covered by the chosen \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a specified graph family and elimination orderings, fill is zero when no edges are added, nonzero B-bounded when the added-edge count is eventually bounded by an explicit subquadratic function B, and dense when quadratically many edges are added.
assumptions_latex: \(G_N=(V_N,E_N)\) is a family of undirected lifted sparsity graphs with \(n_N:=|V_N|\to\infty\).
\(\pi_N\) is a specified elimination ordering for \(G_N\), and \(F_{\pi_N}\) is its added-edge set.
\(B:\mathbb N\to\mathbb R_+\) is explicit and satisfies \(B(n)=o(n^2)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regimes are zero fill when \(F_{\pi_N}=\varnothing\), nonzero \(B\)-bounded fill when \(0<|F_{\pi_N}|\le B(n_N)\) eventually, and dense added fill when \(|F_{\pi_N}|=\Theta(n_N^2)\).

notation.meaning: lifted sparsity graph of family member N
specified elimination ordering for family member N
edges added under the specified elimination ordering
