knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a problem with positive decision variables, a minimization objective \(\operatorname{minimize} f_0(x)\) is DGP-admissible when \(f_0\) is certified log-log convex. A maximization objective \(\operatorname{maximize} f_0(x)\) is DGP-admissible when \(f_0\) is certified log-log concave. A log-log affine objective satisfies either orientation. Under the substitution \(u=\log x\), these objectives become, respectively, minimization of the convex function \(\log f_0(e^u)\) and maximization of the concave function \(\log f_0(e^u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DGP permits minimizing a log-log convex objective or maximizing a log-log concave objective; log-log affine objectives permit either orientation.
knowledge_statements.title: DGP Objective Families

children.title: DGP Constraint Families
children.top_down_role: Log-log curvature and affinity classes admitted in constraints.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Array-valued extension of the scalar DGP constraint templates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An array inequality \(F(x)\leq G(x)\) is DGP-admissible componentwise when every component \(F_k\) is certified log-log convex, every corresponding \(G_k\) is certified log-log concave, and all components are positive. An array equality is admissible when each paired component is log-log affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DGP applies its scalar inequality and equality rules componentwise to array-valued constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F_k(x),G_k(x)>0\) for every constrained component.
The compared arrays have compatible shapes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each component transforms to a convex inequality or affine equality in logarithmic coordinates.

notation.meaning: corresponding scalar components of the constrained arrays

knowledge_statements.title: Componentwise DGP Constraint Extension

assumptions_latex: All constraint expressions take values in \(\mathbb R_{++}\).
Each expression has a valid recursive DGP curvature certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\leq g\) is admissible for log-log convex \(f\) and log-log concave \(g\); \(f=g\) is admissible when both are log-log affine.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inequality and equality forms accepted by the DGP grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive inequality constraint \(f(x)\leq g(x)\) is DGP-admissible when \(f\) is certified log-log convex and \(g\) is certified log-log concave. After \(u=\log x\), it becomes the convex constraint \(\log f(e^u)-\log g(e^u)\leq0\). An equality \(f(x)=g(x)\) is DGP-admissible when both sides are log-log affine, in which case their transformed difference is affine. Constants and variables participate according to their log-log affine metadata, and every expression must remain strictly positive on its declared domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DGP accepts convex-to-concave positive inequalities and equalities between log-log affine expressions; logarithmic transformation converts them to standard convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: DGP Constraint Families

children.title: DGP Checker Architecture
children.top_down_role: Recursive certification using positivity and log-log metadata.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable witness produced by syntax-directed DGP certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A DGP derivation certificate assigns every expression-tree node a positive-domain assertion and a log-log curvature label, together with the primitive-atom or composition rule justifying that label from its children. It is valid when leaf declarations hold, every recorded local rule is applicable with the stated monotonicity and curvature metadata, and root labels satisfy the required objective or constraint orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DGP certificate is a locally checkable annotated expression tree whose node labels and rule witnesses justify the final problem orientation.
assumptions_latex: The expression tree is finite.
Primitive atom metadata are trusted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every valid derivation tree is a finite certificate of DGP admissibility}.
knowledge_statements.title: Recursive DGP Derivation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural complexity of a bottom-up checker pass.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent an expression as a tree with \(N\) nodes, or as a directed acyclic graph with \(N\) nodes and \(E\) child edges. If primitive metadata lookup is constant-time and each local check costs linear time in its number of children, one bottom-up pass uses \(O(N)\) time and stored annotations for a tree and \(O(N+E)\) time with \(O(N)\) stored annotations for a memoized DAG.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an explicit constant-time metadata cost model, bottom-up DGP certification is linear in the expression representation size.
assumptions_latex: Primitive metadata lookup is constant-time.
Each child edge is inspected a constant number of times.
Shared DAG subexpressions are memoized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_{\mathrm{tree}}=O(N),\qquad T_{\mathrm{DAG}}=O(N+E).

notation.meaning: numbers of expression nodes and child edges

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Time Metadata Pass

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failed certification does not imply mathematical non-log-log-convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Failure of recursive DGP rules proves only that the supplied syntax and available metadata do not certify the expression. It does not prove that the represented function is not log-log convex or that no equivalent DGP formulation exists. For a syntax-directed checker that performs no algebraic cancellation, \((x+y)/(x+y)\) is rejected because the reciprocal of the nonmonomial denominator is inadmissible, although the expression equals the certifiable constant \(1\) on \(x,y>0\). Algebraic rewriting, a verified new atom, or an exact graph representation can therefore turn a rejected expression into a certifiable one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DGP rejection is conservative: for example, an unsimplified ratio of a positive posynomial by itself may be rejected even though it equals the certifiable constant one.
assumptions_latex: The checker uses a fixed atom library and syntax-directed rules.
The checker does not perform the algebraic cancellation in the displayed example.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{rejection}\centernot\Longrightarrow\text{non-log-log-convexity}.
knowledge_statements.title: Conservative Rejection Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness and semantic equivalence of accepted DGP problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a recursive checker accepts a DGP problem using sound primitive metadata and sound log-log composition rules, then the componentwise substitution \(x=e^u\), together with the prescribed increasing logarithmic transformation of positive expressions, produces a convex problem. Feasible points correspond bijectively under \(u=\log x\), and the increasing objective transformation preserves optimizers in the admitted objective orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every accepted DGP problem transforms soundly into a convex problem, with feasible points and optimizers corresponding through logarithmic coordinates.
assumptions_latex: All primitive metadata and composition rules used by the checker are sound.
All variables and expressions satisfy their asserted positive domains.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{checker acceptance}\Longrightarrow\text{an equivalent convex logarithmic formulation}.
knowledge_statements.title: Soundness of Recursive DGP Certification
DGP Checker Architecture
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive syntax-directed certification of positivity and log-log curvature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an expression tree whose leaves are positive variables or positive constants and whose atom nodes carry domain, sign, log-log curvature, and coordinatewise monotonicity metadata. Traverse the tree bottom-up. At each atom, first verify its domain and positivity requirements; then apply the log-log composition rule to its already-certified children and assign convex, concave, affine, or unknown curvature. Reject any node with incompatible metadata. Finally, accept a problem only if its objective satisfies the DGP objective rule and every constraint satisfies the DGP constraint rule. Output the transformed convex problem when accepted; otherwise output failure with the first uncertified subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The checker certifies an expression tree bottom-up from atom metadata, then validates objective and constraint orientations and emits either a convex transform or a failing subtree.
assumptions_latex: Every primitive atom has trusted domain, positivity, curvature, and monotonicity metadata.
The input syntax tree is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns either a recursive DGP certificate and convex logarithmic transform, or a local certification failure.

notation.meaning: curvature state not certified by the composition rules

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind matches the checker-architecture leaf, but details such as returning the first uncertified subtree and emitting a transformed problem are implementation-specific and require an authoritative specification or implementation locator.

children.title: DGP-to-DCP Reduction
children.top_down_role: The reduction family connecting DGP-certified models to ordinary convex canonicalization.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Implementation as a CVXPY reduction

children.title: Logarithmic Coordinate Transformation
children.top_down_role: Positive-variable coordinate transformation used before convex canonicalization.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Log Coordinates Exclude the Orthant Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary behavior of the logarithmic coordinate bijection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The bijection \(u=\log x\) covers exactly \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\). If \(x_i^{(k)}\downarrow0\), then \(u_i^{(k)}=\log x_i^{(k)}\to-\infty\), so no finite \(u_i\) represents \(x_i=0\). Replacing a merely nonnegative source variable by a finite log variable therefore deletes its zero boundary unless a separate limiting or extended formulation handles it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite logarithmic coordinates represent strict positivity only; zero lies at minus infinity.
assumptions_latex: Logarithm and exponential are applied componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=0\) has no representative in \(u_i\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: positive sequence approaching the orthant boundary

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Log Coordinates Exclude the Orthant Boundary

assumptions_latex: The source variable satisfies \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maps \(x\mapsto \log x\) and \(u\mapsto \exp u\) give a bijection between \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) and \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports disciplined geometric programming; an authoritative DGP source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise change of coordinates for strictly positive finite-dimensional variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), define \(u=\log x\) componentwise. Then \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and the inverse transformation is \(x=\exp u\), also componentwise. Hence
\[
\log:\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}^n
\quad\text{and}\quad
\exp:\mathbb{R}^n\longrightarrow\mathbb{R}_{++}^n
\]
are mutually inverse bijections. Under this substitution, a positive-valued expression \(f(x)\) is represented in logarithmic coordinates by \(F(u)=\log f(\exp u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strictly positive variables are bijectively replaced by unconstrained log variables; every positive expression becomes its logarithm evaluated at the componentwise exponential.
knowledge_statements.title: Logarithmic Coordinate Transformation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation matches the logarithmic-coordinate leaf, introduces the finite-dimensional positive domain, and keeps TeX commands properly delimited. The bijection and transformed-expression formula are mathematically standard, but no inspectable source reference or locator is supplied.

children.title: Log-Transformed Atom Mapping
children.top_down_role: Translation of DGP atoms into DCP-compatible expressions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Classical Monomial and Posynomial Atom Images
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical transformed expressions for the classical atoms embedded in DGP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a monomial \(m(x)=c\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{a_j}\) with \(c>0\), \[\log m(e^u)=\log c+a^{\mathsf T}u,\] which is affine. For a posynomial \(p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{a_{kj}}\) with \(c_k>0\), \[\log p(e^u)=\operatorname{lse}_{k=1}^K\!\left(a_k^{\mathsf T}u+\log c_k\right),\] which is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monomials map to affine expressions, while posynomials map to log-sum-exp expressions over affine terms.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\).
All displayed coefficients are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) maps to an affine DCP expression and \(p\) maps to a convex DCP expression.

notation.meaning: exponent vector of monomial term k

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Monomial and Posynomial Atom Images

assumptions_latex: The atom \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}_{++}\) has positive domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\).
Its log-log curvature and composition metadata are certified by the DGP grammar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transformed atom \(F(u)=\log f(\exp u)\) has the corresponding DCP curvature on \(U=\{u:\exp u\in D\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator documents the DGP atom-reduction rules or their certified composition grammar.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Atomwise representation underlying a DGP-to-DCP reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}_{++}\), where \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\), and set
\[
F(u)=\log f(\exp u),\qquad U=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^n:\exp u\in D\}.
\]
The atom \(f\) is log-log convex, log-log concave, or log-log affine exactly when \(F\) is respectively convex, concave, or affine on \(U\). A certified DGP expression tree is reduced recursively by replacing each positive variable by its exponential-coordinate representative and each recognized atom by its corresponding \(F\), while preserving the composition relations certified by the atom's monotonicity metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each recognized positive atom is replaced by its log-after-exponential transform, converting log-log curvature into ordinary DCP curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Transformed Atom Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the atom-mapping leaf, and the equivalence between log-log curvature of f and ordinary curvature of its transform F is stated consistently. The recursive grammar-preservation claim depends on the precise DGP atom library, monotonicity metadata, and reduction rules, none of which has an inspectable citation.

children.title: Positive-Domain Solution Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of source variables and objective information after convex solution.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unbounded-Status Transport at a Zero Infimum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Status distinction for positive minimization objectives under logarithmic transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive minimization objective \(f_0\) and \(F_0=\log f_0\), \[\inf F_0=-\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\inf f_0=0.\] Because \(f_0>0\), the source problem is still bounded below in the ordinary real-valued sense and cannot attain value zero. Therefore a transformed status of unbounded below must not automatically be reported as source-objective unboundedness; it represents a zero, unattained source infimum. Exact feasibility and finite attained optima do transport bijectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed positive-objective minimization can be unbounded below merely because the source infimum is zero, even though the source objective is bounded below.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0(x)>0\) on the source feasible set.
The source and transformed feasible sets correspond exactly under \(x=e^u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf F_0=-\infty\) corresponds to \(\inf f_0=0\), not ordinary source unboundedness below.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded-Status Transport at a Zero Infimum

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Transformed Error Becomes Multiplicative Source Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy transport when exponentiating an approximate transformed solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=e^u\) and \(\widehat x=e^{\widehat u}\). If \(\|\widehat u-u\|_\infty\leq\delta\), then \[e^{-\delta}\leq\frac{\widehat x_i}{x_i}\leq e^\delta,\qquad \frac{|\widehat x_i-x_i|}{x_i}\leq e^\delta-1.\] Thus additive log-coordinate accuracy gives a multiplicative rather than scale-independent absolute source-space guarantee. Floating-point exponentiation may additionally overflow or underflow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A log-coordinate error of delta produces multiplicative source-coordinate error factors between exp(−delta) and exp(delta).
assumptions_latex: \(u,\widehat u\in\mathbb R^n\).
Exponentiation is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(e^{-\delta}\leq\widehat x_i/x_i\leq e^\delta\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Transformed Error Becomes Multiplicative Source Error

assumptions_latex: A reduced convex problem in \(u\in\mathbb{R}^n\) is equivalent to the source DGP under \(x=\exp u\).
The source objective \(f_0(x)\) is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: From any transformed solution \(u^\star\), recover \(x^\star=\exp u^\star\) and \(f_0(x^\star)=\exp F_0(u^\star)\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports DGP solution and objective recovery.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal and objective recovery for an exactly equivalent logarithmic reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a solution \(u^\star\) of the reduced convex problem, compute
\[
x_i^\star=\exp(u_i^\star),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.
\]
If the transformed objective is \(F_0(u)=\log f_0(\exp u)\), recover the source objective value as
\[
f_0(x^\star)=\exp(F_0(u^\star)).
\]
For minimization or maximization, the ordering of feasible objective values is preserved because \(\log\) is strictly increasing. Report \(x^\star\) only when the transformed solver status supplies a primal solution; otherwise propagate the corresponding infeasibility, unboundedness, or indeterminate status without exponentiating a nonexistent optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponentiate the transformed optimizer componentwise and exponentiate the transformed objective value; preserve solver failure statuses when no optimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Domain Solution Recovery

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits solution recovery, and primal and objective recovery are correctly expressed under the stated exact-equivalence assumptions. The claims concerning propagation of solver statuses through the DGP reduction require a source describing the canonicalization and status semantics.

children.title: DGP Dual-Information Transport
children.top_down_role: Transport and interpretation of dual information through the logarithmic reduction.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier conversion between a logarithmic ratio constraint and a source difference constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider source minimization of a positive differentiable objective \(f_0(x)\) with \(q(x)=f(x)-g(x)\leq0\), and its logarithmic reduction with objective \(\Phi(u)=\log f_0(e^u)\) and constraint \(H(u)=\log f(e^u)-\log g(e^u)\leq0\). At an active point \(x=e^u\) with \(f(x)=g(x)=s>0\), a transformed multiplier \(\lambda_H\geq0\) corresponds, under the same minimization sign convention, to the source multiplier \[\lambda_q=\frac{f_0(x)}{s}\lambda_H.\] If the source objective is instead kept as \(\log f_0\), the coefficient of \(\nabla q\) is \(\lambda_H/s\). The same scaling identity applies to a free equality multiplier, subject to its declared equality-sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiplier for log(f/g) must be rescaled by both the active constraint value and the chosen objective normalization before it is interpreted for f−g.
assumptions_latex: \(f_0,f,g\) are positive and differentiable near the point.
The source and transformed Lagrangians use the stated minimization and constraint-sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_q=f_0(x)\lambda_H/s\) for the source objective \(f_0\).

notation.meaning: common positive value of both sides at activity
multipliers under the transformed and source normalizations

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Aware Multiplier Scaling

assumptions_latex: A differentiable transformed constraint is \(H(u)=\log h(\exp u)\leq 0\), with \(h(x)>0\).
The recovered point satisfies \(x=\exp u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transformed covector \(p_u\) pulls back to \(p_x=\operatorname{Diag}(x)^{-1}p_u\); multipliers refer to the logarithmically normalized constraint.

notation.meaning: Covectors in transformed and source coordinates.

review_flags: Dual transport depends on the exact canonicalization and constraint normalization; no directly relevant source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate pullback and normalization caveat for differentiable scalar constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x=\exp u\), the differential satisfies
\[
du=\operatorname{Diag}(x)^{-1}dx.
\]
Consequently, a covector \(p_u\) in logarithmic coordinates pulls back to
\[
p_x=\operatorname{Diag}(x)^{-1}p_u,
\]
so that \(p_u^{\mathsf T}du=p_x^{\mathsf T}dx\). For \(H(u)=\log h(\exp u)\), the chain rule gives
\[
\nabla_u H(u)=
\operatorname{Diag}(x)\nabla_x\log h(x).
\]
A multiplier returned for \(H(u)\leq0\) therefore belongs to that logarithmically normalized constraint; it must not be interpreted as the multiplier of a differently scaled source constraint without applying the corresponding scaling rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual covectors transform by the inverse diagonal Jacobian, while returned multipliers belong to the exact logarithmic constraint normalization used in canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.title: DGP Dual-Information Transport

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits dual-information transport. The coordinate pullback and chain-rule formulas are internally consistent, but the interpretation and scaling of returned multipliers depend on the exact normalized constraints and canonicalization implementation. No source locator establishes those conventions.

children.title: DGP Applicability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Domain, recognition, parameter, and numerical boundaries of geometric certification.

children.title: Nonpositive-Domain Failures
children.top_down_role: Models incompatible with logarithmic coordinates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Boundary Optimum Lost by Logarithmic Coordinates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of a zero-valued optimizer when a nonnegative domain is replaced by finite logarithmic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem \(\min\{x:x\geq0\}\) has the unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\). After imposing \(x=e^u\) with \(u\in\mathbb R\), the transformed objective has infimum zero but no minimizer. Thus finite logarithmic coordinates can omit both a feasible boundary point and an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-valued optimizer can become only an unattained limit after logarithmic substitution.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) ranges over \([0,\infty)\).
The transformed model permits only finite real coordinates \(u=\log x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\geq0}x=\{0\}\), whereas \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb R}e^u=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Finite logarithmic coordinate of the positive variable.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary Optimum Lost by Logarithmic Coordinates

assumptions_latex: A modeled variable or atom argument is intended to undergo a real logarithmic transformation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any feasible occurrence of a required logarithm argument with value in \((-\infty,0]\) makes the logarithmic reduction undefined.

notation.meaning: A scalar quantity supplied to a logarithm during reduction.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly treats the positive-domain boundary of DGP canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real logarithmic reduction requires strict positivity, not mere nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The real logarithmic coordinate \(u=\log z\) is defined only for \(z>0\). Thus a DGP reduction is invalid if a variable, parameter, atom output, or atom argument that must be logged can attain \(z=0\) or \(z<0\) at a modeled feasible point. In particular, replacing strict positivity by \(z\geq0\) does not repair the model: \(z=0\) corresponds only to the unattained limit \(u\to-\infty\), and negative values have no real logarithmic coordinate. Such expressions require a different formulation rather than direct DGP canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logged quantity must be strictly positive; zero is only a limiting value and negative values have no real logarithmic coordinate.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpositive-Domain Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind exactly fits the leaf. The strict-positivity requirement, exclusion of zero, and absence of real logarithmic coordinates for negative values are precise and consistent, but the record contains no inspectable source supporting their application to DGP canonicalization.

children.title: Unrecognized Log-Log Curvature
children.top_down_role: Log-log convex expressions outside the available grammar or atom library.

assumptions_latex: A positive expression \(f\) is mathematically log-log convex or log-log concave.
The certification system recognizes only a declared atom library and its composition rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Log-log curvature alone does not imply grammatical certifiability; an unavailable atom or composition certificate causes rejection.
review_flags: The distinction between semantic curvature and grammar recognition needs a source for the intended DGP implementation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic log-log curvature may exceed the expressive power of a fixed grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f:D\to\mathbb{R}_{++}\) has a convex transform \(F(u)=\log f(\exp u)\) on its logarithmic domain. This establishes mathematical log-log convexity, but a grammar-based verifier accepts \(f\) only if its expression tree admits a recursive certificate using recognized atoms, declared monotonicities, known signs, and permitted composition rules. Therefore a log-log convex expression can fail certification when it is represented by an unknown atom or by a composition for which the library has no rule. Rewriting it with certified atoms or registering a sound atom certificate may restore recognition without changing the represented function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function may truly have log-log curvature yet fail DGP certification because its atom or composition certificate is absent from the grammar.
knowledge_statements.title: Unrecognized Log-Log Curvature

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the distinction between semantic log-log curvature and grammatical recognition. The mathematical distinction is coherent, but acceptance, rewriting, and atom-registration behavior depend on a particular verifier and atom library for which no source or implementation locator is supplied.

children.title: Geometric Parameter-Discipline Failures
children.top_down_role: Positive-parameter interactions outside geometric DPP.

assumptions_latex: Every parameter used as a logged quantity has a fixed value in \(\mathbb{R}_{++}\).
The model is intended to admit a parameter-independent canonical form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A positive DGP model can fail geometric parameter discipline when transformed parameter interactions cannot be represented with parameter-independent certified curvature data.
review_flags: The exact geometric DPP parameter rules are implementation-specific and no relevant source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between pointwise DGP validity and reusable parameter-disciplined canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\in\mathbb{R}_{++}^p\) be a parameter and \(\eta=\log\theta\). Pointwise DGP validity at each fixed \(\theta\) does not by itself establish geometric parameter discipline. Certification additionally requires every parameterized subexpression, after logarithmic transformation, to satisfy the system's parameter rules so that its curvature and canonicalization structure are independent of the numerical parameter value. A subexpression fails this discipline when parameters occupy interacting roles that the grammar cannot certify, such as a parameter simultaneously controlling an exponent and a logged base. The model may remain solvable after fixing \(\theta\), but it lacks the claimed reusable parameterized reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise DGP validity does not ensure geometric parameter discipline when parameter interactions alter curvature or canonicalization structure after logarithmic transformation.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Parameter-Discipline Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind matches the terminal container, but the claimed parameter-discipline criterion and the exponent/base interaction example are implementation-specific. An authoritative geometric DPP specification with a section or rule locator is required to determine whether the hypotheses and conclusion are exact.

children.title: Log-Coordinate Scaling Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Numerical difficulties associated with extreme positive values or transformed data.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable evaluation of a basic log-domain expression arising in geometric canonicalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(a_1,\ldots,a_r\), let \(m=\max_i a_i\). Then \[\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^r e^{a_i}\right)=m+\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^r e^{a_i-m}\right).\] Every shifted exponent is nonpositive, preventing overflow caused by exponentiating a large positive input. Very small shifted terms may underflow, subject to the working arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the largest log term before exponentiation prevents overflow in log-sum-exp evaluation.
assumptions_latex: Each \(a_i\) is finite in the working arithmetic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{LSE}(a)=m+\log\sum_i e^{a_i-m},\quad m=\max_i a_i.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Max-Shifted Log-Sum-Exp Evaluation

assumptions_latex: Positive source data and iterates are represented in finite-precision arithmetic.
The logarithmic reduction uses \(u=\log x\) and recovery uses \(x=\exp u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Extreme magnitudes can cause overflow, underflow, loss of relative accuracy, or poor transformed scaling despite exact mathematical equivalence.

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest representable positive finite numbers.

review_flags: Numerical thresholds depend on arithmetic and implementation; no relevant numerical-analysis source locator was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision hazards in logarithmic canonicalization and exponential recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In floating-point arithmetic with positive finite range \([m_{\min},m_{\max}]\), recovery by \(x=\exp u\) overflows or underflows when \(u\) lies outside the representable exponential range, approximately \([\log m_{\min},\log m_{\max}]\). Even inside that interval, widely separated logarithmic coordinates or transformed constants can produce poorly scaled affine and conic data, while forming positive expressions before taking their logarithms can lose relative accuracy. Stable implementations should evaluate log-domain forms directly when available and rescale equivalent transformed constraints; exact equivalence of the real-valued models does not guarantee numerical equivalence of their finite-precision realizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme positive magnitudes can overflow or underflow during exponential recovery and can produce poorly scaled transformed problems even when the mathematics is exact.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Coordinate Scaling Pathologies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits numerical scaling pathologies. children.title: Certification Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Explanatory interfaces for accepted, unresolved, and rejected source models.

children.title: Failing Subexpression Localization
children.top_down_role: Localization of informative grammatical failures within expression structure.

assumptions_latex: The modeled expression is a finite rooted syntax tree.
Each node has locally inferred metadata and an applicable certification rule or recorded failure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a minimal failing subtree relative to the verifier's child-first traversal and local rules.
review_flags: The localization policy is verifier-dependent and no implementation or formal diagnostic specification was supplied.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bottom-up localization of a grammar failure in an expression tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rooted expression tree \(T\), evaluate certification bottom-up. For each node \(v\), first certify every child; if a child fails, descend to a failing child according to a fixed deterministic order. If all children certify but the rule at \(v\) fails, return \(v\), its operator, inferred metadata, required metadata, and the violated rule. If the root certifies, return no failure. A returned node \(v\) is locally minimal in the sense that \(C(v)\) is false while \(C(w)\) is true for every child \(w\) of \(v\). Ties between independent failing branches are reported separately or resolved by the declared traversal order.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certify bottom-up and return the first node whose children certify but whose own rule fails, together with the violated metadata requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Failing Subexpression Localization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits failing-subexpression localization, and the statement explicitly defines its child-first notion of local minimality and tie policy. However, this is a verifier-specific diagnostic algorithm rather than a universal consequence of DCP, and no formal specification or implementation locator supports it.

children.title: Metadata Mismatch Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostics organized by shape, sign, curvature, monotonicity, or domain.

assumptions_latex: Every expression node carries inferred shape, sign, curvature, monotonicity, and domain metadata.
Every atom rule declares the metadata required of its arguments and output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A diagnostic is a checkable tuple identifying the node, metadata field, inferred value, required value, and governing rule.

notation.meaning: Metadata field and its inferred and required values.

review_flags: The diagnostic schema and metadata lattice are system-specific and lack a supplied source or implementation specification.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured certificates for local metadata incompatibilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a failing node \(v\), a metadata-mismatch diagnostic is the tuple
\[
(v,k,m_{\mathrm{inf}},m_{\mathrm{req}},r),
\]
where \(k\) is one of shape, sign, curvature, monotonicity, or domain; \(m_{\mathrm{inf}}\) is the metadata inferred for \(v\) or an argument of \(v\); \(m_{\mathrm{req}}\) is the metadata required by certification rule \(r\); and the two values are incompatible under the verifier's metadata ordering. The tuple certifies a local rejection precisely when the recorded inference and rule can be replayed to confirm that \(m_{\mathrm{inf}}\) does not satisfy \(m_{\mathrm{req}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Report metadata failures as replayable tuples naming the node, field, inferred value, required value, and violated certification rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Metadata Mismatch Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind is appropriate because the record defines a replayable witness of metadata incompatibility. Its tuple fields and replay criterion are coherent, but the metadata ordering, inference records, and rule representation are system-specific and have no cited specification or implementation locator.

children.title: Problem-Form Diagnostic System
children.top_down_role: Explanations for invalid objective or constraint orientation.

children.title: Objective-Form Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Explanations for objective curvature or orientation incompatibilities.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certification Failure Is Not a Nonconvexity Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation boundary for objective-form rejection caused by insufficient curvature metadata.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a sound DCP analyzer cannot certify the curvature required by the declared objective sense, it must reject the objective form. Such rejection establishes only failure of that certification system, not nonconvexity of the represented function or problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to certify an objective is not proof that the objective or problem is nonconvex.
assumptions_latex: The curvature analyzer is sound but need not be complete.
The objective expression is well-defined on its modeled domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{DCPReject}(f_0)\not\Rightarrow f_0\text{ is nonconvex or nonconcave}.
knowledge_statements.title: Certification Failure Is Not a Nonconvexity Certificate

assumptions_latex: The objective expression has certified curvature metadata.
The problem declares either minimization, maximization, or feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A DCP objective is valid exactly when minimization uses a convex objective, maximization uses a concave objective, or feasibility has no substantive objective.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly states the DCP objective-orientation rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: DCP objective-orientation validity and its diagnostic classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f_0\) be the certified objective expression. The objective form is DCP-valid exactly in one of the following cases:
\[
\operatorname{minimize} f_0\quad\text{with \(f_0\) convex},
\]
\[
\operatorname{maximize} f_0\quad\text{with \(f_0\) concave},
\]
or the problem is a feasibility problem with no nonconstant objective. A minimization objective known only to be concave, a maximization objective known only to be convex, or an objective of unknown curvature yields an objective-form diagnostic recording the declared orientation, inferred curvature, and required curvature. Affine objectives satisfy both curvature requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimization requires a convex objective, maximization requires a concave objective, and feasibility requires no substantive objective; affine objectives satisfy either orientation.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Form Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits objective-form diagnostics. The minimization, maximization, feasibility, and affine-objective conditions are standard and internally consistent, but the record supplies no authoritative textbook, DCP specification, or implementation locator as required by the evidence contract.

children.title: Constraint-Form Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Explanations for invalid equality or inequality forms.

assumptions_latex: Each constraint side has certified curvature and domain metadata.
Equality and inequality orientations are fixed by the modeled problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: DCP permits \(f\leq g\) with convex \(f\) and concave \(g\), \(f\geq g\) with concave \(f\) and convex \(g\), and equality only between affine sides.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly states the complete DCP constraint-form rules.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard scalar DCP constraint-orientation conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A scalar constraint is DCP-valid exactly under the applicable curvature condition:
\[
f(x)\leq g(x)\quad\text{requires \(f\) convex and \(g\) concave},
\]
\[
f(x)\geq g(x)\quad\text{requires \(f\) concave and \(g\) convex},
\]
and
\[
f(x)=g(x)\quad\text{requires both \(f\) and \(g\) affine}.
\]
The expressions must also have compatible scalar shapes and nonempty domains on the modeled feasible set. A constraint-form diagnostic records the relation, each side's inferred shape and curvature, and the unmet requirement. Reversing an inequality swaps the required curvature roles but does not alter the represented feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DCP inequalities place convex expressions below concave ones, while equalities require affine sides; shapes and domains must also be compatible.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Form Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits constraint-form diagnostics. The scalar inequality orientations and affine-equality rule are standard and correctly aligned between plain text and LaTeX, with shape and domain requirements stated. No authoritative source reference with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Problem-Role Mismatch Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Cases where a valid expression appears in an inadmissible problem role.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a certified expression from its admissibility in a contextual DCP problem role.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expression may have certified curvature yet be invalid in its assigned problem role. Role validity is contextual: a convex nonaffine expression is admissible in a convex-required role but not in a concave- or affine-required role; a concave nonaffine expression has the converse admissibility; and an affine expression satisfies both convex and concave curvature requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expression certification and contextual role validity are distinct; certified curvature must match the role where the expression is used.
assumptions_latex: Expression curvature has been soundly certified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{ValidExpression}(e)\not\Rightarrow\operatorname{ValidInRole}(e,r).

notation.meaning: problem role assigned to the expression

knowledge_statements.title: Syntactic Validity Versus Role Validity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unknown Curvature Produces an Uncertified Role
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General role-diagnostic behavior when required curvature cannot be established.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the curvature required by a role cannot be certified, the expression must be reported as uncertified for that role even when no opposite-curvature certificate is available. Unknown curvature is therefore distinct from certified wrong curvature, and neither diagnostic alone proves that the underlying mathematical problem is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unknown curvature and certified wrong curvature are distinct role diagnostics; neither rejection alone proves nonconvexity.
assumptions_latex: The analyzer is sound but may be incomplete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \kappa(e)=\mathrm{unknown}\Rightarrow e\text{ is uncertified in every role requiring definite curvature}.

notation.meaning: certified curvature metadata of expression e

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown Curvature Produces an Uncertified Role

assumptions_latex: The expression tree has scalar objective curvature and constraint-side curvature metadata assigned by sound DCP composition rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A role mismatch is reported exactly when the declared problem role is incompatible with these curvature requirements.

notation.meaning: left and right sides of constraint i

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports DCP problem-role diagnostics.
Terminology and diagnostic behavior require a disciplined-convex-programming source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic predicate for objective and constraint roles in scalar DCP problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, the objective \(f_0\) must be convex; for a maximization problem, \(f_0\) must be concave; and a feasibility problem has no optimized objective. Each inequality written \(f_i\le g_i\) must have convex \(f_i\) and concave \(g_i\), while each equality \(f_i=g_i\) must have affine sides. A problem-role mismatch is any violation of the requirement associated with the declared objective sense or constraint relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mismatch occurs when objective sense or constraint role conflicts with the curvature required by disciplined convex programming.
knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Role Mismatch Diagnostics

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The diagnostic is mathematically plausible and locally appropriate, but no inspectable source supports the stated DCP role rules or the exact mismatch predicate.

children.title: Orientation Repair Guidance
children.top_down_role: Scope of source-level changes that expose admissible objective or constraint orientation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraically equivalent normalization of scalar objectives and relations followed by fresh DCP certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sound orientation-normalization procedure may use
\[
f\le g\iff f-g\le0\iff g-f\ge0\iff -g\le-f,
\qquad f=g\iff f-g=0,
\]
and, for a known nonzero scalar \(\alpha\), may multiply both sides of an inequality by \(\alpha\), preserving its sense when \(\alpha>0\) and reversing it when \(\alpha<0\). It may also use \(\min f\equiv\max(-f)\), with the same optimizer set and negated optimal value. After every rewrite, curvature and sign metadata must be recomputed, and the result is accepted only when every resulting objective and relation satisfies its DCP role requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize relations using equivalent difference, sign, and scaling forms, then recompute metadata and accept only a newly certified form.
assumptions_latex: Every rewrite is applied to the complete relation or objective.
Any scaling factor used to orient an inequality has certified nonzero sign.
Curvature and sign metadata are recomputed after rewriting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{x:f(x)\le g(x)\}=\{x:f(x)-g(x)\le0\}=\{x:-g(x)\le-f(x)\},\qquad\arg\min f=\arg\max(-f).
knowledge_statements.title: Orientation Normalization and Recertification

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective Negation Cannot Repair Wrong Curvature
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary on objective sign-and-sense changes as a cure for curvature mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Negating an objective while reversing its optimization sense preserves an objective-form mismatch. If \(f\) is concave and nonaffine, both \(\min f\) and the equivalent \(\max(-f)\) are invalid DCP objectives. If \(f\) is convex and nonaffine, both \(\max f\) and the equivalent \(\min(-f)\) are invalid. A different equivalent reformulation exposing additional certifiable structure is required to change the diagnosis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating an objective while reversing its sense preserves wrong curvature and is not a repair by itself.
assumptions_latex: The objective is nonaffine.
The transformed problem must preserve the optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f\text{ concave nonaffine}\Rightarrow(\min f\text{ invalid and }\max(-f)\text{ invalid}).
review_flags: Corrects the rejected immutable seed's unsound claim that objective negation and sense reversal repair wrong curvature.
knowledge_statements.title: Objective Negation Cannot Repair Wrong Curvature

assumptions_latex: The original relation is algebraically well-defined on its stated domain.
Curvature and monotonicity metadata for every expression are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure either returns an equivalent DCP-compatible orientation or reports that no permitted orientation repair was found.

notation.meaning: left and right expressions of a relation

review_flags: No supplied locator directly specifies an orientation-repair algorithm.
Permitted rewrite set and failure behavior require a DCP implementation or reference source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local repair of objective sense and constraint orientation without changing the feasible set or optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a rejected scalar relation, first normalize equality by moving affine terms only. For an inequality \(f\ge g\), rewrite it as \(g\le f\); accept precisely when \(g\) is convex and \(f\) is concave. For minimizing a concave objective or maximizing a convex objective, multiply the objective by \(-1\) and reverse the optimization sense, recording the transformed optimal value. Recompute all metadata after each rewrite. Stop at the first certified equivalent form; otherwise return the original diagnostic and failure status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize relation orientation, optionally negate and reverse the objective sense, then recertify; fail if no equivalent DCP form results.
knowledge_statements.title: Orientation Repair Guidance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Negating the objective while reversing the optimization sense preserves the curvature mismatch: minimizing concave f becomes maximizing convex -f, and maximizing convex f becomes minimizing concave -f. Thus the proposed step does not produce the claimed DCP-compatible orientation.

children.title: Certification Provenance System
children.top_down_role: Inspectable records of inferred metadata and rule applications.

children.title: Certification Traces
children.top_down_role: Inspectable records of metadata propagation and rule matching.

assumptions_latex: Certification uses a fixed expression tree and a fixed version of the atom-rule registry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A trace is valid when its root judgment follows from its recorded child judgments by the cited rule at every internal node.
review_flags: No supplied source addresses certification traces for disciplined convex modeling.
Trace schema and replay semantics require implementation documentation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replayable derivation certificate for curvature, sign, shape, and domain judgments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certification trace is a rooted directed acyclic record whose entry at each expression node \(v\) contains the atom identifier, child entries, inferred judgment \(J(v)\), applied rule identifier \(r(v)\), and discharged side conditions. Leaf entries record declared constants, variables, parameters, shapes, signs, and domains. The trace certifies the root judgment exactly when every entry can be replayed against the fixed registry and each recorded conclusion equals the rule output on its recorded premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certification trace records enough leaf metadata and rule applications to replay and verify the root DCP judgment.
knowledge_statements.title: Certification Traces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf, but the trace schema, registry assumptions, and replay-validity criterion require inspectable DCP implementation or specification evidence.

children.title: Metadata Provenance
children.top_down_role: Origins of inferred or declared expression metadata.

assumptions_latex: Every modeled object has a stable identifier within the certification artifact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Metadata provenance is complete when every derived metadata value has a finite dependency path to declared inputs and registry rules.
review_flags: No supplied source defines metadata-provenance completeness in DCP certification.
Required metadata fields and stable identifiers are implementation-dependent.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependency provenance for shape, sign, curvature, domain, and parameter attributes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every metadata value \(m(v)\), a provenance entry records whether it was declared or derived. A declared entry identifies its input declaration; a derived entry records the rule version and the finite set \(P(v,m)\) of metadata values used as premises. The provenance certificate is complete when recursively following these dependencies terminates at declarations or immutable registry facts, and it is consistent when replay produces exactly \(m(v)\) for every derived entry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each metadata value records its declaration or derivation dependencies, enabling complete and consistent replay.
knowledge_statements.title: Metadata Provenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed provenance certificate is coherent, but its completeness criterion, stable identifiers, and immutable registry facts are system-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Rule-Application Provenance
children.top_down_role: Origins and locations of certification rule applications.

assumptions_latex: Each certification rule has a stable identifier, version, premise schema, side conditions, and conclusion schema.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recorded application is valid exactly when its instantiated premises and side conditions hold and its conclusion matches the rule instance.
review_flags: No supplied locator supports rule-application provenance.
Exact registry versioning and side-condition schema require a DCP system source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable provenance for each application of a DCP composition or domain rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A rule-application provenance record is the tuple \((r,\nu,J_1,\ldots,J_k,S,J)\), where \(r\) is the rule identifier, \(\nu\) its registry version, the \(J_i\) are instantiated premises, \(S\) is the set of discharged side conditions, and \(J\) is the asserted conclusion. It is accepted only if the versioned rule schema matches the modeled atom, every premise and side condition is verifiable, and applying that schema yields exactly \(J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Record the versioned rule, premises, side conditions, and conclusion so each certification step can be checked locally.
knowledge_statements.title: Rule-Application Provenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind and local-checking description fit the container, but the versioned rule tuple and acceptance semantics lack an inspectable supporting specification.

children.title: Trace Granularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Levels of detail available for certification inspection.

assumptions_latex: All regimes refer to the same model, rule registry, and root certification judgment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Increasing trace granularity preserves the certified root judgment while retaining weakly more replay information.

notation.meaning: deterministic projection to a coarser trace

review_flags: Granularity regimes are system-design conventions rather than a uniquely standardized theorem.
No supplied source specifies projection or replay requirements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three trace regimes ordered by retained certification detail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T_0\) retain only the root result and diagnostics, \(T_1\) additionally retain one judgment per expression node, and \(T_2\) retain every instantiated rule, premise, and side condition. A coherent granularity family provides deterministic projections \(\pi_{2\to1}\) and \(\pi_{1\to0}\) that preserve node identifiers, diagnostic outcomes, and the root judgment. Thus a finer trace can reproduce every coarser trace, although the converse need not permit full replay.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summary, node-level, and rule-level traces form increasingly informative regimes with deterministic projections preserving the root result.
knowledge_statements.title: Trace Granularity Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The granularity hierarchy is a plausible design principle, but the three regimes and deterministic projection guarantees are conventions that require a cited system specification.

children.title: Equivalent Expression Rewrites

children.title: Norm-Quadratic Rewrite Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Recognizable alternatives for norm and convex quadratic structure.

children.title: Norm Rewrites
children.top_down_role: Equivalent source forms exposing supported norm structure.

assumptions_latex: The vector expression is affine: \(z(x)=Ax+b\).
The scalar expression \(t(x)\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|z(x)\|_2\le t(x)\iff t(x)\ge0\ \text{and}\ z(x)^\top z(x)\le t(x)^2\).
review_flags: The supplied section is relevant to norm-bounded quadratic formulations but may not state this exact elementary equivalence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean-norm inequality rewritten as a quadratic inequality with the indispensable nonnegative-bound condition.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\) in the common domain, the second-order-cone constraint \(\|Ax+b\|_2\le t(x)\) is equivalent to the conjunction \(t(x)\ge0\) and \((Ax+b)^\top(Ax+b)\le t(x)^2\). If the norm is minimized directly, then \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax+b\|_2=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax+b\|_2^2\) over any common feasible set, although the two optimal objective values generally differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Euclidean norm bound may be squared only with a nonnegative right side; minimizing the norm and its square has the same minimizers.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm Rewrites

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct Lorentz-cone representation of an affine Euclidean-norm bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z(x)=Ax+b\), \(t(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x+d\), and \(\mathcal Q^{m+1}=\{(s,y):\|y\|_2\le s\}\). Then
\[
\|Ax+b\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+d
\iff
(c^{\mathsf T}x+d,Ax+b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}.
\]
Cone membership automatically enforces nonnegativity of the scalar bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine Euclidean-norm bound is exactly one second-order-cone membership, which automatically enforces a nonnegative right side.
assumptions_latex: A,b,c,d\text{ have compatible finite dimensions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|Ax+b\|_2\le c^{\mathsf T}x+d\iff(c^{\mathsf T}x+d,Ax+b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Norm Rewrite

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite linear lifts for affine one-norm and infinity-norm bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an affine vector \(z(x)\in\mathbb{R}^m\),
\[
\|z(x)\|_1\le t(x)
\iff
\exists u\in\mathbb{R}_+^m:\ -u\le z(x)\le u,\quad\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}u\le t(x),
\]
and
\[
\|z(x)\|_\infty\le t(x)
\iff
-t(x)\mathbf1\le z(x)\le t(x)\mathbf1.
\]
Both formulations are polyhedral and imply \(t(x)\ge0\) whenever feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-norm bounds admit an absolute-value linear lift, while infinity-norm bounds are componentwise linear inequalities.
assumptions_latex: z(x)\text{ and }t(x)\text{ are affine}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|z\|_1\le t\iff\exists u\ge0:-u\le z\le u,\ \mathbf1^Tu\le t;\quad \|z\|_\infty\le t\iff-t\mathbf1\le z\le t\mathbf1.
knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral One- and Infinity-Norm Rewrites

children.title: Quadratic Rewrites
children.top_down_role: Equivalent source forms exposing supported convex quadratic structure.

assumptions_latex: The matrix \(Q\in\mathbb{S}^n_+\) is positive semidefinite.
A factor \(R\) satisfies \(Q=R^\top R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\top Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2\), and \(x^\top Qx\le t\iff\|Rx\|_2\le\sqrt{t}\) for \(t\ge0\).
review_flags: The supplied locator is provisional and may discuss a more specialized uncertain quadratic setting.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-semidefinite quadratic forms rewritten through a Euclidean-norm factorization.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Because \(Q=R^\top R\), the quadratic form satisfies \(x^\top Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2\) for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\). Consequently, for a scalar \(t\ge0\), the constraint \(x^\top Qx\le t\) is equivalent to \(\|Rx\|_2\le\sqrt{t}\). When \(t\) is a nonnegative constant this is a second-order-cone constraint; when \(t\) is variable, introducing \(s\ge0\) with \(s^2\le t\) requires a suitable conic representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factor a positive-semidefinite quadratic form as a squared Euclidean norm, then rewrite constant nonnegative sublevel bounds as norm constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic Rewrites

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Completion-of-Squares Rewrite for a Convex Quadratic
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact squared-affine-norm representation and its range condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2a^{\mathsf T}x+b\) with \(Q\succeq0\) and \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\). Then \(q\) admits a representation \(q(x)=\|Rx+d\|_2^2+\gamma\) if and only if \(a\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\). In that case one choice is \[q(x)=\left\|R(x+Q^\dagger a)\right\|_2^2+b-a^{\mathsf T}Q^\dagger a.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex quadratic is a squared affine norm plus a constant exactly when its linear coefficient lies in the range of its PSD quadratic matrix.
assumptions_latex: Q\in\mathbb S_+^n
q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2a^{\mathsf T}x+b
Q=R^{\mathsf T}R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: a\in\operatorname{range}(Q)\iff q(x)\text{ is a squared affine norm plus a constant}
knowledge_statements.title: Completion-of-Squares Rewrite for a Convex Quadratic

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Convex Quadratic Inequality as a Second-Order-Cone Constraint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact SOC rewrite that does not require the linear coefficient to lie in the quadratic matrix range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\succeq0\), let \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2a^{\mathsf T}x+b\), and let \(t\) be affine or constant. With \(\ell(x)=2a^{\mathsf T}x+b-t\), \[q(x)\le t\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \left\|\begin{bmatrix}2Rx\\ \ell(x)+1\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2\le1-\ell(x).\] This rewrite is valid for every \(a\); no range condition is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every convex quadratic inequality has an exact SOC rewrite, including cases where completion as one squared affine norm is impossible.
assumptions_latex: Q=R^{\mathsf T}R\succeq0
q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx+2a^{\mathsf T}x+b
t\text{ is affine or constant}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(x)\le t\iff\left\|[2Rx;\,2a^{\mathsf T}x+b-t+1]\right\|_2\le1-(2a^{\mathsf T}x+b-t)

notation.meaning: affine residual 2a transpose x plus b minus t

knowledge_statements.title: General Convex Quadratic Inequality as a Second-Order-Cone Constraint

children.title: Norm-to-Quadratic Relations
children.top_down_role: Connections between squared-norm expressions and quadratic representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-to-Quadratic Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective and sublevel correspondence between PSD quadratic forms and their factor norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(x\in C\), \(x^\top Qx=\|Rx\|_2^2\). If the minimum of \(\|Rx\|_2\) over \(C\) is attained, then the quadratic and norm objectives have identical minimizer sets and \(\min_{x\in C}x^\top Qx=(\min_{x\in C}\|Rx\|_2)^2\). Their sublevel sets satisfy \(x^\top Qx\le\alpha^2\) if and only if \(\|Rx\|_2\le\alpha\) for every \(\alpha\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PSD quadratic is the square of its factor norm; when the minimum is attained, the objectives have the same minimizers, and their nonnegative sublevel bounds correspond.

children.title: Log-Sum-Exp Rewrites

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact translation identities exposing a normalized log-sum-exp expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and scalar \(a\),
\[
\operatorname{LSE}(x+a\mathbf1)=a+\operatorname{LSE}(x).
\]
Consequently, with \(m=\max_i x_i\),
\[
\operatorname{LSE}(x)=m+\log\!\left(\sum_i e^{x_i-m}\right),
\]
and all shifted exponents satisfy \(x_i-m\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log-sum-exp is translation equivariant; subtracting the largest component gives an exact normalized expression with nonpositive exponents.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb{R}^n
n\ge1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LSE}(x)=\max_i x_i+\log\sum_i e^{x_i-\max_j x_j}.
knowledge_statements.title: Translation and Max-Shift Rewrites

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of nonnegative weighted log-sum-exp to the unweighted atom, including zero-weight removal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(w_i\ge0\) with at least one positive weight and set \(I_+=\{i:w_i>0\}\). Then
\[
\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n w_i e^{x_i}\right)
=\log\!\left(\sum_{i\in I_+}e^{x_i+\log w_i}\right).
\]
Positive weights are absorbed as additive offsets and zero-weight terms are removed. If all weights vanish, the extended-real value is \(-\infty\), not a finite log-sum-exp atom.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weights become logarithmic offsets, zero-weight terms disappear, and all-zero weights do not define a finite log-sum-exp value.
assumptions_latex: w\in\mathbb{R}_+^n
\sum_i w_i>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \log\sum_i w_i e^{x_i}=\operatorname{LSE}((x_i+\log w_i)_{i\in I_+}).
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Log-Sum-Exp Rewrite

Introducing \(u_i\ge0\) gives the conic rewrite \[(u_i,1,x_i-t)\in K_{\exp}\quad(i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n u_i\le1,\] where \(K_{\exp}=\operatorname{cl}\{(u,v,w):v>0,\ u\ge v e^{w/v}\}\). Thus the original epigraph constraint is represented using exponential-cone memberships and one linear inequality.

\(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log(\sum_i e^{x_i})\le t\iff \exists u:\ (u_i,1,x_i-t)\in K_{\exp},\ \sum_i u_i\le1\)

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Theoretic Rewrite Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Entropy variational representation of finite log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(\Delta_n=\{p\in\mathbb{R}_+^n:\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}p=1\}\), and define \(H(p)=-\sum_i p_i\log p_i\), with \(0\log0=0\). Then \[\log\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^n e^{x_i}\right)=\max_{p\in\Delta_n}\{p^{\mathsf T}x+H(p)\}.\] The maximizer is \(p_i=e^{x_i}/\sum_j e^{x_j}\). Equivalently, for every \(p\in\Delta_n\), log-sum-exp dominates \(p^{\mathsf T}x+H(p)\), with equality at the softmax distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Log-sum-exp is the maximum over probability vectors of a linear expectation plus Shannon entropy; equality occurs at the softmax distribution.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log(\sum_i e^{x_i})=\max_{p\in\Delta_n}(p^{\mathsf T}x+H(p))\)

source_refs.locator: §3.3, conjugate functions; log-sum-exp and negative-entropy example

source_witnesses.locator: §3.3, conjugate functions; log-sum-exp and negative-entropy example

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact gap identity refining the entropy variational representation of log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(q_i=e^{x_i}/\sum_j e^{x_j}\), and \(p\in\Delta_n\). Then
\[
\log\!\left(\sum_i e^{x_i}\right)-p^{\mathsf T}x-H(p)
=\sum_i p_i\log\frac{p_i}{q_i}
=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\ge0,
\]
with equality exactly when \(p=q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gap in the entropy variational formula is exactly the KL divergence from the trial distribution to softmax.
assumptions_latex: x\in\mathbb{R}^n
p\in\Delta_n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{LSE}(x)-p^{\mathsf T}x-H(p)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|\operatorname{softmax}(x))\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Softmax Relative-Entropy Gap Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel-conjugate statement underlying the entropy variational rewrite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=\log(\sum_{i=1}^n e^{x_i})\),
\[
F^*(p)=\begin{cases}
\sum_i p_i\log p_i,&p\in\Delta_n,\\
+\infty,&p\notin\Delta_n,
\end{cases}
\]
with \(0\log0=0\). Thus negative Shannon entropy on the probability simplex is the Fenchel conjugate of log-sum-exp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Fenchel conjugate of log-sum-exp is negative Shannon entropy on the probability simplex and infinity outside it.
assumptions_latex: n\ge1
F:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F^*(p)=\sum_i p_i\log p_i+\delta_{\Delta_n}(p).

knowledge_statements.title: Perspective Rewrites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-scale perspective reformulation of a proper convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, and define its positive-scale perspective by \(g(x,t)=t f(x/t)\) for \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(t>0\). Then \(g\) is convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_{++}\), and for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}\), \[g(x,t)\le s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad f(x/t)\le s/t.\] Thus a scaled epigraph with a strictly positive scale can be rewritten as an epigraph constraint for the perspective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a strictly positive scale, scaling a convex function and its argument together gives a convex perspective, and its epigraph inequality can equivalently be divided by the scale.

\(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
\(s\in\mathbb{R}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional Rewrites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set rewrite for a scalar linear-fractional expression with positive denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a,c,x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(b,d\in\mathbb{R}\), and define \(r(x)=(a^{\mathsf T}x+b)/(c^{\mathsf T}x+d)\) on \(D=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^{\mathsf T}x+d>0\}\). For every fixed \(\alpha\in\mathbb{R}\) and every \(x\in D\), \[r(x)\le\alpha\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^{\mathsf T}x+b\le\alpha(c^{\mathsf T}x+d).\] Thus a sublevel feasibility test for a linear-fractional expression is an affine inequality together with the positive-denominator domain constraint.

\(b,d\in\mathbb{R}\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact normalization of a positive-denominator linear-fractional program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_x\frac{a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta}{c^{\mathsf T}x+d}\quad\text{subject to }Ax\le h,\] and assume \(c^{\mathsf T}x+d>0\) at every feasible \(x\). Set \(\tau=(c^{\mathsf T}x+d)^{-1}>0\) and \(y=\tau x\). Then the problem is equivalent, through \(x=y/\tau\), to \[\min_{y,\tau}\ a^{\mathsf T}y+\beta\tau\quad\text{subject to }Ay\le h\tau,\quad c^{\mathsf T}y+d\tau=1,\quad\tau>0.\] The strict positive-scale constraint is part of the exact bijection; replacing it by \(\tau\ge0\) requires additional conditions excluding feasible zero-scale points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Charnes–Cooper normalization converts a positive-denominator linear-fractional program into an affine optimization problem on a strictly positive scale slice.

\{x:Ax\le h\}\ne\varnothing

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quasilinear level-set structure on a positive-denominator domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(x)=(a^{\mathsf T}x+\beta)/(c^{\mathsf T}x+d)\) on \(D=\{x:c^{\mathsf T}x+d>0\}\). For every \(\alpha\in\mathbb R\), \[\{x\in D:r(x)\le\alpha\}=D\cap\{x:(a-\alpha c)^{\mathsf T}x+\beta-\alpha d\le0\},\] and \[\{x\in D:r(x)\ge\alpha\}=D\cap\{x:(a-\alpha c)^{\mathsf T}x+\beta-\alpha d\ge0\}.\] Thus \(r\) is both quasiconvex and quasiconcave on \(D\).

\alpha\in\mathbb R

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-over-linear expressions as perspectives of positive-semidefinite quadratic forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb{S}_+^n\), \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), \(t>0\), and \(s\in\mathbb{R}\), and define \(q(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Qx\). The perspective of \(q\) satisfies \[tq(x/t)=\frac{x^{\mathsf T}Qx}{t}.\] Consequently, its epigraph has the equivalent semidefinite representation \[\frac{x^{\mathsf T}Qx}{t}\le s\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{bmatrix}s&(Q^{1/2}x)^{\mathsf T}\\Q^{1/2}x&tI_n\end{bmatrix}\succeq0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic form divided by a positive scalar is its perspective and has an equivalent block positive-semidefinite epigraph representation.

\(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\)
\(s\in\mathbb{R}\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneity law explaining when a perspective becomes a fractional expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) is positively homogeneous of degree \(p\), meaning \(f(\lambda x)=\lambda^p f(x)\) for every \(\lambda>0\), then for \(t>0\), \[t f(x/t)=t^{1-p}f(x).\] Thus the positive-scale perspective of a degree-one function is independent of \(t\), while the perspective of a degree-two function is \(f(x)/t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-p homogeneous function acquires the factor t to the power 1-p under perspective; degree two is exactly the quadratic-over-linear case.

knowledge_statements.title: Denominator-Sign Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of cross-multiplication without a known nonzero denominator sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real \(u,v,\alpha\) with \(v\ne0\), \[\frac{u}{v}\le\alpha\iff\begin{cases}u\le\alpha v,&v>0,\\u\ge\alpha v,&v<0.\end{cases}\] At \(v=0\) the ratio is undefined. Therefore the rewrite \(u/v\le\alpha\iff u\le\alpha v\) is valid only under \(v>0\); if the denominator can change sign, the feasible set requires a sign disjunction and generally is not represented by one convex inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-multiplication preserves an inequality only for a positive denominator, reverses it for a negative denominator, and is invalid at zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Rewrites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semidefinite epigraph rewrite of the largest eigenvalue.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\) and \(t\in\mathbb{R}\), the spectral bound \[\lambda_{\max}(X)\le t\] is equivalent to the linear matrix inequality \[tI-X\succeq0.\] Likewise, \(\lambda_{\min}(X)\ge t\) is equivalent to \(X-tI\succeq0\). These equivalences follow from the characterization of semidefinite order by the eigenvalues of a real symmetric matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower eigenvalue bounds on a symmetric matrix are exactly equivalent to positive-semidefinite linear matrix inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(X\in\mathbb{S}^n\)
\(t\in\mathbb{R}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{\max}(X)\le t\iff tI-X\succeq0\)

children.title: Matrix-Inequality Rewrites
children.top_down_role: Equivalent forms exposing supported semidefinite order structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Inequality Rewrites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Schur-complement conversion between block LMIs and quadratic matrix inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{S}^n\), \(C\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\), and \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\). Then \[\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Thus a matrix inequality containing an inverse may be replaced by an affine block linear matrix inequality whenever the inverted block is positive definite. The symmetric counterpart using \(A\succ0\) and the Schur complement of \(A\) is equivalent as well.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic matrix inequality involving a positive-definite inverse is equivalent to a block positive-semidefinite linear matrix inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{S}^n\)
\(C\in\mathbb{S}_{++}^m\)
\(B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times m}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\iff A-BC^{-1}B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\)

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact PSD block-matrix criterion for a singular pivot block.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb S^n\), \(C\in\mathbb S^m\), and \(B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}\). Then \[\begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\] if and only if \[C\succeq0,\qquad\operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(C),\qquad A-BC^\dagger B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Equivalently, the range condition is \((I-CC^\dagger)B^{\mathsf T}=0\). The range condition is indispensable: for scalars \(A=C=0\) and \(B=1\), the pseudoinverse complement is zero but \(\begin{bmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}\) is indefinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singular PSD pivot permits an exact pseudoinverse Schur rewrite only with the off-diagonal range condition; omitting it gives false positives.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb S^n
C\in\mathbb S^m
B\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{bmatrix}A&B\\B^{\mathsf T}&C\end{bmatrix}\succeq0\iff C\succeq0,\ \operatorname{range}(B^{\mathsf T})\subseteq\operatorname{range}(C),\ A-BC^\dagger B^{\mathsf T}\succeq0
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Schur-Complement Criterion

children.title: Spectral-to-Semidefinite Relations
