knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a grammar-accepted objective to monotone convex feasibility tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a DQCP minimization problem with optimal value \(p^*\) and a finite bracket \(L\leq p^*\leq U\), replace the objective by the threshold constraint \(f_0(x)\leq t\) and canonicalize the resulting problem as a convex feasibility problem. An exact feasibility oracle updates \(U\leftarrow t\) after a feasible test and \(L\leftarrow t\) after an infeasible test. With midpoint thresholds, after \(k\) tests the bracket width is \((U-L)2^{-k}\); therefore \(\lceil\log_2((U-L)/\varepsilon)\rceil\) tests suffice for width at most \(\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Concave Disciplines
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Difference-of-convex grammar underlying convex-concave procedure models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A convex-concave disciplined model represents each permitted nonconvex inequality as \[u_i(x)-v_i(x)\leq0,\] where \(u_i\) and \(v_i\) are convex expressions certified by a composition grammar; affine equalities may also be present. At a reference point \(x^k\) where \(v_i\) is subdifferentiable, choosing \(s_i^k\in\partial v_i(x^k)\) gives the convex restriction \[u_i(x)-v_i(x^k)-\langle s_i^k,x-x^k\rangle\leq0.\] Grammar acceptance certifies the decomposition, but it does not certify global optimality of iterations based on these restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The discipline certifies difference-of-convex expressions, enabling convex local restrictions but not global optimality guarantees.
assumptions_latex: \(u_i,v_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) are convex
\(\partial v_i(x^k)\neq\varnothing\) for linearization
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_i(x)-v_i(x^k)-\langle s_i^k,x-x^k\rangle\leq0\) is a convex constraint.

notation.meaning: Convex subdifferential of v_i at the reference point.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighboring-Grammar Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance and guarantees are relative to a specified disciplined grammar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a disciplined grammar \(G\), let \(\mathcal{A}_G\) be the expressions accepted by its syntax and composition rules, and let \(\mathcal{S}_G\) be the semantic class that those rules certify. The boundary between grammars \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) consists of \(\mathcal{A}_{G_1}\setminus\mathcal{A}_{G_2}\), \(\mathcal{A}_{G_2}\setminus\mathcal{A}_{G_1}\), and expressions rejected by both. Membership in \(\mathcal{A}_{G_1}\) implies only the guarantee defining \(\mathcal{S}_{G_1}\); it does not imply acceptance by \(G_2\), convex canonicalizability, or the algorithmic guarantees associated with \(G_2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additive Growth for Local Atom Canonicalization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-size upper bound for uniformly bounded local graph reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a source expression DAG contain \(N\) atom nodes. If every node is replaced once by a bounded-arity graph representation using at most \(a\) auxiliary scalars, \(r\) affine relations, \(k\) cone blocks, and \(s\) stored coefficients, then canonicalization introduces at most \(aN\), \(rN\), \(kN\), and \(sN\) such objects, respectively, apart from the original affine data. Hence uniformly bounded local reductions have componentwise \(O(N)\) representation growth when shared nodes remain shared.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Canonicalizing each shared expression-DAG node once with a bounded local graph gives linear representation growth.
assumptions_latex: The source DAG has \(N\) atom nodes.
Local graph representations have uniform bounded arity and size.
Each shared node is canonicalized once.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S(C(P))=O(N)\text{ componentwise under the stated convention}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential growth caused by destroying common-subexpression sharing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define a shared expression DAG by \(e_0=x\) and \(e_{j+1}=e_j+e_j\). Its DAG has \(O(j)\) nodes, whereas recursively duplicating both references produces a syntax tree with \(2^j\) leaves. Thus preserving sharing requires \(O(j)\) representation size, while expansion before canonicalization may require \(\Theta(2^j)\), although both expressions equal \(2^j x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Destroying common-subexpression sharing can expand a linear-size DAG into an exponential-size tree.

No algebraic simplification collapses the expanded tree before size is incurred.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a source model \(P\), let \((n_s,m_s,z_s)\) count scalar variables, scalar constraints, and stored nonzeros, and let \((n_c,m_c,z_c)\) be the corresponding counts for a canonical conic representation \(C(P)\), including auxiliaries. knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact aggregate epigraph can obscure source-objective separability.

children.title: Ill-Conditioned Equivalent Representations
children.top_down_role: Equivalent canonical forms with substantially different numerical behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benign boundary for row transformations of a full-column-rank equality operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) has full column rank and \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\), then \((QA)^{\mathsf T}(QA)=A^{\mathsf T}A\). Thus \(QA\) and \(A\) have identical singular values and \(\kappa_2(QA)=\kappa_2(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orthogonal row transformations preserve singular values and spectral condition number.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) has full column rank
\(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual Distortion Under Equivalent Row Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies numerical distortion despite exact feasible-set equivalence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Ax=b\) and invertible \(T\), the transformed residual is \(T(Ax-b)\), and \(\sigma_{\min}(T)\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2\le\lVert T(Ax-b)\rVert_2\le\sigma_{\max}(T)\lVert Ax-b\rVert_2\). Exact feasibility is unchanged, while residual magnitudes and residual-based stopping tests can be distorted by the singular-value spread of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible row transformations preserve exact solutions but can strongly distort residual norms.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is invertible
Residuals use the Euclidean norm
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sigma_{\min}(T)\lVert r\rVert_2\le\lVert Tr\rVert_2\le\sigma_{\max}(T)\lVert r\rVert_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual Distortion Under Equivalent Row Transformations
Ill-Conditioned Equivalent Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent equality representations with arbitrarily different conditioning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\leq1\), consider the feasibility problems \[x=b\qquad\text{and}\qquad D_\varepsilon x=D_\varepsilon b,\quad D_\varepsilon=\operatorname{diag}(1,\varepsilon),\quad x,b\in\mathbb{R}^2.\] Because \(D_\varepsilon\) is invertible, both representations have exactly the feasible set \(\{b\}\). Nevertheless, the equality operator in the first representation has spectral condition number \(1\), whereas \(\kappa_2(D_\varepsilon)=1/\varepsilon\). Thus equivalent canonical forms can have arbitrarily different conditioning as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\), even though their exact feasible sets and objective values coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible row scaling preserves an equality-defined feasible set but can make its coefficient matrix arbitrarily ill-conditioned.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\leq1\)
Conditioning is measured by the spectral condition number
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:x=b\}=\{x:D_\varepsilon x=D_\varepsilon b\}\) while \(\kappa_2(D_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^{-1}\to+\infty\).

Adding sound capabilities can therefore make a certified model representable without changing its source-level feasible set or objective.

Certified but Not Solver-Representable Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates grammar certification from representation by an available solver stack.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be accepted by a disciplined grammar, so that its asserted curvature, domains, and constraint directions are certified. The status certified but not solver-representable means \[P\text{ is grammar-certified}\qquad\text{and}\qquad P\notin\mathcal{C}.\] This status makes no claim that \(P\) is infeasible, unbounded, or nonconvex. It records only the absence, in the selected software stack, of a complete reduction from the certified source structure to a supported solver input.

The installed reductions and solver-supported cones are fixed

children.title: Certified but Infeasible or Unbounded Models
children.top_down_role: Convexity certification without feasibility or a finite optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Infeasible and Unbounded Affine Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal affine programs separating structural certification from feasibility and finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}0\) subject to \(x\le 0\) and \(x\ge 1\) is affine and infeasible. The problem \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R}-x\) subject to \(x\ge 0\) is affine, feasible, and unbounded below. Thus correct disciplined-convexity certification implies neither feasibility nor a finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simple affine programs show that convexity certification guarantees neither feasibility nor boundedness.
assumptions_latex: The minimization convention is used.
Affine objectives and constraints are admitted by the grammar.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified Infeasible and Unbounded Affine Models

assumptions_latex: The model is accepted by a sound disciplined-convexity checker and canonicalized as a conic program.
The canonical primal has the form \(\inf_x c^{\mathsf T}x\) subject to \(Ax+b\in K\), where \(K\) is a closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Syntactic certification implies neither \(F\neq\varnothing\) nor \(p^\star\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Primal optimal value in the extended reals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates valid convex syntax from feasibility and finite optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certified canonical model may still be infeasible or unbounded. For \(F=\{x:Ax+b\in K\}\), infeasibility means \(F=\varnothing\), in which case the minimization value is conventionally \(p^\star=+\infty\). If \(F\neq\varnothing\) and for every \(M\in\mathbb R\) there exists \(x_M\in F\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}x_M<M\), then \(p^\star=-\infty\) and the model is unbounded below. Both outcomes are compatible with correct curvature analysis and valid conic canonicalization, because certification checks structural convexity rather than existence or boundedness of solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model can satisfy disciplined convexity and canonicalize correctly while having no feasible point or an objective unbounded below.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified but Infeasible or Unbounded Models

children.title: Certified but Numerically Unresolved Models

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Equivalence Does Not Ensure Numerical-Status Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of exact model equivalence from finite-precision termination behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Multiplying an equality \(a^{\mathsf T}x=b\) or inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) by a positive scalar preserves its exact feasible set. Nevertheless, finite-precision iterates, unnormalized residual magnitudes, conditioning, and tolerance tests can change under scaling. Thus equivalent canonical data need not receive identical numerical termination outcomes unless the solver's scaling and status tests ensure the relevant invariance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Equivalent positive rescalings preserve the exact problem but can change finite-precision residuals and solver termination outcomes.
assumptions_latex: Constraint scaling factors are strictly positive.
Solver decisions use finite-precision computations and tolerance-based tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_1\equiv D_2\not\Rightarrow S_\theta(D_1)=S_\theta(D_2)\) in general.

notation.meaning: Canonical data defining the same exact optimization problem
Numerical status under fixed solver settings \(\theta\)

assumptions_latex: A certified model has been transformed into valid finite-dimensional canonical data \(D\).
A solver is run with specified tolerances, iteration limits, arithmetic, and termination rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned status \(\mathtt{unknown}\) neither proves nor disproves feasibility, infeasibility, boundedness, or optimality.

notation.meaning: Solver status map under numerical settings theta.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes mathematical model validity from inconclusive numerical termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_\theta(D)\) denote the status returned for canonical data \(D\) under numerical settings \(\theta\). The model is numerically unresolved when \(S_\theta(D)=\mathtt{unknown}\) and the solver supplies no accepted certificate of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness. Such a result may follow from an iteration or time limit, numerical breakdown, insufficient accuracy, or failure of residual and gap tests. It is an epistemic solver outcome: it does not alter the model's certified convexity and does not entail any particular exact status for the underlying optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid canonical model is numerically unresolved when the solver terminates without an accepted certificate of optimality, infeasibility, or unboundedness.
knowledge_statements.title: Certified but Numerically Unresolved Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates generated storage from total retained representation storage.

Under unit-cost record creation and complete inspection of \(N\) reachable input records, expansion time is \(\Theta(N+S)\). Additional generated storage is \(\Theta(S)\); total retained storage is \(\Theta(N+S)\) only when the original representation remains resident.

assumptions_latex: Every generated record is explicitly materialized.
Record creation and references have unit cost.
Every reachable input record is inspected.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expansion-size blowup caused by duplicating shared nested representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a compact expression DAG contains shared nested atoms, fresh inlining on every incoming path can produce the unfolded-tree size \(U\). Repeated-sharing depth-\(d\) DAGs of size \(O(d)\) can have \(U=2^{\Theta(d)}\). Reusing an expansion avoids this path duplication only when the representation contract guarantees that the generated auxiliary witnesses may be shared without changing projected semantics.
